title: Mike Macdonald wants Emmanuel Henderson thinking of being a great WR and All-Pro returner
summary: Seahawks rookie receiver Emmanuel Henderson was a sixth-round pick, which means he has to compete just to make the roster.
full_text: ' Seahawks rookie receiver Emmanuel Henderson was a sixth-round pick, which means he has to compete just to make the roster. But head coach Mike Macdonald wants Henderson thinking about a lot more than just making the roster. Macdonald said after Sunday night's preseason game, in which Henderson caught one pass, returned to kickoffs, and was a gunner on punts, that he wants Henderson to fulfill his potential, which should mean a lot more than just making a team. Asked whether special teams is the reason Henderson is in Seattle, Macdonald answered, "It's one of the reasons, for sure, but why stop there?" "That's the stuff that really popped, and gets you excited from his college tape, the return game," Macdonald said. "He should be trying to be an All-Pro returner, too. He should be thinking of being a great receiver in our league as well." Henderson spent three years at Alabama but didn't get on the field much before transferring to Kansas last year. In his one year at Kansas, Henderson was chosen by the Big 12 coaches as a first-team All-Big 12 returner and a third-team All-Big 12 receiver. Macdonald thinks Henderson has just scratched the surface of what he can do.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Robert Saleh on starting defense giving up TDs: Glad it happened in preseason
summary: The Titans' starting defense gave up a 36-yard touchdown pass on the first possession and a 69-yard touchdown run on the second possession.
full_text: The Titans played their starters in Sunday night's preseason game, and the defense gave up two first-quarter touchdowns to Seattle's backups. But Titans head coach Robert Saleh was seeing the glass as half full after the game. Saleh said he hated seeing his team give up a 36-yard touchdown pass on the first possession and a 69-yard touchdown run on the second possession, but he believes making mistakes in the preseason is part of the process of his players learning his defense. "The two plays are hateful," Saleh said. "The pass play, I'm glad it happened, because that is a fundamental issue in the defense that if you don't get those reps, you don't recognize it fast enough, and for it to happen, glass half full, glad it happened. Half empty, it's a shitty thing that happened. . . . Those two plays, wish we had them back, but overall I thought the defense was pretty good today." Saleh believes his defense played fundamentally sound football, outside the mistakes that can be corrected that resulted in the two long touchdowns. "It was those two plays. Felt really good about all the different things that were happening," Saleh said. Saleh is confident that the mistakes being made in the preseason will get corrected before the regular season. "Like I said, I'm glad it happened because it's an easy fix. For the player to feel that, it's like, 'I get it now,'" Saleh said. "It's a really cool a-ha moment. Unfortunately it happened in a game-like atmosphere. Thank God it was preseason. One hundred percent will get fixed."
author: Michael David Smith

title: S Bud Clark, OL Mason Richman out for months after being injured Sunday night
summary: The Seahawks have taken three big losses before the season even starts.
full_text: The Seahawks have taken three big losses before the season even starts. During the joint practice with the Titans earlier in the week, the Seahawks lost wide receiver Jake Bobo for the season with a right leg injury. During Sunday night's preseason game in Tennessee, the Seahawks saw safety Bud Clark and offensive guard Mason Richman leave with injuries. Coach Mike Macdonald said after the 19-16 loss to the Titans that Clark and Richman were diagnosed with major injuries that will keep them out for months. "We have had three heartbreaking injuries this week," Macdonald said, via Brady Henderson of ESPN. Clark, the team's second-round pick, broke his ankle and will miss "multiple months." He was injured on the Titans’ first play from scrimmage on a 9-yard run by Tony Pollard and wore a vacuum splint on his right leg as he left the field. Henderson reports that another of the Seahawks' backup safeties, Rodney Thomas II, underwent surgery last week to repair a fracture in his hand. Thomas has a chance to return next week. It is unclear what Richman's injury is, but Macdonald called it "long term." Richman is the backup to Grey Zabel, though he started at left guard against the Titans with Zabel not playing.
author: Charean Williams

title: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty diagnosed with sprained ankle
summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty needed help off the practice field on Sunday after injuring his right leg.
full_text: '' Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty needed help off the practice field on Sunday after injuring his right leg. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Jeanty was diagnosed with a sprained ankle. It is unclear whether the sprain is a high- or low-ankle sprain, and Schefter said the Raiders are unsure how much time Jeanty will miss. However, it is not considered a long-term injury. The injury initially appeared serious, but the Raiders now can breathe easy. Jeanty, the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 draft, is slated to be a focal point of Las Vegas’ offense in 2026 under new head coach Klint Kubiak. In 17 games as a rookie last year, Jeanty finished with 1,321 yards from scrimmage — 975 rushing, 346 receiving on 55 catches — with 10 total touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Saints send LB Deion Jones to 49ers for RB Zamir White
summary: The Saints are trading veteran linebacker Deion Jones to the 49ers in exchange for running back Zamir White, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
full_text: The Saints are trading veteran linebacker Deion Jones to the 49ers in exchange for running back Zamir White, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The Saints needed running back help with Alvin Kamara out at least a month with an MCL sprain. Devin Neal (hamstring) and Kendre Miller (back) have also missed time in camp with injuries. The 49ers signed White on Aug. 12 as they dealt with backfield injuries of their own. Christian McCaffrey returned to practice on Sunday. Jones reunites with 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris after the two were together with the Falcons from 2016-20. Jones was a Pro Bowler in 2017. Jones spent the past two seasons with the Bucs, and he played all 17 games last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian McCaffrey says recent practice absences were planned as part of load management
summary: Christian McCaffrey returned to practice on Sunday, his first time on the field with his teammates since Aug. 8.
full_text: Christian McCaffrey returned to practice on Sunday, his first time on the field with his teammates since Aug. 8. The 49ers' terming his injury as "tightness" raised some eyebrows given he had calf tightness during the 2024 training camp that carried into the season. His absence has some others wondering whether it had anything to do with his contract. The running back said Sunday the time away was planned as part of his load management. "This was kind of part of the plan from the jump," McCaffrey said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "Was to ramp up pretty big, get 9, 10 practices in, kind of come back down, and then ramp back up so we're fresh for the duration." McCaffrey played only four games in 2024 with what was later announced as Achilles tendinitis, and he had a separate injury to his posterior collateral ligament. The 49ers have been deliberate with his practice schedule since. McCaffrey, 30, led the league with 413 touches last year. "I can probably be my worst enemy in how much I just love being out there," McCaffrey said. "I want to run. I want to go. I want every play. I'm a competitor. I love it." He sounds as if he will be ready for Week 1. "I feel great," McCaffrey said. "So I feel fresh, and it's good to be back out there." McCaffrey has watched Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor sign extensions this offseason, pushing him to the fifth-highest paid player at his position. He makes an annual average of $19 million a season and is under contract through 2027. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said recently that McCaffrey's absence was not related to his contract.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks second-round S Bud Clark carted off with leg injury
summary: Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark was carted off with a right leg injury in Sunday night's preseason game against the Titans.
full_text: ' Seahawks rookie safety Bud Clark was carted off with a right leg injury in Sunday night's preseason game against the Titans. Clark was injured on the Titans' first play from scrimmage on a 9-yard run by Tony Pollard. The second-round pick wore a vacuum splint on his right leg as he left the field. His teammates wished him well before he departed. In the joint practice earlier in the week, the Seahawks lost wide receiver Jake Bobo for the season with a right leg injury. Clark was competing for playing time behind starters Ty Okada and Julian Love after the Seahawks lost starter Coby Bryant in free agency. Clark totaled three tackles in his preseason debut. The Seahawks now will lean on D'Anthony Bell, A.J. Finley and Rodney Thomas. The team's first-round pick, running back Jadarian Price, has not suited up in the preseason, and he won't play next week either as he works his way back from upper-leg soreness.
author: Charean Williams

title: Could Deshaun Watson get a two-game audition for the starting job?
summary: Browns coach Todd Monken surely knows which quarterback he'll name as the team's starter on Monday.
full_text: '' Browns coach Todd Monken surely knows which quarterback he'll name as the team's starter on Monday. Given the extent to which he downplayed Deshaun Watson's jarring postgame remarks from Saturday about being booed loudly by the home crowd, it's hard not to wonder whether it will indeed be Watson. Based on Monken's belief that quality play will quickly unruffle feathers, it's possible that Monken is inclined to give Watson the first two games, both on the road at Jacksonville and Tampa Bay, to see if Watson can pull off an upset or two. If the Browns somehow start 2-0, the vibe could be much different when the Browns open their home schedule in Week 3 against the Panthers. However it goes, it seems clear that Monken won't be making a 17-game decision right out of the gates. The man who wins the job as of Week 1 also wins the privilege of being the first guy benched. Monken has said the announcement is coming on Monday. Which means he knows. And when he begins telling others, it will be just a matter of time until someone blabs — and everyone knows. If nothing else, look for the Browns to curry favor with an insider or two by leaking it minutes before the official announcement is made. And with Monken due to speak to reporters again at 12:50 p.m. ET on Monday, expect to hear something late in the morning. If we don't hear something tonight.
author: Mike Florio

title: Three years since selling Commanders, Daniel Synder has become "invisible"
summary: Daniel Snyder is the perfect example of a fundamental truth: The only thing better than being rich and famous is being rich.
full_text: Daniel Snyder is the perfect example of a fundamental truth: The only thing better than being rich and famous is being rich. Snyder had become rich and notorious until the NFL forced him out of Club Oligarch. While many owners were believed to be inclined to keep him around despite allegations of misconduct and mistreatment of employees, the tipping point arrived when the other owners had reason to believe Snyder may have been picking their pockets, by allegedly diverting ticket revenue from Commanders games (40 percent of which are shared with the rest of the league) to non-Commanders events at the stadium he owned. Whatever the reason(s), some owners who were previously concerned about creating a standard that could potentially be used against them agreed that Snyder had to go. And in the three years since he left, Snyder has become (as explained by Mark Maske of Front Office Sports ) " invisible ." In 2023, Snyder sold the Commanders to a group led by Josh Harris for a then-record $6.05 billion. (That record will soon be shattered, when a group led by Vinod Khosla acquires the Seahawks for $9.612 billion.) Snyder had been linked to potential investment in an English soccer club. That never happened. And he has completely disconnected from any relationship he made in more than 20 years of franchise ownership. “I don’t think anybody is in touch with him about anything," an unnamed NFL team official told Maske. "I don’t know who he hangs out with. I don’t know who he talks to. Certainly nobody in the NFL is talking to him.” Snyder and his wife have relocated to London, with no apparent plan to return to the United States. “He’ll never be back,” an unnamed Snyder associate told Maske. “In London, they . . . don’t bother him." That said, Snyder hovers over former Raiders coach Jon Gruden's lawsuit against the NFL and Commissioner Roger Goodell. Gruden's case arises from the weaponization of confidential emails harvested during Beth Wilkinson's investigation of the team. A small universe of people had access to them. Snyder, given that he owned the network from which the emails were gathered, was necessarily one of them. And with Snyder out of the country, getting his testimony in the Gruden case will entail a complicated and cumbersome process. But Gruden seems to be very motivated to get to the bottom of who ordered the Code Red against him, resulting in his forced resignation from the Raiders in October 2021. His lawyers presumably will do whatever it takes to get Snyder under oath, so that he can be grilled about any knowledge he may have regarding the leaks that led to Gruden's ouster.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ashton Jeanty exits Sunday's practice with apparent leg injury
summary: Jeanty went down after diving to make a catch during the day's session.
full_text: '' The Raiders have a significant injury concern with one of their top offensive players. According to multiple reporters on the scene, running back Ashton Jeanty exited Sunday’s practice early with an apparent right leg injury. Jeanty went down after diving to catch a pass from Kirk Cousins, going down awkwardly. Jeanty was not able to put weight on his right leg as he was helped off the field with trainers and did not return. As a team, the Raiders took a knee for a moment in silence after Jeanty went down. The No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 draft, Jeanty is slated to be a focal point of Las Vegas’ offense in 2026 under new head coach Klint Kubiak. In 17 games as a rookie last year, Jeanty finished with 1,321 yards from scrimmage — 975 rushing, 346 receiving on 55 catches — with 10 total touchdowns.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Browns will waive Dae’Quan Wright, who has agreed to play for LSU
summary: Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright is poised to do something that once would have been unthinkable: Leave the NFL and go play in the NCAA.
full_text: '' Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright is poised to do something that once would have been unthinkable: Leave the NFL and go play in the NCAA. The Browns are waiving Wright, and he has an agreement in place to play for LSU this season, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. It's possible that Wright could get claimed on waivers, which would complicate matters, although it sounds like Wright has decided he wants to play this year for LSU, where he surely has a lucrative NIL offer in place, and wait until next year to pursue the NFL. Wright going back to college after signing with an NFL team never would have been possible under the rules that have governed college football for more than a century, but those rules have gone out the window. The NCAA keeps losing court battles over player eligibility rules, to the point where there aren't many rules left. Wright can play anywhere he wants in college, and he has chosen LSU. Wright spent his first two years of college football at Virginia Tech, then spent two more years at Ole Miss, where he played for Lane Kiffin, who will now coach him at LSU. Browns head coach Todd Monken called it " crazy " that a player currently on the Browns' roster will be playing college football this season, but until the NCAA comes up with eligibility rules that can withstand court challenges, the sport is in crazy times.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaguars sign DT Tommy Akingbesote, waive CB Devon Marshall
summary: The Jaguars have made a pair of roster moves on Sunday.
full_text: The Jaguars have made a pair of roster moves on Sunday. Jacksonville announced the club has signed defensive tackle Tommy Akingbesote. A Cowboys seventh-round pick in 2025, Akingbesote did not make Dallas’ 53-man roster. He then spent time with Carolina and Buffalo on the practice squad. He did not appear in a regular-season game as a rookie. The Bills let him go last week. As a corresponding move, the Jaguars waived cornerback Devon Marshall with an injury designation.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Todd Monken anticipates naming a starting quarterback on Monday
summary: Monken says Saturday's comments from Deshaun Watson won't be a factor.
full_text: '' The Browns are getting closer and closer to naming a starting quarterback. In a Sunday press conference with reporters via Zoom, coach Todd Monken said the team will name a starting quarterback on Monday. What else at this point does he need to do to get there? "I still have a few things to weigh out," Monken said. "I'm not going to get into that. But we anticipate naming a starter tomorrow." Monken said Saturday's postgame comments from quarterback Deshaun Watson regarding getting booed during the game (and being cheered when he suffered a torn Achilles tendon in 2024) will not be a factor in the decision. The first-year coach also was asked about the reality that, for the Week 3 home opener, the fans could respond negatively to Watson's presence as the starter. "I'm not concerned about that," Monken said. "What I'm concerned about is us playing well, as a team and on offense. Because when you play well, none of the other stuff matters." Monken is approaching all of this from a football perspective, which is fine. But the Watson situation is far more complicated than that. There's a history that predates Monken's hiring. An ugly one, which reached a low point on Saturday. Monken seems to think none of that matters, focusing only on the quality of the next performance and not the past vibe that the trade for Watson, his contract, and his play has created. For example, Monken compared fan reaction to going to a restaurant and getting cold soup. This ignores the simple fact that, as far as pro football goes, there's only one restaurant in town. And the soup has been cold, moldy, and littered with rubber bands , consistently and repeatedly. It's entirely possible that Monken, who said the decision is ultimately his, has made his choice and will spend the next day getting everyone in the building on board who needs to be on board. And, possibly, to figure out a solution to Watson's role — if the decision is made that Watson won't be the starter. Really, if Monken doesn't know which way things are going today, what will change between now and Monday? More immediately, the Browns have another home game on Thursday night to cap the preseason. At this point, it would be ludicrous to put Watson on the field again, five days after being relentlessly booed. If he's not the starter, and if with Monken saying the starting quarterback will not play on Thursday, the Browns likely will need to use Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green in the last game that doesn't count, if Watson isn't named the starter.
author: Mike Florio

title: A day after signing with Dolphins, LB Stephen Dix Jr. was making defensive calls in a game
summary: The preseason is often about figuring out the contours of the roster.
full_text: '' The preseason is often about figuring out the contours of the roster. Sometimes, it's simply about getting through the game. On Saturday, the Dolphins extensively used a player who'd signed with the team a day before — and who hadn't participated in any portion of any training camp, with any team. And Stephen Dix Jr. was thrilled to have the opportunity, not just to play but to play a significant role. "We had a linebacker who I met this morning in my office; Steve came in, met him, and he started the whole second half where we had to tell him the call, he had to give the call, then we had to tell him what to do on every single play," coach Jeff Hafley told reporters after the game. "So we were able to play only like two calls in the second half, which has never happened to me in my life. So I just give him credit for going out and fighting. That's what the preseason is all about, to find out who those guys are." Dix welcomed the challenge, and the opportunity. "I think I had a quick 30-minute meeting with [linebackers] coach [Al] Washington," Dix told reporters. "They told me, ‘Look bro, just go out there run sideline to sideline. I’m going to be in your ear and I’m going to tell you the call and tell you what to do.’ . . . Like that’s literally any football player’s dream, get told what to do and just go play ball. It was exciting. It was so fun out there." Dix, undrafted out of Arkansas, had been signed by the Cardinals but released in June. "This is my dream, I’m doing exactly what I set out to do as a kid, and the journey doesn’t stop here," Dix said. "It’s obviously putting together enough days to make the team and continue my career. Today was just surreal. It was a blessing. I can’t be more thankful. . . . To get this tryout and to get called to come up here and sign and not only sign and play, what more can I ask for? That’s all I wanted, was an opportunity to put the pads on." Dix was on the field for 34 defensive snaps and two special-teams plays. He made one tackle and had two assists. Regardless of whether he wins a spot on the 53-man roster, he may have done enough to get a spot on the practice squad, where he can keep working toward his next opportunity.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kellen Moore: We wanted to accomplish more offensively on Saturday
summary: Zach Wilson made a good case for the Saints' backup quarterback job in the team's first preseason game, but his second outing did not go as well.
full_text: '' Zach Wilson made a good case for the Saints' backup quarterback job in the team's first preseason game, but his second outing did not go as well. Wilson started against the Rams on Saturday after replacing Spencer Rattler in the opener, but failed to put any points on the board while going 6-of-12 for 55 yards and an interception. Rattler was 14-of-23 for 141 yards, but he also threw an interception in the red zone that was returned for a 100-yard touchdown during the 34-0 loss. After the game, head coach Kellen Moore said he feels both quarterbacks have had good camps but that Saturday's game was "a big-time missed opportunity." "We’re gonna have to watch the film really closely," Moore said. "Gut reaction is obviously we want to accomplish more as an offense. . . . We pushed these guys this week, we challenged them with some big-time opportunities with some joint practices and this game. I love the work collectively that we got over the course of the week. It's just obviously we missed an opportunity here. I've got to prepare our guys better, I've got to get our guys ready to go for this opportunity." The Saints will close out the preseason against the Dolphins on Friday and Moore will be looking for at least one of the quarterbacks to make more of their chance this time around.
author: Josh Alper

title: Christian McCaffrey returns to 49ers practice
summary: There is more positive news on the injury front for the 49ers.
full_text: There is more positive news on the injury front for the 49ers. According to multiple reporters on the scene, running back Christian McCaffrey has returned to practice. McCaffrey has been sidelined by what the team has termed only as "tightness." McCaffrey had been sidelined since Aug. 10 . While his level of participation does not have to be announced because it is not yet the regular season, video from multiple reporters shows McCaffrey is at least going through individual drills. Head coach Kyle Shanahan recently told reporters that McCaffrey's absence was not contract-related . McCaffrey registered a career-high 413 touches in 17 regular-season games last season, a figure that also led the league. He then had 37 more in the club’s two postseason games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Vrabel is protecting key starters in preseason due to depth concerns
summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel has kept quarterback Drake Maye and other key starters out of the first two preseason games.
full_text: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel has kept quarterback Drake Maye and other key starters out of the first two preseason games. He'll apparently do the same in the final game, on Thursday at the Browns. Asked whether it's important to get those players game reps before the regular-season opener at Seattle, Vrabel had a simple response. "I do not think we have a very deep team," Vrabel said, "so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available. And if that means playing Thursday as part of preparation, then that is what we will do. I have not made that decision yet, but I would say that that is something that I am confident in with where we are set up currently." That's the balance every coach must strike when it comes to the preseason. Preparation versus injury risk. Full contact and live tackling enhance that risk. And no coach wants to be the one who lost an important player for the season, before the season even began. And to the extent the Patriots lack depth, Vrabel needs to get the young players ready to go for the real thing. Live reps in preseason games can help. "There are a lot of ebbs and flows of a professional football game, and how can you handle making a mistake?" Vrabel said. "How can you handle getting blocked? How can you handle having a good play and then coming back and being able to do it again? And how they bounce back, how they handle different situations. What they do in live action, I think, is really critical." Whatever the plan, the real thing is only 17 days away. And, one year after the Patriots opened the season by losing at home to the team that became the worst in the league, the Patriots go on the road to face the Super Bowl champion — in a rematch of a game the Patriots badly lost the last time around.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers place Tyler Biadasz on season-ending injured reserve
summary: Chargers center Tyler Biadasz will not play at all this season.
full_text: Chargers center Tyler Biadasz will not play at all this season. The Chargers have officially placed Biadasz on injured reserve, ending his season. That's no surprise, as the Chargers had said Biadasz had an ACL injury, but the team was exploring the possibility that he might be able to return late in the season. Now there's no hope of that. Biadasz will not play until 2027. The 28-year-old Biadasz signed a three-year, $30-million contract with the Chargers in March and was expected to be their starting center this season. He was the Commanders' starting center last season. The Chargers have signed wide receiver Gary Jennings to use the roster spot opened up by putting Biadasz on injured reserve.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers activate George Kittle from PUP list
summary: Kittle, who suffered a torn Achilles tendon in January, is now eligible to practice and may be ready to play in Week One.
full_text: '' 49ers tight end George Kittle is getting close to a return. The 49ers announced they have activated Kittle from the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list. That doesn't necessarily mean Kittle will play in the 49ers' Week One game against the Rams in Australia, but it is a strong indication that Kittle is progressing toward being able to play in the opener. Kittle tore his Achilles tendon in January and has reportedly healed ahead of schedule. He's not eligible to practice, and if practice goes well we may see Kittle when the season starts.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Browns place DE Alex Wright on IR with Achilles tear
summary: Cleveland replaces Wright on the roster with veteran Derek Barnett.
full_text: '' Three days ago, Browns defensive end Alex Wright left practice on a cart during joint practice with the Bills, due to a lower-leg injury. On Saturday, coach Todd Monken said he didn't have any information about Wright. On Sunday, the truth was leaked. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, Wright has a season-ending rupture of the Achilles tendon . The Browns will place him on injured reserve. Per the report, former first-round defensive end Derek Barnett will take Wright's place on the roster. Last November, the Browns signed Wright to a three-year, $33 million extension. A third-round pick in 2022, Wright has 51 regular-season appearances and 15 starts. Wright was listed as the starting defensive end across from Jared Verse. Barnett played for the Eagles from 2017 into 2023. He was released late in the regular season and claimed on waivers by the Texans, where he remained through the 2025 season. UPDATE 1:15 p.m. ET : The Browns have announced both moves.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bill Belichick is looking into the potential acquisition of players who get a fifth year
summary: Some schools, like Notre Dame, aren't exploring the addition of players from the class of 2022 who end up getting a fifth year of eligibility through the court system.
full_text: Some schools, like Notre Dame, aren't exploring the addition of players from the class of 2022 who end up getting a fifth year of eligibility through the court system. Others, like LSU, are. North Carolina is one of the ones that are. Coach Bill Belichick recently acknowledged that the Tar Heels are considering the possibility of making eleventh-hour additions to the roster. " We’ve looked at a number of them ," Belichick said Friday. "Each case is a little bit different. If it works, it works. If it doesn't, it doesn't. I don't think there's anything we're counting on, but we're always open to anything that will help the team." With G.M. Michael Lombardi on paid leave due to an internal investigation, it's unclear who's spearheading the effort. Regardless, the effort is underway. For coaches like Lane Kiffin of LSU, it's about putting the finishing touches on a roster that would be good enough to take the Tigers to the top of the mountain. For Belichick, who's entering his second season after a disastrous debut, it's about winning enough games to turn down the temperature on the hot seat. However it goes, the clock is ticking. North Carolina opens the season six days from now, against TCU in Ireland.
author: Mike Florio

title: RB Ja’Quinden Jackson was released from hospital, returned home with Eagles Saturday night
summary: The Eagles shared a positive update on running back Ja'Quinden Jackson after a scary moment in Saturday's game against the Patriots.
full_text: '' The Eagles shared a positive update on running back Ja'Quinden Jackson after a scary moment in Saturday's game against the Patriots. Jackson was taken off the field at Gillette Stadium in an ambulance and transported to a local hospital after being injured on the opening kickoff of the game. Jackson's agent shared that he had full movement and a negative CT scan upon being evaluated by doctors. The Eagles said that Jackson was later released from the hospital and that he returned to Philadelphia with the rest of the team. Jackson signed with the Eagles earlier this month. He spent last season on Jacksonville's practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy will not play in season opener
summary: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy will not play in the Tigers' first game of the 2026 season.
full_text: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy will not play in the Tigers' first game of the 2026 season. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz said in July that Hardy has been medically cleared to return after being shot in the upper leg in May, but Hardy has not practiced yet and Drinkwitz said on Saturday that the team doesn't "have a timetable on" when he will be on the field. Missouri opens their season against Arkansas-Pine Bluff on September 3. "It's up to his body and his response , and I know he's doing everything he can," Drinkwitz said, via Pete Thamel of ESPN.com. "[I] feel like, right now, it's in his best interest to hold off." Hardy led the SEC in rushing yards last year and moved to the top of the list of 2027 draft prospects, but the uncertainty about his return has clouded that outlook ahead of this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Odell Beckham Jr. missed chance to make a touchdown catch
summary: Receiver Odell Beckham Jr. had a chance to step conclusively away from the roster bubble on Saturday.
full_text: Receiver Odell Beckham Jr. had a chance to step conclusively away from the roster bubble on Saturday. It didn't work out. Beckham dropped a touchdown pass at the back of the end zone during the Giants' preseason game at Miami. The good news is that coach John Harbaugh doesn't seem to be inclined to hold the gaffe against Beckham. "He was in the air a long time,'' Harbaugh told the New York Post . "He got up — way up. I know he would say, 'I wake up at four in the morning and I'm making that play.' He knows he can make that play, and it's a really tough play to make. "Making it would have just been spectacular. I looked at that play as a positive in his favor . I thought it was impressive where he was at, going to get the ball. I think he's capable of still making that play.'' Beckham still wishes he had answered the door when opportunity knocked. "I'm pissed,'' Beckham said, per the Post . "This is the one that keeps me up at night. It's a play I know I can make. I just felt like I was hanging so long. You take it on the chin like a man. The confidence is still there. I know I'll make that play the next time." Beckham was on the field for 33 snaps against the Dolphins. Targeted four times, he caught two passes for 17 yards. In the Week 1 preseason game, Beckham caught two passes for six yards, in 16 snaps. Looming over the entire situation is next week's deadline for cutting all rosters from 90 to 53. Beckham is likely somewhere between No. 5 and No. 7 on the depth chart. Will he make the cut, especially since (unlike young receivers at the bottom of the roster) Beckham likely won't be playing special teams? There's value in having him around. He can mentor other players. And the fans gave him a very warm reception when he entered the Week 1 home game against the Vikings. Beckham is also a bargain, with a one-year, $1.3 million deal. If he ends up with a roster spot, the next question is whether Beckham will get meaningful playing time and/or opportunities during games. With Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, and Malachi Fields destined for big roles in the Giants' passing game, Beckham may have to leapfrog Calvin Austin III, Darnell Moody, and/or Jalin Hyatt to make a real contribution.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Milton has strong game, but Cowboys backup QB competition "long from over"
summary: The Cowboys know Dak Prescott is their starting quarterback, but they still have a decision to make about who will be the next man up on the depth chart.
full_text: The Cowboys know Dak Prescott is their starting quarterback, but they still have a decision to make about who will be the next man up on the depth chart. Joe Milton got the start on Saturday against the Cardinals and made a strong case for the job. Milton was 9-of-13 for 179 yards and a touchdown before giving way to Sam Howell, who went 7-of-10 for 65 yards and an interception. Milton also had a good game after replacing Howell in the preseason opener and head coach Brian Schottenheimer credited him with "two good halves" on Saturday, but said the competition remains open. “This is long from over ,” Schottenheimer said. “We’re going back to Frisco, thankfully, get a chance to be home and put some more training camp days in. You’ve got to give Joe his credit, he’s played really well the past two games, but we have a lot of confidence in Sam as well.” Milton joined the Cowboys late in the 2025 preseason and said he feels a " major difference " from where he was a year ago. We'll find out soon whether that difference has been enough for him to secure the backup job.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers sign TE Khalil Dinkins
summary: The 49ers brought tight end Khalil Dinkins back to the roster on Saturday.
full_text: '' The 49ers brought tight end Khalil Dinkins back to the roster on Saturday. Dinkins signed with the team after going undrafted in April, but was waived off of their non-football injury list in July. Defensive lineman Xavier Thomas was waived with an injury designation in a corresponding move. Dinkins had 37 catches for 399 yards and seven touchdowns in 49 games at Penn State. George Kittle remains on the physically unable to perform list, but the Niners hope he will be able to go at the start of the regular season. Jake Tonges, Luke Farrell, Brayden Willis, Hayden Rucci, and Josiah Deguara are their other tight ends.
author: Josh Alper

title: Rashawn Slater returns to Chargers practice
summary: The Chargers got a key piece of their offensive line back at practice on Saturday.
full_text: The Chargers got a key piece of their offensive line back at practice on Saturday. Left tackle Rashawn Slater took part in practice for the first time in a couple of weeks. Slater missed all of last season after tearing his patellar tendon and an issue with the same knee put him on the sidelines. Slater was a limited participant in his return to action, but it is a positive sign for his chances of being ready to go for Week 1. The Chargers are set to be without center Tyler Biadasz at the start of the season after he injured his knee. Head coach Jim Harbaugh has expressed confidence in Jake Slaughter's ability to handle the job, but having Slater back will make it easier for everyone to share confidence in the entire unit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni: "It's still a competition" between Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee for QB2
summary: As the Browns and Raiders work through their starting quarterbacks for Week 1, the Eagles are still trying to figure out their QB2.
full_text: '' As the Browns and Raiders work through their starting quarterbacks for Week 1, the Eagles are still trying to figure out their QB2. After Saturday's preseason game between Philadelphia and New England, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said "it's still a competition" between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee. "I think both the guys are battling, and I'm really confident in both of the guys," Sirianni told reporters after the game. "We'll see where that goes." Dalton has been getting first dibs during the preseason games, but that's apparently not a tipping of Sirianni's hand. "The reason Andy is going in first -- in practice they're still rotating," Sirianni said. "Andy is going in first because he's not going to play as much as Tanner because he has had more experience and he has more experience within this type of system, and Tanner needs to continue to play there because I think you saw the improvements there from Tanner. So we got to continue to give both of them opportunities within practice and potentially games." On Saturday, Dalton got the start and played 22 snaps. McKee had 38 snaps. Dalton completed three of 10 passes for 44 yards; McKee connected on 16 of 22 for 173 yards and two touchdowns. McKee's performance drew praise from Sirianni. "[I] thought today he did some good things," Sirianni said. "You know, there will be plays that we're going to have to correct and there was a lot of positives. I know stat-wise he came out having a pretty good game, and so, but obviously for all of us there will be corrections within it. But, yeah, thought he did some good things. Made some nice plays. Had a couple fourth downs that we would have liked to convert. Not saying those are his fault in that situation, but those fourth downs hurt us, not converting there." Dalton definitely has the experience. Now 38, he started immediately for the Bengals as a rookie in 2011. After nine years with the Bengals, Dalton has bounced from the Cowboys to the Saints to the Panthers (where he spent three seasons) to Philly. He has 169 career regular-season starts. McKee, in contrast, has two starts in three seasons with the Eagles. He has created preseason buzz during his much shorter career, but he has yet to be entrusted with the primary backup spot behind Hurts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eliot Wolf on Christian Gonzalez: "Each side is trying to do what's right for them"
summary: When the Falcons signed running back Bijan Robinson to a new contract, the Lions and running back Jahmyr Gibbs used the Robinson deal as the template for quickly getting their own contract done.
full_text: ' When the Falcons signed running back Bijan Robinson to a new contract, the Lions and running back Jahmyr Gibbs used the Robinson deal as the template for quickly getting their own contract done. When the Seahawks signed cornerback Devon Witherspoon to a new contract, it seemed that the same thing would happen for both the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez. Eight days later, it hasn't happened — even though Witherspoon and Gonzalez are represented by the same firm. During Saturday's preseason game between the Patriots and Eagles, New England executive V.P. of football operations Eliot Wolf addressed the lingering impasse. "Each side is trying to do what’s right for them ," Wolf said on the game broadcast, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. "Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed. We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done." Gonzalez hasn't practiced since August 10. The Patriots say he's injured. Maybe he is. The circumstances invite speculation that, if it's an injury, it's something he'd possibly be practicing through if he had the security that comes from a long-term second contract. Obviously, it's turning out not to be as simple as taking Witherspoon's deal, which pushed the new-money APY to $33 million per year, and changing the numbers in order to get Gonzalez to, say, $34 million annually. From the team's perspective, Gonzalez is under contract through 2027, thanks to his fifth-year option. From the player's perspective, Gonzalez wants to replace the $20.378 million he's due to earn under the balance of his rookie deal with something that sets a new bar for the cornerback market.
author: Mike Florio

title: It's time for the Browns and Deshaun Watson to go their separate ways
summary: After Saturday's game and press conference, it's impossible for the Browns to play Watson again.
full_text: '' On the surface, there's no reason for the Browns to walk away from the last year of Deshaun Watson's disastrous five-year, $230 million contract. They're paying him $46 million for 2026; why not have him on the team? At a deeper level (and it's not much deeper than the surface), it's time for this failed experiment to end. The fans don't want him. And, given the way the fans responded to him during his last two games in Cleveland, Watson no longer wants them. He was surprised and bothered by the boos he heard on Saturday. And he's still upset by the fact that fans cheered when he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during the 2024 season. Watch the full press conference . It's simply no longer sustainable. And it benefits no one for it to linger. Watson won't say it out loud, at least not yet. Asked if he regrets coming to Cleveland in the first place, Watson made the objectively ridiculous claim that he doesn't regret "anything in my life." "I had different thoughts on how it was going to be, but it is what it is," Watson said. "Sometimes the tables turn, and I’m patient enough because I’m a child of God, to wait for that time to change. So, I’m not tripping on it.” In other words, he's willing to count the days until he can get out of Cleveland for good. (Most Browns fans are probably doing the same thing.) How can the Browns play him this year, especially at home? Asked whether he can put the cheering when he was injured and the booing when he was healthy behind him, Watson bluntly said, "I don't know." “The only time I feel that energy is when I’m in the stadium or it’s on social media," Watson said. "Like I mentioned before, when I’m in public, no one’s mentioning anything. So I think that’s the only time those people who are holding it in is trying to disrupt the energy. Because on social media, players can’t respond back and in the stadium, players can’t respond back. So, I get it, I understand it. It is what it is. . . . I don't know. It’s a mental battle every day. I feel like I get more love on road games than I do at home games. So if it is my spot and [coach Todd Monken] does make me the starter, maybe it’s 17 away games, then. I don’t know.” Here's what we know. It's a toxic situation that someone within the Browns organization should admit can't continue. At this point, it's not about football or analytics or finding a way to get value for the investment. It's about finding the best path forward for the team and for the player. In many cases, an organization will do only what's right for the team, regardless of whether it's right for the player. In this case, the interests are fully aligned. Watson clearly wants to move on. The Browns should want to do the same. The specific details of the divorce would require some thought. The nuances of the accounting rules could make it impossible to execute the plan to layer lingering cap charges through 2030 if he's cut or traded (if anyone would want to trade for his $1.3 million base salary, and if he would be willing to waive his no-trade clause). Even without a trade or an outright release, the two sides can do what the Texans did once the relationship between Watson and his former team was permanently fractured in 2021: pay him to not play. This time around, the Browns would be paying Watson the last $1.3 million on his $230 million deal, while letting him leave a town that he no longer wants. And that arguably never wanted him.
author: Mike Florio

title: Saints-49ers trade grades: New Orleans adds Zamir White after onslaught of RB injuries
summary: The Saints bolstered a running back group that saw Alvin Kamara and two others suffer preseason injuries
full_text:
The second week of the NFL preseason closed with a trade. According to ESPN , the New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers agreed to a deal that sends linebacker Deion Jones to the Bay Area in exchange for running back Zamir White . The transaction addresses depth for both teams, particularly for the Saints, with No. 2 running back Alvin Kamara nursing an MCL sprain .
White signed with the 49ers less than two weeks ago. He inked a one-year deal worth $1.2 million and was projected to enter the season on the lower rungs of San Francisco's depth chart. Instead, he arrives in New Orleans with a chance to see playing time early in the campaign. White has never played a snap outside of Las Vegas, as he spent the first four years of his career with the Raiders and accumulated 736 rushing yards over 45 games.
Jones landed on the Saints' roster a few days earlier on Aug. 7 by way of a one-year, $1.3 million contract. While he was an every-week starter for the Atlanta Falcons in each of his first six professional seasons, he filled a smaller role across three different teams over the last four years. Jones most recently played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and tallied 29 tackles in 17 games last year.
Below are trade grades for the Saints and 49ers.
Kamara's injury is a boon to Travis Etienne , who should take firm command of the No. 1 running back role in New Orleans if the former's absence carries into the regular season. It creates depth concerns in the backfield, though, especially since Kamara is not the only one on the shelf. Devin Neal aggravated a hamstring injury in Saturday's preseason game, and Audric Estime hurt his ankle in the preseason opener, leaving the Saints without the second, fourth and fifth options on their unofficial depth chart.
Adding White to the group should keep the running backs afloat through the end of training camp, and he is capable of eating up a few snaps in the opening weeks of the regular season if called upon.
Boosting the running back depth without taking on any additional salary is a win for the Saints, especially since the linebacker they are parting with was no lock to make the roster in the first place. Jones was a cut candidate whom the team listed as a fourth-teamer.
The 49ers were in need of linebacker depth with only Fred Warner and Tatum Bethune available to them, and Jones fits the mold of a third option. He could even push Bethune for the primary backup role, but the latter made eight starts in 2025 when Warner suffered his gruesome ankle injury and may still factor into the team's plans after making those important contributions.
Regardless of how Jones fits into the equation, all San Francisco had to part with to acquire him was a deep backup who, at best, was sixth in line for carries. Removing players from behind Christian McCaffrey is always a risk given his extensive injury history, but the 49ers have plenty of more enticing backups they would turn to before White, who might not have even made the roster in the first place.
The team also just signed Khalil Herbert in a corresponding move to Patrick Taylor Jr.'s landing on injured reserve, so the cupboard is far from bare.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Raiders' Ashton Jeanty injured after landing awkwardly, has sprained ankle according to reports
summary: The second-year running back was unable to put any weight on his right leg
full_text:
LAS VEGAS -- Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty was helped off the practice field on Sunday without putting any weight on his right leg. The second-year rusher had been having a strong practice when he landed awkwardly diving for a catch thrown by Kirk Cousins during 11-on-11 drills. His teammates immediately froze as he lay on the ground. Trainers tended to him, then helped him up and aided him off the field. As he left, the entire team got down on a knee and stayed silent for a while before finishing practice.
The team did not immediately provide information on Jeanty's injury following practice.
According to an ESPN report , Jeanty is believed to have sprained his ankle. The Raiders are still unsure how long he will be out, but it is not considered a long-term injury.
Jeanty is coming off a quality rookie season in Las Vegas, totaling over 1,300 yards with 10 total scores.
Throughout the day, Jeanty had been splitting reps with rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . It is presumed Washington will begin handling the first-team reps while Jeanty is sidelined.
The running back with the most rushing yardage on the Raiders roster as of now, besides Jeanty, is Dare Ogunbowale. 594 career rush yards, 850 career receiving yards
In his first NFL preseason action against the Arizona Cardinals , Washington Jr. ran six times for 63 yards, including a 53-yard run, and he proved that he can be utilized in pass protection and be a weapon in the passing game.
He followed that up with another strong performance against the Houston Texans , running nine times for 56 yards and adding two catches for 18 yards.
Should Jeanty have to miss any time due to injury, the Raiders seem to have a dependable back to take his place.
author: Dave Richard

title: Grading every rookie QB from NFL preseason Week 2: Fernando Mendoza lackluster, Jalon Daniels draws high marks
summary: Of the 15 rookie quarterbacks who saw action this week, a small handful put on a show
full_text:
There are only a couple of quarterbacks in the 2026 rookie class who can realistically expect to play in NFL games this season. Of that group, only No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is virtually guaranteed to have the opportunity to start. Strong showings in the preseason can go a long way in increasing the number of first-year quarterbacks who carve out meaningful roles on their respective teams, though.
For most of the professional newcomers who have been in action over the last two weeks, impressive preseason showings will help them latch onto rosters as second or third options. Take Joey Aguilar or Jalon Daniels , for instance. Both scored touchdowns in consecutive outings, and Daniels oversaw a comeback win for the Buccaneers in preseason Week 2. They could go from undrafted free agents to important depth pieces because of their strong play.
There were 15 rookie quarterbacks in action during the second week of the preseason. Some started, others entered the lineup during the second half, and one saw less than a minute of action.
Below are grades for each of those rookie quarterbacks who played in Week 2.
Adjusting from college football to the NFL is hard. Do not let one rough preseason game against a stellar defense get in the way of Fernando Mendoza's potential to find ample success as a pro, potentially as soon as the latter stages of his rookie year. It really was a tough one, though. The No. 1 overall pick threw a pick-six that went 80 yards the other way on the Raiders ' opening possession, and he finished his first start 8-for-15 for 86 yards. He also took a sack for a loss of 11 yards. Mendoza did not reduce the gap between him and Kirk Cousins , but that was never the goal of this preseason. Las Vegas has no reason to rush him into the lineup.
Geno Smith gave Cade Klubnik a tough act to follow when he completed all seven of his passes and scored a touchdown, but his potential backup held his own against a Steelers defense that forced all kinds of pressure on the pocket. Klubnik did not orchestrate any scoring drives but helped the Jets get into field goal range during a two-minute drill at the end of the first half. He spent most of his time on his own half of the field and took two sacks, but it was not as if he received much help from his offensive line. A 16-yard keeper went down as New York's longest rush of the day.
It was always going to be a massive ask for Drew Allar to replicate the kind of magic he sparked in his professional debut. He did not come particularly close to repeating that three-touchdown effort. The most positive takeaway from Week 2 was that he went turnover-free; Will Howard , in comparison, threw two interceptions before giving way to his backup. Allar took three sacks and completed fewer than 50% of his 23 throws, and the Steelers gained just six first downs with him under center in the second half. If there was anything to build on, it was a 38-yard strike to rookie tight end Lake McRee .
There is some arm talent in Joey Aguilar. A week after he delivered a 43-yard dart on the lone throw of his professional debut, he connected with Trebor Pena on a 29-yard touchdown. Aguilar's highlights have come in the second half against reserve defenses, but they are meaningful nonetheless for an undrafted free agent fighting for a roster spot. In total, he threw just one incompletion across 10 attempts against the Panthers and racked up 130 yards plus the scoring play.
For the second consecutive week, Athan Kaliakmanis went down as the Commanders ' passing leader. It was an even wider margin this time around as he outdid Sam Hartman, 162 yards to 67, despite throwing just three more passes than his fellow backup. The first play of the fourth quarter was the source of one-third of those yards as he delivered a 55-yard strike down the sideline to Nick Nash . Outplaying Hartman in two chances, albeit without a touchdown drive, gives Kaliakmanis a chance to lock down Washington's No. 3 role.
Progress. Luke Altmyer was clean in the turnover department in the 17-13 win over the Commanders, which is a step in the right direction after he tossed a pair of interceptions in his debut. Taking four sacks, however, gives the Illinois product something new to work on. Chalk some of that up to the offensive line, since he was under pressure for most of his outing. Altmyer did not take a step toward the No. 2 job but should latch on as a third option with the potential to develop into more.
The Falcons might just have something in Jack Strand . He arrived in Atlanta as a relative unknown, having gone undrafted out of Division II Minnesota State–Moorhead, but he made a name for himself in two preseason outings. Following the rushing touchdown he logged in Week 1, Strand erupted for 212 passing yards, a touchdown and another score on the ground in a drubbing of the Colts . He and Cooper Rush combined to complete 16 of their first 17 throws, and his rushing ability (22 yards on nine carries) is obvious and differentiates him in the battle for the No. 3 quarterback job.
Joe Fagnano is racking up the volume this preseason. The Ravens clearly want to find out what they have in the undrafted signal-caller, considering they gave him 48 passing attempts across two games. On one of those throws in Week 2, he accounted for the lone touchdown of the 13-3 win over the Vikings with an 8-yard scoring toss to LaJohntay Wester . Fagnano converted on 75% of his passes (which, amazingly, was a regression from Week 1) and showed off a little bit of mobility, too. Everything points to Fagnano taking the No. 3 role from Austin Reed .
Ty Simpson swapped roles with Stetson Bennett IV this week after handling the lion's share of work in Week 1. The reduced workload limited him in his attempt to recreate the 21-for-25, two-touchdown clinic he put on the week prior, but he still found a rhythm and oversaw two lengthy drives in his three possessions of action. Both went 11 plays, and while the first ended in a turnover on downs, the Rams capped off their final series with a touchdown in the 34-0 blanking of the Saints .
Mark Gronowski 's greatest asset is his ability to make plays on the ground, and he got two chances to show it in his pro debut. He took two carries for nine yards, which is the only thing he had to write home about after gaining just one yard through the air on five attempts. Each of his three possessions were three-and-outs. The extremely limited playing time Gronowski has seen this preseason does not bode well for his chances of making the roster, not to mention his ineffectiveness on Saturday.
Former college teammates reunited in Chicago when Miller Moss signed with the Bears as an undrafted free agent, and both he and his former USC pal Caleb Williams saw the field in Week 2. Moss' role increased from the week prior, when he threw just eight passes, as he tossed a team-high 21 of them in the loss to the Bengals . His final line was solid, but they were mostly empty numbers as four of his drives ended in punts, one resulted in a missed field goal, and another concluded with a turnover on downs.
Cole Payton was a darling of Week 1 with his passing touchdown and 45 rushing yards, but he hardly had an opportunity to show off those dual-threat skills again this weekend. Payton came in for the Eagles with 57 seconds to play, had a completion scrapped for a penalty, connected on a 10-yard pickup and finished off his short day with a strip sack.
After Tommy DeVito worked the first half, Behren Morton took all the second-half snaps in the Patriots ' 24-21 win over the Eagles. That timeshare gave him the opportunity to flex his clutch gene. The second of his two touchdown drives decided the game. Trailing 21-17 with about a minute to play, Morton unleashed a 37-yard ball to Nick DeGennaro , who beat his defender to get into the end zone for the game-winner. It put the final touches on a splendid 13-for-17 day for Morton in which he accumulated 129…
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL preseason Week 2 overreactions: Shedeur Sanders will start for Browns, Jets' defense is fixed
summary: Not everything that unfolded in the second batch of preseason action is worth reading into
full_text:
The NFL preseason is ripe for overreactions. Much of what unfolds on game days should be taken with a grain of salt as teams hold back the "good stuff" from their playbooks and rest their starters. At the same time, some of the offseason's most important decisions come down to these games. Such is the case in Cleveland, where the Browns might have settled their quarterback competition after a preseason Week 2 eyesore from Deshaun Watson and a solid showing from Shedeur Sanders .
Sanders may be the biggest winner from the second set of preseason games . De'Zhaun Stribling could be on his way to a stellar rookie season with the 49ers if Thursday's display of receiving prowess was any indication. And the Jets ' defense actually looks… competitive?
Not all of those takeaways are guaranteed to play out come the regular season. Some of what unfolded in the second week of the preseason will go down as mere exhibition fallout rather than meaningful data.
Let's separate overreactions from reality.
The plan was always for Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders to get one start apiece to open the preseason. Now that Todd Monken has the data points he set out to acquire, a decision on which of the two will open the regular season atop the depth chart is imminent. In fact, i t could come as soon as Monday . And after Watson's disastrous showing on Saturday, it is hard to picture the veteran winning the job.
It is not as if Sanders went out and won the job himself. He threw an interception in each of his first two preseason outings and was underwhelming in Week 1, albeit with a decent bounce-back effort (9-for-11, 74 yards, one touchdown, one interception) in Week 2. The potential pecking order in Cleveland is more a product of Watson looking unplayable on Saturday.
While Watson outplayed Sanders a week ago, he floundered in his most recent appearance with poorly placed throws and a 5-for-12, 35-yard stat line with an interception. Browns fans booed him off the field, and while Monken said Watson's postgame comments toward the Cleveland faithful will not impact the starting quarterback decision, they were a poor look.
It has been difficult to find uplifting storylines from 49ers camp due to their onslaught of injuries, but De'Zhaun Stribling's emergence as a potentially game-changing rookie is as pleasant a development as any in the Bay Area. A week after he racked up seven catches for 63 yards as the leader of San Francisco's receiving unit, Stribling tied with KhaDarel Hodge for the most catches (four) and yards (46) of any 49er on Thursday.
Importantly, three of those catches came on connections with starting quarterback Brock Purdy . The two were on the same page from the get-go in the rout of the Chargers and strung together three completions on the opening drive. Stribling then hauled in a 21-yard grab from Mac Jones on the team's second possession.
Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in April's draft, saw his Rookie of the Year odds spike. Per DraftKings , his +1100 odds are the fifth-shortest behind only Jeremiyah Love , Jadarian Price , Fernando Mendoza and Carnell Tate . He has been as productive as any of them this preseason, but the sheer volume of contenders for the award (and the fact that Love and Price, at least, figure to hold larger roles) still means he will have to outperform expectations to win the honor .
Verdict: Overreaction… but possible!
Tua Tagovailoa threw just three passes in the first week of the preseason and watched Saturday's 34-6 drubbing of the Colts from the sideline. That is a starter's preseason workload. His grasp on the role is tenuous, though.
Neither Cooper Rush nor Jack Strand will unseat Tagovailoa from the starting job, but the Falcons have to appreciate what they combined to deliver in this week's offensive showcase. Strand, an undrafted rookie, racked up 212 passing yards, 22 rushing yards and a touchdown both through the air and on the ground. Cooper Rush went 10-for-11.
The real threat to Tagovailoa is twofold. First, he has been underwhelming in camp. Second, Michael Penix Jr . is cleared for 11-on-11 work and figures to make a run at the job. This always figured to be a two-man battle, and now that Penix is healthy, he has about three weeks to make up ground and potentially leap past his fellow southpaw. His momentum from 7-on-7 and individual drills gives him a shot to do so.
The Jets' defense infamously went the entire 2025 season without recording an interception. The group secured two takeaways in one game during Week 2 of the preseason. Andre Cisco , who is in the mix for a starting role at one of the safety spots, hauled in the first one while reserve cornerback Samuel Womack III grabbed the second. Both came against Steelers quarterback Will Howard .
Toss in a David Bailey sack, two sacks from Nate Lynn and another from Chase Wilson , and it was a banner day for New York. The starting unit played into the second quarter of a game in which the Steelers went scoreless.
Remember, though, that this came against Pittsburgh's No. 2 offense. And keep in mind that while the Jets overhauled the unit with a plethora of free agent additions, none of them are elite players. Aaron Glenn needs this group to hold its own in 2026, and it may just do that. But this shutout means very little.
When J.J. McCarthy fell short of Kyler Murray in the competition for the Vikings ' starting quarterback duties, the reasonable conclusion was that he would settle in as the No. 2 option in the group. Even that might be a stretch for the third-year pro at this point. He had a rough go of it against the Ravens' defense on Saturday; across 18 snaps, he completed just five of 10 passes, took three hits and fell victim to a sack.
Coach Kevin O'Connell said that McCarthy would have played longer if not for being "banged up" during his limited work. That highlights another issue with the former first-round pick: he simply cannot stay healthy.
While O'Connell said a week ago that McCarthy is Minnesota's No. 2 quarterback, it is increasingly clear that he does not have a long-term future in this offense. Carson Wentz might give the Vikings a better chance of winning games if Murray misses any time.
The search to find a successor to Mason Crosby since his departure in 2022 has been anything but smooth for the Packers . It appears that they finally have an answer, however. They were the only team to use a draft pick on a kicker in 2026, and it looks like an astute move. Sixth-rounder Trey Smack has been a preseason standout.
In Week 1, Smack drilled a 58-yard field goal and matched that distance on a kick that was ultimately waved off for a defensive penalty. He went 3-for-3 in his professional debut. That was just the start of it. He was even better this week and made all four of his field goal attempts , with two coming from more than 50 yards out. His longest was a 59-yard blast.
After a year in which Green Bay missed four extra points and was as reliable as a coin flip on kicks beyond 50 yards, special teams could suddenly be a legitimate weapon.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson's comments towards Browns fans won't impact decision on starting quarterback
summary: Watson called Browns fans 'disrespectful' following Saturday's loss
full_text:
While it appeared that Deshaun Watson's postgame comments all but ended his chance at winning his position battle over Shedeur Sanders, Browns coach Todd Monken said that they will not be factored into his decision. Monken added that he plans to announce who will be the team's starting quarterback on Monday.
Watson followed up his poor performance during Saturday's loss to the Bills by taking aim at fans who booed him during the game. Saturday was Watson's first game in front of Cleveland's home fans since his tore his Achilles in Week 7 of the 2024 season. Watson went 5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception during Cleveland's eventual 31-7 loss.
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said . "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."
To make his point, Watson noted that Saturday wasn't the first time that he felt the ire of Browns fans. He added that he gets treated better by opposing fans.
"Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt," he said. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in your home stadium, and they cheer."
Watson said that his experiences with Browns fans are usually only negative on either social media or during home games. He was hoping that the situation regarding the fans' treatment of him would be better given his involvement in the city and after he worked to get himself back in position to compete to be the Browns' starting quarterback.
"I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in and being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person that I know I am and the character would help," he said . "And I guess it hasn't. So that's why I say it's personal. So it is what it is. People have their own opinions. There's only so much you can do to change that. So at the end of the day, I just have to continue to just work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward."
Saturday was a continuation of the downward spiral that has been Watson's career, especially since he arrived in Cleveland in 2022. A three-time Pro Bowler with the Texans , injuries and inconsistent play have plagued Watson throughout his time with the Browns. He is 9-10 as the Browns' starting quarterback with just 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a mediocre 61.2% completion percentage.
Adding to the frustration that has been Watson's story in Cleveland is the amount of capital the Browns spent to get him. They sent Houston six draft picks that included three consecutive first-round picks in addition to signing Watson to a record-setting, five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract. It's undeniably one of -- if not the -- worst transactions in the history of sports .
There's also the fact that the Browns traded for Watson despite the fact that he had already been sued by over two dozen female massage therapists for sexual harassment and sexual assault (in 2022, it was announced that 20 of the 24 women who sued Watson had reached confidential settlements). Watson's time in Cleveland began with him serving an 11-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy.
In addition to Watson's plight, the fact that he's competing against the immensely popular Sanders doesn't help his cause. Sanders, who made the Pro Bowl as a rookie, went 9 of 11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and an interception against the Bills. Sanders also shone during his postgame press conference when he was asked about the fans' treatment of Watson.
"I think we all need to understand that we're all human," he said . "I don't really do things to humans I wouldn't want done to me. ... Just for our fans, I appreciate y'all showing up and everything. However y'all feel about the situation, about Deshaun, I think it's more about a bigger purpose than just respect. The respect thing that I feel like should be there. Because we're out trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise the best way possible. We're going out there every game and doing everything we can do. I don't really appreciate that."
As noted above, Watson didn't do himself any favors both during and after Saturday's game. And while Monken said that his postgame comments won't impact his decision, Watson's response when asked if he can play through more boos from Browns fans if he wins the starting job should be cause for concern.
"I don't know," he said. "It's a mental battle every day. I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games. If it is my spot and he does makes me the [starter], maybe it's 17 away games then. I don't know."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: George Kittle injury update: Latest on 49ers star's status, potential return
summary: Kittle has been working his way back from a torn Achilles
full_text:
For a change, the 49ers have some positive news from an injury standpoint. San Francisco has activated tight end George Kittle from the physically unable to perform list. Kittle has been working his way back from a torn Achilles injury that was sustained during January's playoff win over the Eagles .
After sustaining the injury, Kittle set his sights on being back on the field for the 49ers' season-opener, which will be against the Rams . Kittle has reportedly hit every benchmark the team has laid out for him.
"I want to play in every football game that I possibly can play in, but I'm also aware it's an 18-week season," Kittle said earlier this month . "If you miss Week 1 and you're playing Week 2, hey, it is what it is ... I'm just going to keep that as my goal, and then we'll adjust from there if we need to."
It goes without saying that Kittle's return is a big boost for a 49ers team that is seemingly always dealing with injuries . Now, 32, Kittle has been one of the best players at his position since joining the 49ers in 2017. Last year, he was named to his seventh Pro Bowl despite missing six games during the regular season.
A certified 49ers legend, Kittle has a chance to reach several individual franchise milestones in 2026. He's 565 yards from passing Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for second place on the team's career receiving list. Kittle is also just receiving touchdowns away from third on the franchise's all-time list, behind only Owens and fellow Hall of Famer Jerry Rice.
Last season, Kittle moved past Owens and into second in franchise history (behind only Rice) in career receptions.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Mike Vrabel makes surprising admission about Patriots: 'I don't think we have a very deep team'
summary: Vrabel's team apparently has a pretty big deficiency entering the 2026 season
full_text:
Following his team's preseason win over the Eagles , Patriots coach Mike Vrabel made an honest acknowledgment about his team that is typically something that wouldn't be heard from a coach, let alone one that is coming off a Super Bowl appearance.
Vrabel's surprising assessment of his team came after he was asked about resting his starters for a second straight preseason game . Instead of breezing past the question with a non-answer, Vrabel went with the direct approach.
"I don't think we have a very deep team, Mike," Vrabel said while addressing the reporter who asked the question. "So, you know, I think we have to make sure that we're preparing our football team, and that we're doing everything that we can to keep our best players available. And if that means playing Thursday (in New England's final preseason game) as part of preparation, that's what we'll do. Have not made that decision yet, but I would say that that's something that I'm confident in with where we're set up currently."
Vrabel's admission quickly generated attention on social media, and for good reason. He essentially said that he is keeping his starters out of preseason games because the Patriots can ill afford to lose any of their starters, as they currently do not have the depth necessary to replace them.
That's troubling on several levels, most especially because, in a physical sport like football, depth is a critical component to a team. It's one of the biggest things a team needs to have in order to endure the rigors of a 17-game regular season and a three- or four-game postseason.
Fortunately for Patriots fans, the team's apparent lack of depth can improve. New England will have the ability to sign a slew of players who will be available at the end of the preseason when teams make their initial 53-man roster cuts. The Patriots can also trade for players from other teams at any time until November 10.
Another option, and the most tangible one, is for Vrabel and his staff to continue coaching up the backups who currently make up the roster. Part of that, Vrabel said, will involve working on consistency and not making the same mistake twice.
"As far as some of the younger guys, we need to make new mistakes, because you need to be able to count on some of these guys when we put the roster together to be able to contribute," Vrabel said. "I think that there's a lot of ebbs and flows in a professional football game. How can you handle making a mistake? How can you handle getting blocked? How can you handle being a good play and then coming back and being able to do it again?
"How they bounce back, how they handle different situations, what they do in live action, I think is really critical."
From a depth perspective, one notable positive from Saturday's game was second-year running back Lan Larison . Larison, a former undrafted rookie who suffered a season-ending foot injury last preseason, had 12 touches for 74 yards that included a touchdown run and a 28-yard reception.
"I felt like Lan certainly had a good performance," Vrabel said. "A gritty, tough, performance tonight. He did some really good things."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Bills express support for Ed Oliver following the tragic death of his son
summary: Buffalo is rallying around Oliver after tragedy strikes his family
full_text:
Prior to the Bills ' preseason win over the Browns , general manager Brandon Beane issued a statement regarding veteran defensive tackle Ed Oliver's tragic family situation.
According to ESPN , Oliver's son -- who was two years old -- died after he was found unresponsive in a swimming pool by family members at a residence outside Houston on June 28. Oliver, who, along with his family, has been mourning the tragic loss, has asked for "privacy and prayers at this very difficult time."
"On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to publicly express our condolences to Ed Oliver and his family on the devastating loss of his son," Beane said. "It's an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we all grieve this tragic loss."
Bills coach Joe Brady and quarterback Josh Allen spoke about Oliver following Buffalo's 31-7 preseason win over the Browns.
"As a coach, as a father, it's my job to be what he needs from me right now," Brady said. "And that's loving him and giving him the privacy that he deserves, and whatever it looks like, no matter how someone might want to handle it, it's however he wants us to handle it."
"There's nothing that you can say to make the situation any better except being there for Ed in whatever way he needs," Allen said. "As a team, we're going to continue to love up on him.
