title: Bears vs Bengals: Inside the snap counts, stats, and a sloppy loss
summary: The Chicago Bears looked crisp and disciplined last week in their preseason win against the Cleveland Browns, but yesterday against the Cincinnati Bengals, they looked like a different team. The Bengals rolled to a 27-9 win, as the Bears failed to get anything going. They were just 2 of 14 (14.3%) on third downs and […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears punter Tory Taylor (19) punts the ball against the Cincinnati Bengals in the first half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears looked crisp and disciplined last week in their preseason win against the Cleveland Browns, but yesterday against the Cincinnati Bengals, they looked like a different team. The Bengals rolled to a 27-9 win, as the Bears failed to get anything going. They were just 2 of 14 (14.3%) on third downs and 1 of 3 on fourth downs, while committing 11 penalties for 81 yards after only getting flagged twice vs Cleveland. The Bengals were 46.2% on third-down tries and were penalized 9 times for 49 yards. The Bears had 430 yards of offense last week, but just 322 yesterday in Cincy, while the Bengals put up 346. Chicago’s three quarterbacks only completed 55.8% of their passes for 250 yards, and it wasn’t all inaccuracy, as there were a few drops too. The Bears had the game’s only takeaway (an interception), but they didn’t get any sacks. They held the Bengals’ ground game to just 64 yards on 20 attempts (3.2 ypc), but allowed 282 passing yards and 3 touchdowns through the air. Head coach Ben Johnson said the Bears had only one injured player: reserve linebacker Nephi Sewell. Before we get into some more numbers, here are all the Bears who did not play against the Browns. And here is how the Bears started the day on both sides of the ball. Here are the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats. Offense With so many players participating for the Bears in the preseason, I’ll split the snap count lists into two for both the offense and the defense. Also, keep in mind that special teams snaps in these preseason games often indicate the reserve players coaches have in mind for the third phase, either on the 53-man roster or for the practice squad. Caleb Williams was just 2 for 5 in his one series for 28 yards. Roschon Johnson led the Bears in rushing with 42 yards on 12 attempts. He added a catch for a yard. Case Keenum was 9 for 17 for 119 yards. Jahdae Walker had the Bears’ longest play from scrimmage on his only catch, a 36-yard reception from Keenum. Rookie tight end Sam Roush had 2 receptions for 30 yards. Wideout Maurice Alexander led the Bears in receiving with 60 yards on 5 catches. Rookie Miller Moss was 13 of 21 passing for 103 yards, and he had a 5-yard scramble. Salvon Ahmed had 6 runs for 36 yards and 3 catches for 14 yards, plus a tackle on special teams. Receiver JP Richardson had 5 receptions for 48 yards and a 14-yard kick return. Defense Corner Dontae Manning had 5 tackles and 3 passes defended, plus a tackle in the third phase. Dayo Odeyingbo had a QB hit. Neville Gallimore had 3 tackles and a QB hit. Daniel Hardy had 2 tackles, a TFL, and a special teams tackle. Rookie linebacker Wayne Matthews III tied for the team lead with 7 tackles on defense, and he added another on special teams. Ruben Hyppolite II also had 7 tackles. Jordan van den Berg had 3 tackles. Defensive end Jeremiah Martin had a tackle, a tackle for loss, and a QB hit. UDFA safety Skyler Thomas had 2 tackles and an interception. Special Teams *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was 3 for 4 on field goals, with his miss coming from 53 yards (wide right). Tory Taylor had 6 punts and a 51.8 average (40.8 net), with 1 punt inside the twenty. Receiver Kaden Davis had 1 tackle, 2 punt returns for 11 yards and 2 kick returns for 48 yards. Long snapper Beau Gardner had a tackle. To check out the full Bears vs. Bengals box score, ESPN has an easy-to-navigate site. All statistics, snap counts, and accompanying pictures are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistics and Information System.

title: The Bengals may be ready to find a new swing tackle
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals handily defeated the Chicago Bears on Saturday night, going to 2-0 in the preseason so far, by a score of 27-9. The defense kept the Bears out of the end zone throughout the entire game — even though the Bears’ starters played while the Bengals benched theirs — and both Josh Johnson […]
full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals guard Cody Ford (61) leaves the field after a game against the Arizona Cardinals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals handily defeated the Chicago Bears on Saturday night, going to 2-0 in the preseason so far, by a score of 27-9. The defense kept the Bears out of the end zone throughout the entire game — even though the Bears’ starters played while the Bengals benched theirs — and both Josh Johnson and Sean Clifford were able to score touchdowns. They may have an offensive line problem. though. It’s not with their starters—Orlando Brown Jr, Dylan Fairchild, Ted Karras, Dalton Risner, and Amarius Mims are set and did not play in Week 2 of the preseason. They have an issue with their backup offensive linemen. Over the last three years, Cody Ford has been the team’s swing tackle, though he has played every position on the line save center. He started at right guard for the Bengals on Saturday night, and he struggled (especially in pass protection, earning a 0.0 from PFF). And it hasn’t just been this game either. Based on multiple reports, Ford has had an inconsistent camp at best, and obviously hasn’t inspired trust that he can back up Brown and Mims—both of whom are big guys and have missed games for the Bengals in the past. The Cincinnati Enquirer’s Kelsey Conway was able to discuss the issue with head coach Zac Taylor, and he said no decisions have been made. “I think that’s still pretty open,” he said, per Conway . “I think there’s guys we’re still looking at, and I wouldn’t say there’s any decision we’ve made there.” The Bengals have done so well this offseason when it comes to reshaping the defense. They added Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Bryan Cook, and others, and they added some talent in the draft as well. What they didn’t do was address the offensive line. Hopefully, whoever they decide earns the job doesn’t even need to step on the field, but they need to do something before the season starts. Luckily, there is going to be a large number of cuts made soon, and there’s bound to be someone they could sign as their swing tackle. Or, if they want to be more proactive, they could look at making another trade to bring in a backup offensive tackle. Hopefully they just do something.

title: Bengals News: Josh Johnson makes his case to stick with Cincinnati
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals moved to 2-0 in the preseason Saturday night, taking down the Chicago Bears 27-9 at Paycor Stadium. With Zac Taylor choosing to rest Cincinnati’s starters following Thursday’s joint practice, the game was primarily about giving the players fighting for roster spots another opportunity to make their case. They certainly took advantage of […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Josh Johnson #11of the Cincinnati Bengals runs with the ball against the Chicago Bears during the preseason game at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals moved to 2-0 in the preseason Saturday night, taking down the Chicago Bears 27-9 at Paycor Stadium. With Zac Taylor choosing to rest Cincinnati’s starters following Thursday’s joint practice, the game was primarily about giving the players fighting for roster spots another opportunity to make their case. They certainly took advantage of it. The Bengals’ backups held their own against a Bears team that played a number of its starters, and Cincinnati eventually pulled away for a convincing victory. One of the biggest stories was Dohnte Meyers , who continued his remarkable push for a roster spot, while Colbie Young also made an impact with a touchdown reception. The defense did its part as well, limiting Chicago to three field goals and nine total points, with rookie Landon Robinson among those making noise up front. Evan McPherson remained automatic, hitting both of his field-goal attempts—including a 58-yarder—and all three extra points. But here’s the discussion topic: what do we make of Josh Johnson? The 40-year-old veteran quarterback turned in one of the better performances of the night, completing 15 of 23 passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns without an interception . He connected with Young for a 17-yard touchdown and later found Tanner Hudson for a six-yard score, helping Cincinnati take a 17-9 lead into halftime. Obviously, nobody is suggesting Johnson is going to challenge Joe Burrow for the starting job. But the Bengals brought him back because of his experience, knowledge of NFL offenses and ability to step into a difficult situation if needed. And if Cincinnati is looking for a veteran No. 3 quarterback who can keep the offense functional in an emergency, Johnson’s performance Saturday certainly didn’t hurt his case. In fact, considering how well he operated the offense and the fact that Cincinnati’s other veteran quarterback, Joe Flacco, remains ahead of him on the depth chart, it’s worth asking whether Johnson has already done enough to secure his roster spot. title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 21
summary: It is Day 21 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Football: NFL Championship: Green Bay Packers QB Bart Starr (15) in action, scoring game winning touchdown behind block from teammate Jerry Kramer (64) vs Dallas Cowboys. Ice Bowl. Green Bay, WI 12/31/1967 CREDIT: Marvin Newman (Photo by Marvin Newman /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) It is Day 21 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Get comfy, get somewhere warm for Day 21 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit perhaps the most mythologized game in Cowboys history. Played in conditions so severe that it became known simply as the Ice Bowl. Sunday, December 31, 1967 Lambeau Field, Green Bay, Wisconsin Final Score: Green Bay Packers 21, Dallas Cowboys 17 The Cowboys arrived in Green Bay seeking revenge. The Packers had beaten them 34-27 in the previous season’s NFL Championship Game, intercepting Don Meredith in the end zone on Dallas’ final possession. Green Bay was attempting to win an unprecedented third consecutive league championship, while Tom Landry’s emerging Cowboys were trying to prove they were ready to replace the league’s established power. The conditions became as important as the teams. The temperature at kickoff was marked with the wind chill between 33 and 37 below zero. The field gradually hardened into an icy surface, officials stopped using their metal whistles after one froze to a referee’s lips, and several players required treatment for frostbite. It remains the coldest game in NFL history. Green Bay appeared far more comfortable early. Bart Starr found Boyd Dowler for an eight-yard touchdown on the Packers’ opening scoring drive and connected with him again for another long score early in the second quarter. Dallas had barely moved the football before falling behind 14-0. The Cowboys remained alive because of their defense. Willie Townes stripped Starr on a sack, allowing George Andrie to recover the fumble and return it seven yards for a touchdown. Later in the half, Packers safety Willie Wood mishandled a punt and Dallas recovered at the Green Bay 17-yard line. Danny Villanueva converted a 21-yard field goal, cutting the deficit to 14-10 at halftime despite the Cowboys producing only two first downs during the opening half. Neither team scored during the third quarter, but Dallas finally broke through on the first play of the fourth. Running back Dan Reeves took a handoff moving left, stopped and threw across the field to a wide-open Lance Rentzel. The 50-yard touchdown gave the Cowboys a 17-14 lead and placed them within minutes of the first championship in franchise history. Dallas’ defense protected that advantage until Green Bay took possession at its own 32-yard line with just over five minutes remaining. Starr completed five consecutive passes during the defining drive, using Donny Anderson and Chuck Mercein out of the backfield to move the Packers down the frozen field. Mercein’s 19-yard catch reached the Dallas 11 before an eight-yard run moved Green Bay to the three. Anderson then advanced to the one-yard line, but two further rushing attempts failed when he lost his footing on the ice. Green Bay called its final timeout with 16 seconds remaining. An incomplete pass would have stopped the clock and allowed the Packers to attempt a tying field goal, while another unsuccessful running play could have ended the game. Starr went to the sideline and suggested keeping the ball himself. On third down, he took the snap and followed blocks from center Ken Bowman and guard Jerry Kramer, who drove Dallas defensive tackle Jethro Pugh backward. Starr crossed the goal line with 13 seconds left, giving Green Bay its only points since early in the second quarter and producing the decisive image of the Ice Bowl. Dallas attempted several desperation passes after the kickoff, but none were completed. Green Bay had survived 37 consecutive minutes without scoring to win 21-17 and secure its third straight NFL championship. The Packers later defeated the Oakland Raiders 33-14 in Super Bowl II, completing the final championship season of Lombardi’s tenure as their head coach. This game belongs on the countdown because Cowboys history cannot be told through victories alone. Dallas had gone from an expansion franchise to standing one yard and 13 seconds away from defeating one of football’s greatest dynasties. The loss delayed the Cowboys’ first championship, but it also confirmed that Landry’s team had become one of the NFL’s elite organizations. #Cowboys vs #Packers 1967 The Ice Bowl Final Score: Green Bay Packers 21, Dallas Cowboys 17 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/ckd9UoneWw — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 23, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The official kickoff temperature was minus-13°F. Temperatures during the game ranged from approximately minus-12°F to minus-14°F. title: Cowboys depth chart becomes clearer in win at Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys moved to 2-0 on the 2026 preseason with another road win against a NFC West opponent on Saturday night, 34-13 at the Arizona Cardinals. Like the preseason week one opponent Seattle Seahawks, the Cardinals are another team the Cowboys will also see in the regular season. The Cowboys made some statements about […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Jaishawn Barham #55 of the Dallas Cowboys gets ready to rush the passer during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. Cowboys won 34-13. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys moved to 2-0 on the 2026 preseason with another road win against a NFC West opponent on Saturday night, 34-13 at the Arizona Cardinals. Like the preseason week one opponent Seattle Seahawks, the Cardinals are another team the Cowboys will also see in the regular season. The Cowboys made some statements about their depth chart going into their final week of preseason prep, with Oxnard training camp now behind the team and practice resuming in Frisco on Tuesday. Joe Milton had the offense humming in the first half when Dallas built a 24-6 lead by the break, while Sam Howell did not have the same success in the second half. Jaydon Blue returned to the field after not being seen much at practice leading up to this game, missing the joint practice against the Saints too, and led the team in carries. These 15 carries for Blue compared to eight for Israel Abanikanda and five for Malik Davis don’t nearly tell the full RB competition story though, as Davis again looked good in his limited opportunities, and even Phil Mafah took his one carry of the night for a 15-yard touchdown. Jonathan Mingo scored a touchdown on a 53-yard bomb from Milton. Mingo is an experienced player looking to separate himself from the fan-favorite, Camden Brown. It wasn’t long after this though that Brown had a 69-yard catch and run that was a yard away from being another preseason touchdown for the UDFA, keeping the WR depth chart fight entertaining. On defense, Jaishawn Barham asserted himself in his rookie debut, playing as the “green dot” of Christian Parker’s defense and flying around to make the types of plays that made him one of the stars of the Oxnard portion of camp. Shavon Revel Jr. had an interception that gave the offense a short field to score the first touchdown of the night, and take a lead they never relinquished. Let’s get to a few notes on another exhibition win for Brian Schottenheimer’s team: Malik Davis Malik Davis came into this game as a known commodity when it came to his quick burst ability as a runner between the tackles with above average power as well. Davis has proved this in regular season opportunities, as well as against the Seahawks last week, and got the opportunity off the bat in this game to get going on the ground. It was what Davis did in other phases of the game that caught the eye in a much bigger way though. Following Revel’s interception, the Cowboys faced third and goal and were looking at having to settle for a red zone field goal on a short field. Instead, Davis got open in the pass game on a scramble drill from Milton and caught a nice touch pass near the sideline, turning it up field for a touchdown. Later in the game, Davis had the key blitz pickup on Camden Brown’s big gain, which set up Milton’s QB draw touchdown a play later. It sure looked like Malik Davis gained even more confidence from the coaching staff as a legitimate candidate to be RB2 on Saturday. There were other players in real-time that were taken out of the game after making a few plays, joining the “on ice” contingent, and time will tell very shortly if this was the case for Davis – leaving Blue to get on the field and eat up most of the remaining reps. Blue did show some shiftiness on a few interior carries and accelerated around the corner on a few others as the Cowboys continue to show in these vanilla preseason game plans they want to run the ball between the tackles with purpose. Jaishawn Barham, Shavon Revel Jr. Speaking of Shavon Revel’s confidence-building interception and 22-yard return, this was one of several plays for rookie LB Jaishawn Barham that should get graded upon film review as a “green check” or a “plus”. The Dallas defense was able to get the home team behind the sticks, thanks in large part to Barham undercutting a blocker and making a tackle for loss on an early down run. On third and 13, the Cowboys dropped into their zone coverage, and in one rep showed a tightness and cohesiveness doing so that may not have been seen at all in the zone played last season. The one singular area the Cowboys defense did make some noise in last year was when they had offenses in longer downs and distances, but still the overall idea for 2026 is that Christian Parker will bring improvements in all elements, having the clean start to do so with after how porous this defense was a year ago. Revel, Barham, Shemar James, and Julius Wood all got to their spots in the expanding zone defense quickly and efficiently, and it put Revel in position to intercept the errant pass and finish the play with a turnover. This was a great example of the exact type of improvements the Cowboys are looking for on defense, and setting up short fields for an offense that hasn’t even put Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Javonte Williams, George Pickens, or Ryan Flournoy on the field yet is a huge, huge deal. Doing so will give the Cowboys a chance to win the red zone differential by a significant margin when the regular season rolls around, as this win against the Cardinals also flashed more strong defense in the red area for Dallas. For the second week in a row, the combination of Tyrus Wheat and James Houston off the edge in a short field situation got the quick pressure for Wheat and rookie LT Overton to combine on a third down sack and force a field goal attempt. Interior Defense For the interior of the defense, the players the Cowboys have on ice are expected to make it extremely difficult for many roster longshots to get a real chance, but some players did their best to make another good impression against the Cardinals. Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbonnia should handle the majority of snaps as down linemen, but among the best of the rest, Jay Toia reminded everyone what he can do in this game. A seventh-round pick from 2025 that appeared in five games as a rookie, Toia has taken another step with his get-off on the snap and strength to push the pocket. The DT had a hit on Kedon Slovis that nearly forced a fumble on a possession for the Cardinals that started after a Howell interception in the end zone. This led to the Cowboys getting off the field with a fourth-down stop, creating the second instance in as many preseason games where the defense was able to turn up the intensity and pick up either the special teams (muffed punt) or offense following a turnover. With Overton also flashing in both pass rush and run support as a down lineman in this game, the Cowboys overall situation up front on defense is as good as it’s been in a long time, with stars in waiting to start games, and young depth ready to step in as well. The NFC West has been known as a division where all opponents are strong in the trenches anyway, and through two preseason games against opponents from this division, the Cowboys work to be better in the trenches themselves is showing itself well. Miscellaneous Phil Mafah’s touchdown to cap the scoring on the night was not how the Cowboys drew up that particular run play, with Mafah completely cutting it back and reversing fields to the end zone, but it was still a nice highlight for the second-year back in a battle for carries. Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams didn’t forget about rookie seventh-round receiver Anthony Smith in this game either, getting him a touch on a sweep carry. There is still a lot to figure out about who this team will keep at WR as they return to Texas. For one final note on the offense, this was yet another game where rookie fourth-round pick Drew Shelton was inconsistent. Dallas understandably had to pivot from their usual offseason and draft approach of prioritizing offensive line talent and depth above all…

title: Cowboys at Cardinals Stock Report: Joe Milton takes QB2, Jaishawn Barham announces self
summary: Saturday night went about as well as you could have expected it to for the Dallas Cowboys. They scored. And they did so often. Players answered important questions like who will serve as key backups at quarterback and running back for example. Young and future stars like Jaishawn Barham corroborated the hype that they have […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals running back Evan Hull (43) runs the ball against Dallas Cowboys linebacker Jaishawn Barham (55) in the first half at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Saturday night went about as well as you could have expected it to for the Dallas Cowboys. They scored. And they did so often. Players answered important questions like who will serve as key backups at quarterback and running back for example. Young and future stars like Jaishawn Barham corroborated the hype that they have had for the past month. Heck, it was only the preseason, but the Cowboys even beat the boogeyman in the Arizona Cardinals. Hopefully that translates to November 1st. As you can imagine our stock report is full of high marks, but there are some notes for improvement as well. Let’s begin. Stock Up: Jaishawn Barham We have all seen someone shine in training camp just for them to fade when the lights actually turned on. In his first test, Jaishawn Barham said that this would not be the case for him. Only a preseason game and all of that, but Barham looked incredible in Arizona. Barham makin’ plays right away #DALvsAZ | @JaishawnBarham 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/kuZmG9kwXv — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 It isn’t just that Barham presents an answer for the Cowboys at middle linebacker. That is a big deal given the team’s need for one all offseason, clearly. It is the force with which Barham plays. He is of a different breed, and thankfully that breed took him to the Cowboys. Stock Up: Shavon Revel Camp has also seen second-year cornerback Shavon Revel shine at different times. We have told ourselves that this is indeed impressive because he was going against the likes of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on a regular basis, but doing it against someone else is still a different thing. For so long it has seemed like confidence may be a catalyst for Revel, and that came to him against the Cardinals by way of getting on the board with an interception. Shavon gets us back the ball 🔄 #DALvsAZ | @ShavonRevel 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/UzpMTPRWgq — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 More of this, please. Stock Up: Malik Davis Ladies and gentlemen, we have found the RB2 for the Dallas Cowboys. the offense turns the INT into a TD 💪 #DALvsAZ | @Campaign_Lik 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/3TOSx2hFAw — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 People on social media are equating Malik Davis to Jourdan Lewis in terms of how he is just hanging around the roster and refuses to let the team move on from him. I love that comparison, and it is certainly apt. We can quibble about how some of Davis’ roster security is because of how others haven’t fully taken the bull by the horns regarding the RB2 spot, but the point is that if you give him an inch he is going ot make the absolute most with it. I want that dude on my team. Stock Up: Jonathan Mingo Speaking of people who refuse to go away! GOIN' DEEEEEEP 👀 #DALvsAZ | @ogmingo1k 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/dyIt4aRRyg — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 The Cowboys are definitely going to carry Mingo, right? I mean, they should. Right? Right? There is no doubt that Jonathan Mingo’s time with the Cowboys has been… unique. His arrival coincided with the peak of toxicity that the front office was stirring up over the last two years, and in some ways people made up their mind about him the moment the trade was struck. He hasn’t performed, it was noted that this was actually his first ever NFL touchdown (preseason or regular season), but he seems to be turning a corner. Stock Up: Joe Milton The jury is back. They have conferred and determined that Joe Milton is in fact QB2 for the Dallas Cowboys. QB sneak ⬆️ #DALvsAZ | @Qbjayy7 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/EjxHTseodo — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 This particular moment was hardly Milton’s best one from the night, but that’s because the other highlights are scattered around to the players who he helped perform. He had that many moments to pick and choose from. It was clear that the Cowboys wanted to see what Milton could do from a passing perspective and he absolutely cleared whatever bar anybody had. He has come so far in his second season with the team and is now marrying his rocket arm with proper anticipation and overall reading of defenses. He has a different feel for the game and that he is under contract through next season gives the team some serious stability behind Dak Prescott. Stock Up: Camden Brown Camden Brown had already made the roster in many people’s minds, but in case you were still doubting: . @Qbjayy7 to @CamdenBrown7 for a HUGE gain❗️ 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/vj4VZ0O8Wo — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 We have seen more than enough at this point in time. Tell me that reach near the end didn’t give you PTSD from the Dez catch, though. Stock Up: LT Overton What a night Saturday was for the rookies! first career sack for @LebbeusO 🔥 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/7dRtDwdRfg — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 Being fully honest here, this was clearly a coverage sack. Everybody deserves credit for making it happen, but LT Overton is the person who the box score rewards as he was the one who brought down the quarterback. For all of the discussion about new rookies and defenders there hasn’t been a ton of mention around Overton. Time will tell how the roster math shakes out, but it is great to see him thrive nonetheless. Stock Up: Phil Mafah Let’s give it up for the Mafah Man! Phil Mafah got one carry on the night, and he sure did make the most of it by cashing in for a score. to the ➡️, to the ⬅️, to the endzone #DALvsAZ | @PhilMafah1 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/41A7X2M4GV — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 As awesome as this moment was, it is a bit telling that Mafah received only a single carry, especially given how much the team ran the ball in the second half. Any hope that he could grab the RB2 spot dissipated a while back, but he can definitely help in his own way. Stock Down: Zack Kuntz Due to injuries the Cowboys only had two tight ends in this game in Zack Kuntz and Luke Schoonmaker. You can argue that Kuntz was on the outside looking in as far as roster discussion before this game even began, but he didn’t exactly have a game that would make anybody change their mind. Sometimes that’s just the way it goes. Maybe this is a practice squad situation. Stock Down: Devin Moore This game marked the debut of fourth-round rookie Devin Moore, and it was a bit underwhelming to say the least. Cornerback has been among the biggest question marks on the overall roster for some time. We have given a fair bit of leeway to the idea that Christian Parker will just naturally raise the floor there, but there was definitely hope that a player like Moore would battle his way into some conversations. That has not happened yet and that is okay. Stock Down: Sam Howell If it was Joe Milton’s night then it was also not Sam Howell’s. Milton left a very high bar to clear when he sat on the bench for the second half, and the calculus of the game hardly worked in Howell’s favor as a result. The broadcast, the Cowboys one to be clear, even discusses this as the Cowboys had a rather large lead and were not in the same sort of passing mode that they were in the first half. This naturally inhibited the opportunity from a volume standpoint for Howell. Still, he had a chance. The Cowboys…

title: From forgotten Patriot to the Cowboys new backup plan
summary: The Dallas Cowboys have found themselves a backup quarterback. It wasn’t easy and took a little bit of trial and error, but lo and behold, they are finally reaping the rewards of making a good trade. And those rewards come courtesy of Joe Milton III. This story first began last offseason when the team was […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys drops back to pass during the first quarter of the preseason NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys have found themselves a backup quarterback. It wasn’t easy and took a little bit of trial and error, but lo and behold, they are finally reaping the rewards of making a good trade. And those rewards come courtesy of Joe Milton III. This story first began last offseason when the team was searching for a young quarterback they could develop after the failed Trey Lance experience. Rather than wallowing in disappointment or changing up their strategy, the front office reloaded and found a great opportunity to acquire Milton thanks to the New England Patriots’ abundance of depth. The Patriots already had a franchise quarterback in their pocket in Drake Maye, and they just signed free agent Joshua Dobbs. Keeping Milton meant they’d have to use a roster spot for a developmental guy buried on the depth chart. That wasn’t what they wanted to do, so they found a suitor and shipped him off, and that suitor was the Cowboys. Initially, it felt like an easy win for the Cowboys. Unlike the previous Lance trade, the team did not have to give up a fourth-round draft pick. Not even close. The trade cost next to nothing as the Cowboys gave up a late-round pick (no. 171) for an early seventh-round pick (no. 217). That’s essentially a 46-spot move back on Day 3 of the 2025 draft. Like we said, almost nothing. This seemed like a screaming deal for Dallas considering the sample size they had on Milton was pretty decent. He had played one game in 2024, and he looked really good. He showed nice poise in the pocket, made good decisions with the football, and placed the ball in great spots. It was only one game, but how could the Patriots let this guy go for so cheap? It didn’t add up. I know it's only one game, but Joe Milton looked fantastic in his NFL debut last year. He hung in the pocket, made good decisions, and rifled the ball right where it needed to go. There are legitimate reasons for Cowboys fans to be excited by this move. pic.twitter.com/RXXHJk3IlJ — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) April 6, 2025 Sadly, it didn’t take long for that excitement to wear off. It was as if the clock struck midnight and he turned back into a pumpkin. Reports in his first camp validated the Patriots’ apprehensions and showed that he’s still a developing quarterback. When preseason action rolled around, there would be glimpses of his mobility and cannon arm, but far more instances of him airmailing passes or launching short-range missiles that would carom off the body of his intended targets. He just wasn’t ready. Oddly, the Cowboys went into last season with Milton and only Milton as their backup, despite clear signs that he wasn’t ready for the spotlight. Fortunately for the offense, he wasn’t needed. Dak Prescott was healthy the entire year and played all 17 games. When Milton was called into action, it was garbage time only, and he did exactly what you’d expect. He wowed us with some big plays, and then he’d cap off the drive with a bad throw that ended up in the arms of the other team. He played sparingly in four games last year, all of which were three-score losses. The high-variance play of Milton seemed to suggest that the Cowboys had once again whiffed on a developmental QB. At least this one didn’t cost much, but that cost would be much greater if they had to throw him into action to help win a meaningful football game. That’s why it made perfect sense for the Cowboys to hedge their bets and sign free agent quarterback Sam Howell. The veteran came with his own baggage, but at least now the team could decide between the lesser of two evils after a good old training camp battle. What’s happened since is hard to explain. The steps Milton has taken in a matter of a year have been massive. His play on Saturday was a completely different quarterback than we’ve seen previously during his time in Dallas. He showed great poise in the pocket, stood tall, and calmly made his reads. He wasn’t skittish or looking to run at the first sign of trouble. His footwork was steady, and he delivered perfect strikes to his receivers. What’s even more impressive than his clean pocket moments is what he did when things broke down. And they did. When the pocket collapsed, Milton calmly stepped forward and relocated. He didn’t panic and take off running the ball. He simply evaded pressure, stayed behind the line of scrimmage, and re-calculated his position. Against the Cardinals, the young quarterback delivered so many well-thrown balls while on the run. It was a thing of beauty. After watching him wind up and misfire so many times last year, seeing him throw with a soft touch and accuracy was nothing short of amazing. The improvements Milton has made are almost night and day different. This wasn’t just one game. It’s now two games stacked on top of each other. Two really great halves of football for the young quarterback where he’s now gone 21/28 passing (75% completion rate) for 286 yards, three touchdowns, and no picks. That’s a 142.8 passer rating. He’s also rushed for a touchdown. His confidence is showing, and his understanding of what he is supposed to do was on full display. Better familiarity with the playbook and correcting previous mistakes has put him in a great position going forward. He’s only halfway through his cheap rookie deal, meaning the Cowboys have player control over the next two seasons for just $1 million per year. Having secured a quality backup is a great achievement, and that is what the Cowboys have done. It didn’t come instantly, but through patience and hard work, Milton looks to be the guy they can call on if Prescott misses action. It’s a good feeling to have that added sense of security and know that the awesomeness of the team’s explosive receivers won’t fizzle out if their starter goes down. A friendly reminder that all the Cowboys gave up for Joe Milton III is a Day 3 pick swap of 46 spots (traded pick 171 for 217). pic.twitter.com/pf4v7vgPmN — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) August 23, 2026

title: What Von Miller adds to Cowboys pass rush – beyond unrealistic sack expectations
summary: Like it or not, sacks are still the pass rusher’s currency of choice, even if there are advanced metrics available that give us a much clearer picture of a player’s pass-rushing efficiency. And, of course, the first wave of reporting about the Von Miller signing was all about sacks, both about his being the NFL’s […]
full_text: Like it or not, sacks are still the pass rusher’s currency of choice, even if there are advanced metrics available that give us a much clearer picture of a player’s pass-rushing efficiency. And, of course, the first wave of reporting about the Von Miller signing was all about sacks, both about his being the NFL’s active career sack leader and about his nine sacks with Washington last year, his most in a single season since 2021. And Von Miller raised expectations himself on the Night Cap show with Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson: “I can still walk into 8-10 sacks now. And that’s just walking in.” Even the $2 million in incentives in Miller’s Cowboys contract is structured around the number of sacks: $500k — 8 sacks + playoffs $1m — 10 sacks + playoffs $1.5m — 12 sacks + playoffs $2m — 14 sacks + playoffs But this focus on sacks may be a little short-sighted, as John Owning points out . I'm a fan of the Von Miller signing, but I find it hilarious how everyone is quoting the 9 sacks from last year but ignoring the 9.5% pass-rush win rate (very not good) in addition to 8 total quick pressures (less than 2.5 secs). We gotta be honest and not cherry pick stats.… — John Owning (@JohnOwning) August 17, 2026 Sacks, pressures, pass-rush win rates — are we splitting hairs here, or is there value in looking at some advanced metrics in more detail? There may be, especially if you want to get a better feel for how Von Miller might slot into the Cowboys’ pass-rush rotation. To do that, we’ll start by comparing Miller against last year’s defensive rotation in Dallas as well as this year’s presumptive edge-rush rotation. Then we’ll take a closer look at what pass-rush win rate can tell us about this year’s unit. Two ways to measure pass-rush success For this comparison, I’m using two metrics that look at pass-rush success from slightly different angles: Pressure% and Pass-Rush Win Rate. Pressure% is a simple calculation that adds up sacks, hits, and hurries into a total pressure number and divides it by a player’s pass-rush snaps. The data for this calculation is based on the PFF pressure numbers. For example, Von Miller recorded 36 pressures on 289 pass-rush snaps in 2025. That gives him a 12.5% Pressure%. Also, PFF doesn’t count half sacks, so where the PFF shows 10 sacks for Von Miller, official NFL statistics credit him with 9.0. Pass-Rush Win Rate (or Win%) is a proprietary PFF metric that looks at something slightly different than Pressure%. Rather than simply counting pressures, it measures how often a pass rusher is credited with winning his matchup against the blocker. PFF describes its underlying “beaten defender” data as a way of measuring how successful a pass rusher is at beating his man. That distinction is important because the pass rusher doesn’t control how long the quarterback holds the ball. A defender can beat his blocker, but if the quarterback gets rid of the ball quickly enough, the defender may not be credited with a sack, hit, or hurry. PFF can still credit him with a pass-rush win. So, in simple terms: Pressure% asks: How often did the pass rush produce a recorded pressure? Win% asks: How often did the pass rusher beat his blocker? Those aren’t necessarily the same thing — and the difference between the two is where this gets interesting. Establishing some pressure and win-rate benchmarks Before we look at the Cowboys, it helps to establish what constitutes a good Pressure% and Win%. Using PFF data for 99 edge rushers who recorded more than 180 pass-rush snaps in 2025, the players neatly divide into five performance tiers of roughly 20 players each, with almost all having the same cutoffs — only the top tier shows a slightly different cutoff. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Pressure% Win% Description >15 >16 Blue-Chip Players >12.5-15 12.5-16 NFL starter quality at position >11.0-12.5 11.0-12.5 Average to slightly below average player >9.0-11.0 9.0-11.0 Underperformer <9 <9 Red Flag Source: PFF, 99 Edge rushers with >180 pass rush snaps These aren’t official PFF thresholds (even if I’m using their color scheme), and there is obviously some subjectivity in drawing the lines. They’re simply a useful framework for putting the Cowboys’ numbers into context. And this is where things start getting interesting, because a player’s Pressure% and Win% don’t always tell the same story. And the relationship between the two numbers can be particularly revealing. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Relationship What it tells us What it can mean Cowboys example Pressure% > Win% Pressure production is running ahead of the player’s overall win rate. His pressure production is running ahead of the rate at which PFF credits him with winning pass-rush reps. That can indicate a player who is particularly effective at turning his wins into pressures, although the two metrics aren’t directly interchangeable. James Houston: 13.7 Pressure% / 11.4 Win% Pressure% ≈ Win% Pressure production broadly matches the player’s rate of winning pass-rush reps. What we see in the pressure numbers is consistent with what is happening at the line of scrimmage. There is little evidence that either metric is significantly understating or overstating the player’s performance. Sam Williams: 8.9 / 8.7 Pressure% < Win% The player is winning more pass-rush reps than his pressure numbers would suggest. The player’s underlying pass-rush performance may be better than his pressure production indicates. Wins can fail to become pressures when the quarterback gets the ball out before the rusher can affect the play. The underlying pass-rush numbers show a player who was consistently productive when rushing the passer. Dante Fowler presents a different profile. His 12.1 Pressure% puts him around the average-to-starter boundary, but his 14.3 Win% moves him comfortably into the starter-quality range. title: 10 thoughts on Cowboys 34-13 preseason win over Cardinals
summary: Two preseason games, two preseason wins. The Dallas Cowboys completed their second preseason game of the year with a 34-13 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With a late west coast start time, this one kept fans up late, but it gave us plenty to see. Here are 10 thoughts on this after-hours football affair. 1. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Joe Milton #10 of the Dallas Cowboys throws the ball during the first quarter of the preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two preseason games, two preseason wins. The Dallas Cowboys completed their second preseason game of the year with a 34-13 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With a late west coast start time, this one kept fans up late, but it gave us plenty to see. Here are 10 thoughts on this after-hours football affair. 1. Milton has arrived Last year, Joe Milton III looked very raw. That screaming deal we thought the Cowboys got from the Patriots looked like they might’ve been snookered after he was seen overthrowing everyone. But that’s not the guy we’re seeing now. What a difference a year makes. The third-year quarterback looked fantastic. He calmly hung in the pocket, and only ran when he absolutely needed to. He made smart decisions and his touch was near perfect, whether he was settled in the pocket or on the run. He completed 9/13 passes for 179 yards with two touchdowns. He also had a rushing touchdown on a quarterback draw. It was a very sharp first half of football. 2. Efficient offense After stalling out and turning the ball over on downs at the Arizona 12-yard line on their opening drive, the Cowboys offense went on a run, scoring in all four of their remaining first-half possessions. Touchdown. Touchdown. Touchdown. Field goal. That’s not too shabby. Punter Bryan Anger never had to trot onto the field. 3. That was 55 again Those were the words spoken by Cowboys’ announcer Bill Jones after it was clear that the rookie linebacker from Michigan was going to be a regular thing in this one. After missing last week recovering from a groin injury, Jaishawn Barham was wreaking havoc in this one. On the Cardinals first possession, he dipped under the offensive lineman to escape the block to take down the running back for a one-yard loss. Not much later, he crashed down again to make a play. It was a nice debut for the team’s young linebacker. 4. A pick for Revel Don’t look now, but another young Cowboys defender made a play. That was the theme of the night and it was great that second-year corner Shavon Revel Jr. got in on the action. After being tested repeatedly in camp by the game’s toughest receivers, Revel got a little reprieve with the Cardinals backup receivers. He was in the hip pocket of former Cowboys wide receiver Simi Fehoko and when he slipped, Revel was in perfect position to intercept the pass and return it for 22 yards. 5. Stingy defense Not only was the offense scoring often, but the defense was not allowing the Cardinals to get into the end zone. All Arizona had to show for in the first half was two measly field goals. In fact, if it wasn’t for a questionable Caelen Carson pass interference penalty, the Cowboys defense wouldn’t have allowed a single touchdown through the first six quarters of football. We know it’s only preseason, but that’s still pretty good for this defense. 6. Sneaky Malik-y Malik Davis will be on this Cowboys roster. Again. After an impressive showing last week that reminded people why he’s still in the building, the veteran running back was back at it again, making people miss and thumping through defenders. Davis started the game and ran the ball five times for 29 yards and added a touchdown reception on an eight yard dump-off pass. 7. Blue skidoo, he can too Not to be outdone, the second-year running back Jaydon Blue had himself a good game as well. The young back showed a lot of shiftiness, cutting well, and even jumping over defenders. He showed good patience and more drive than he had shown last week. With Davis solidifying one of the running back spots, Blue needed this to keep him in the running as nothing is promised. He finished the game with 75 yard on 15 carries. 8. Don’t write offah Mafah Not to be outdone, second-year back Phil Mafah had the most impressive individual run late in the fourth quarter when he changed direction and ran the ball for a 15-yard touchdown to close things out. Just when you thought he might be the odd man out, he put himself back into the mix. It was a good showing for all of the Cowboys backs this week and should make final roster cuts interesting. 9. Offensive line The run game was in full swing, and a large part of their success was thanks to how well the Cowboys’ second-string offensive line played. They opened up running lanes and gave the quarterbacks plenty of room to operate for the most part. The team swapped tackles as the rookie Drew Shelton started at left tackle while Nate Thomas started at right. The rookie Shelton had a couple of plays where he was beat quickly, but held his own for most of the night. It was a good overall showing by this unit. 10. Mingo/Brown Entering camp, the Cowboys were just hoping that one player would emerge as a potential candidate for that fifth receiver with several guys in the mix. Lately, that pool has been reduced to two guys, Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown. Last week, it was the undrafted rookie Brown who stole the show, although Mingo also played well. On Saturday, it was Mingo who struck first with a long touchdown, but not much later Brown was doing his thing again. This battle is interesting as some figured Brown had locked in a spot last week, but Mingo does a lot of the little things that the coaches love, making a strong push to continue to stick around in Dallas.

title: Cowboys news: Joe Milton’s big night wows again
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won their preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday night, 34-13. It was a big night for backup QB Joe Milton. Jaisahwbn Barham and Shavon Revel Jr. helped spearhead the defense, while all the running backs got in on the action. Let’s recap in our news segment. Cowboys backup QB opens […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys prepares to snap the football during the first quarter of the preseason NFL game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys won their preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals on Saturday night, 34-13. It was a big night for backup QB Joe Milton. Jaisahwbn Barham and Shavon Revel Jr. helped spearhead the defense, while all the running backs got in on the action. Let’s recap in our news segment. Cowboys backup QB opens eyes with preseason performance – Nick Brinkerhoff, USA Today In the battle for the QB2 job, Joe Milton took a big step forward. He was spectacular against the Cardinals on Saturday night. The Dallas Cowboys starting quarterback wasn’t in the lineup for the team’s preseason game on Aug. 22 against the Arizona Cardinals . Instead, it was Joe Milton III that got the nod from head coach Brian Schottenheimer. And Milton made the most of the opportunity. The third-year pro out of Tennessee shined in the opening 30 minutes, leading the Cowboys to a 24-6 halftime lead and accounted for all three touchdowns. Game Recap: Milton leads Cowboys to 34-13 win-Kurt Daniels, Dallascowboys.com A quick recap of the action from Saturday night when the Cowboys had a great showing. Third Quarter The Cardinals weren’t going to go quietly into the night, opening the second half with a lengthy drive to the end zone. They marched 64 yards in 12 plays with Minshew completing 4 of 5 passes for 39 yards. Running back Corey Kiner finished things off with a 1-yard run off left tackle to make things more interesting, 24-13. Although the Cowboys now had a new quarterback behind center in Howell, the offense didn’t skip a beat. An 11-play, 57-yard drive reached the Arizona 11-yard line, where Aubrey added another three points with a 29-yard field goal. Terence Steele’s job isn’t at risk despite Cowboys’ interesting words and antics – Levi Dobro, The Landry Hat Terence Steele has been at the center of a lot of discussion when it comes to the Cowboys’ offensive line. Although things have have been rocky for him, it looks like spot is secure in the starting lineup. Steele is an entrenched starter for this Cowboys team, so much so that he didn’t even play against Seattle. And it’s not like his backups played particularly well or anything, but Dallas’ choice to play Drew Shelton at left tackle and Nate Thomas at right tackle with the 2s this week sparked debate. To add fuel to this fire, both head coach Brian Schottenheimer and offensive coordinator Klayton Adams made comments this week about Steele needing to be more consistent. But if you really dive into what they said and look at the situation, this isn’t an indictment of Steele, nor is his job on the line. Jerry Jones has every reason to believe in Cowboys’ playoff potential after latest NFL predictions – Sam Haider, Sporting News Might this Cowboys team be “Super”? Better yet, is Jerry Jones right to possibly feel that way? “Quarterback Dak Prescott has a solid offensive line in front of him, as well as an elite wide receiver duo in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens,” Clay wrote. While the Cowboys boasted one of the NFL’s most explosive offenses in 2025, questions remain on the other side of the ball. They finished fifth in the league in scoring, averaging 27.7 points per game, but their defense struggled throughout the season, surrendering an NFL-worst 30.1 points per contest. The Cowboys have since made significant changes in hopes of improving that unit. Former Penn State Star, NFC East Rival Admits Cowboys Won Micah Parsons Trade – Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated Well, that settles it. A former NFC East legend claims the debate is over as we have a clear winner following Dallas’ trade of Micah Parsons. Despite his ties to Parsons and dislike for the Dallas franchise, Arrington was willing to admit the Cowboys are the winners of the 2025 trade with the Green Bay Packers . When asked on Thursday night for his thoughts, he made it clear that he didn’t like saying it, but gave the nod to Jerry Jones. “If you’re saying addition by subtraction, you probably gotta say,” Arrington said while starting to mouth the word “Cowboys,” according to Edward Lewis of the New York Post . “I’m not going to say it!” Cowboy CeeDee Lamb’s home in Fairview burglarized, $300,000 in luxury bags stolen, according to report – Michael Cuviello, Dallas Morning News Cowboys star receiver was a victim of a crime while away at Cowboys training camp. The Fairview home of Dallas Cowboys star receiver CeeDee Lamb was burglarized while he attended the team’s training camp in California, with four luxury bags valued at $300,000 reported stolen, according to Fairview Police Department records obtained by the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. The burglary occurred between midnight and 3 a.m. July 30, an incident report shows. Police were notified shortly after 1:20 p.m. the following day. The report lists Lamb as the victim and classifies the offenses as burglary of a habitation and theft of property valued at $300,000 or more. Under stolen property, it lists four luxury bags with a reported value of $300,000.

title: How is this Broncos’ run game going to be?
summary: Last week’s Reacts poll is a bit of a moot point after the Broncos did not showcase an electric rushing attack against the Packers the way they had against the Falcons. And so it goes with the run game in Denver. One week up, next week down. While everything must be filtered with the fact […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Pat Bryant #13 after catching a touchdown pass against the Green Bay Packers during the first half of the preseason game at Empower Field At Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week’s Reacts poll is a bit of a moot point after the Broncos did not showcase an electric rushing attack against the Packers the way they had against the Falcons. And so it goes with the run game in Denver. One week up, next week down. While everything must be filtered with the fact that both were preseason games, and against different defenses, Jonah Coleman’s impressive NFL debut in the first preseason matchup averaging six yards a carry was fun to watch and definitely earned him a well-deserved “most impressive performance” vote from Broncos Country. While the most impressive performance for the Packers game is likely Bo Nix or Jaylen Waddle, the lack of a rushing attack is concerning. Preseason or not. Sean Payton is certainly concerned. “Obviously that wasn’t good enough. There weren’t a lot of things… I said this after the game—just pick a topic. Pick penalties, we lose there, kickoff, kickoff return, we lose that battle; rushing numbers, we lose that. We can’t just say, ‘Hey, this is preseason [game] two,’” Payton said after the loss. “Each phase saw their share of what ended up being the final score. So tomorrow we’ve got to be able to come in, coaches the same way, and look closely at what we’re doing and get the corrections made. You can’t not pay attention to these games, these scrimmages, these important steps towards the start of the regular season.” And certainly Payton wasn’t happy with the rushing totals, especially as they led to a lot of third-and-longs. “Yes, it wasn’t good. It wasn’t good. We’ll look at the tape, but we had too many minus plays, too many penalties offensively,” he added. “I don’t know how many third-and-10 or more we had, but quite a bit, right?” So, Broncos Country, does this preseason result mean much when evaluating the run game this season? title: Maybe the Broncos losing to the Packers is exactly what they needed
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Obviously, what the Denver Broncos put forth on Friday night was not good enough. Maybe that’s a good thing, especially for a team that has expectations of playing in and winning the Super Bowl this season. Yes, it’s the preseason, and you don’t want to get carried away with the positive […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on in the first half of a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Obviously, what the Denver Broncos put forth on Friday night was not good enough. Maybe that’s a good thing, especially for a team that has expectations of playing in and winning the Super Bowl this season. Yes, it’s the preseason, and you don’t want to get carried away with the positive or negative. But you also want to create good habits and trends heading into the regular season. At the same point, having areas to improve or sharpen is never a bad thing. The Broncos have one more week of practice and the third preseason game to do just that. Then the real fun begins. From penalties and special teams play to the line of scrimmage and just playing and looking sloppy against the Green Bay Packers, there’s no doubt Sean Payton will expect better and more. “Well, I think they won a lot of the battles,” Payton said to the media after Friday’s game. “You can take the line of scrimmage, you can take the kick coverage, they’ve got a big return. Penalties that impacted field position a lot, rushing battle, pick a topic. I would say yes. … But I can’t think of one area that we played or outplayed them, honestly. I’m just being honest.” Setting a standard and ensuring everyone is aligned to consistently live up to that is one of the reasons the Broncos are where they are. And it starts with Payton creating that culture. When that doesn’t happen, even in the preseason, it’s a moment to grow. “I wouldn’t necessarily say ‘bothered,’” Broncos cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian said to the media. “We’ve just got to bring that same mentality each week. It can’t be one-offs or different weeks, or ‘we don’t feel like playing,’ or ‘we’re not doing what we’re supposed to do.’ So, I think that’s the thing. You’ve just got to bring it every week and come with that mindset.” Having those times to learn, refocus, and be reminded of the expectations is never a bad thing. And you’d much rather have them come in the preseason. “Obviously, we’re not where we (want to be),” McMillian said to the media. “It’s preseason, so we can’t get too far down, but that’s not our ball. That’s not our type of ball. That’s not what we want to be like, so we’re just going to watch the film, review, and have a better week next week.” Broncos links

title: Lions DT Skyler Gill-Howard is clicking but still not happy with 1 part of his game
summary: If you look at any standouts, stock-ups, or winners from the Detroit Lions’ preseason win over the Washington Commanders, that list is almost certainly going to have rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard. While he didn’t show up much on the box score—one tackle for loss and one QB hit—he was clearly disruptive to anyone who […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-AUGUST 22: Detroit Lions defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard (50) lines up during the second half of an NFL preseason football game between the Washington Commanders and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images If you look at any standouts , stock-ups , or winners from the Detroit Lions’ preseason win over the Washington Commanders, that list is almost certainly going to have rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard. While he didn’t show up much on the box score—one tackle for loss and one QB hit—he was clearly disruptive to anyone who was watching even moderately closely. That’s reflected a little better in his overall PFF score (80.8), which was the highest of any Lions defender who logged at least 20 snaps Saturday afternoon . Gill-Howard was drafted by the Lions in April to bring some pass-rushing juice to the interior of the defensive line, and that’s exactly what he did against the Commanders. He continues to flash, and it’s earned him a nickname from coach Dan Campbell. “‘Sun Bleach’ just continues to make plays,” Campbell said. “He does it in practice. You can feel him out there. He just is relentless, and he plays snap-to-whistle, and he’s all out.” Gill-Howard admits things are starting to click after a slow start to camp. Remember that he’s not just making the jump to the NFL; he’s also playing for the first time since suffering a season-ending injury last October with Texas Tech. “I can feel things really click. I’m starting to react right quick, just getting used to the NFL,” Gill-Howard said after Saturday’s game. But getting to the quarterback is not enough to make it full-time in this league, and being a one-trick pony is not a way to get playing time in Detroit. The coaching staff demands balance from their defensive linemen, and that means being able to stop the run. That’s where Gill-Howard actually believes he took a step back against the Commanders, despite getting more early-down reps in the first half. “Obviously I can move around guys, but in the run where it gets gritty, I have to be better. Today wasn’t the best in the run game, but I didn’t allow too much,” Gill-Howard said. One thing working against the rookie defensive tackle is his size. At just 6-foot, 280 pounds, offensive linemen can sometimes outweigh him by 40-50 pounds. In college, he utilized his quick first step and athleticism to get around blocks, but in Detroit’s scheme, they don’t want players shooting gaps, as it could jeopardize gap integrity for the entire unit. “I was just trying to shoot gaps,” Gill-Howard admitted. “We don’t play an attack front here. They’re going to talk to me about that when we watch film tomorrow. I be trying to shoot gaps, but I’ve got to play with my hands better.” Ironically, Gill-Howard’s best play of the game came in the run game. He shot into the backfield and took down Commanders running back Kayton Allen for a 3-yard loss. Skyler Gill-Howard showed flashes vs the Commanders. Physical and quick penetrator pic.twitter.com/yJSdQYqDF9 — Billy M (@BillyM_91) August 23, 2026 While this is another example of him shooting the gaps, he credited his film study for this play. “I knew exactly what they were running, if I’m being honest,” Gill-Howard said. “We talked about that a lot during our little film session yesterday—well, the whole week, really. The guard, he left that a-gap wide open, so I know he’s trying not to get beat in there. So I know I’m fast enough to just shoot it off the backside. That was my job on that play; I knew exactly what they were running.” The run game may be a work in progress, but Gill-Howard’s quickest route to playing time is as a situational pass rusher. And by all accounts, he’s putting in the work, effort, and production to find his way onto the field early in the 2026 season. “He knows who he is and he knows how he has to play,” Campbell said. “And he plays with pride in everything, and he’s crafty, he’s explosive, and he’s violent.”
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit Lions stock report: Risers, fallers at every position vs. Commanders
summary: The Detroit Lions’ second preseason game of the 2026 season is in the books, and it’s time to check in on the players who helped or hurt their stock against the Washington Commanders. Attendance The Lions rested 17 players (including 10 starters), along with three others on injury lists (PUP/NFI). Let’s take a quick look at the […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-AUGUST 22: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jackson Meeks (13) lines up before a play during the second half of an NFL preseason football game between the Washington Commanders and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ second preseason game of the 2026 season is in the books, and it’s time to check in on the players who helped or hurt their stock against the Washington Commanders. Attendance The Lions rested 17 players (including 10 starters), along with three others on injury lists (PUP/NFI). Let’s take a quick look at the roster with our game-day depth chart , noting that the players without a position color did not play in this game. Additionally, if a player’s name is written in red, they came into the game injured; if they were injured during the game, their name is boxed in black. Quarterback Stock neutral: Josh Dobbs, Luke Altmyer Did not play: Jared Goff It was a bit of a mixed showing from the reserves on Saturday, with both quarterbacks flashing promise, while also making some glaring mistakes. Dobbs got the start and turned the ball over on the first two drives, but ran a 50-yard read-option touchdown on drive three and settled in after that. Altmyer was sacked three times on his opening drive, but he settled in once the Lions established their rushing attack. Overall, in a game meant to separate the two, the QB2 job looks unsettled, with neither seizing the opportunity. Running back Stock up: Jacob Saylors, Trayveon Williams, Raheem Blackshear Did not play: Jahmyr Gibbs Injured: Isiah Pacheco (MCL sprain), Sione Vaki (back spasms) Game injury: Jabari Small (concussion) Saylors got the start and likely remains in the lead for the RB4 job, but after a terrific show by every reserve running back, he has some real competition for the job. Saylors is a steady runner who can put power behind his pads, find the daylight in the defensive line, and has the balance to cut back against the grain. Small entered this game as Saylors’ biggest challenger, displaying power and quickness, but he unfortunately suffered a concussion on his sixth snap and was forced from the game. With only a week before cutdown, it’s a tough time for an injury. Williams was arguably the most impressive runner on Saturday, displaying wiggle, burst, decisiveness, and vision. He not only ran 10 times for 36 yards and a touchdown , but also caught a screen pass and took it for 24 yards . In all, Williams managed to outrush the entire Washington offense by himself. Blackshear had the lowest production output of the backs (2.6 yards per carry), but some of that can be attributed to the situation he found himself in: being asked to run into a loaded box when the Commanders’ defense knew it was a run. Three straight runs gained a total of eight yards, and on fourth-and-two, he got what they needed to run out the clock. Wide receiver Stock up: Lucky Jackson, Tay Martin Stock neutral: Isaac TeSlaa, Greg Dortch, Tom Kennedy, Malik Cunningham Stock down: Dominic Lovett, Tarik Black Did not play: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams Game injury: Cedrick Wilson (knee) With the Lions’ running game cooking, it was a quiet night for the receivers: only Cedric Wilson and Lucky Jackson caught more than one pass (two each), and Wilson was tied for third in receiving yards (21); Jackson was fifth (15). Martin, Kennedy, and Cunningham each caught one pass for double-digit yardage; solid but average production. Lovett, who had a chance to separate himself with a good game, caught just one pass for six yards in a disappointing outing, while Black couldn’t manage a catch, despite entering the game in the second quarter and playing into the fourth quarter. Martin remains the most fascinating reserve receiver in my eyes. Yes, he dropped a critical third-down pass, but he was also a catalyst in springing Dobbs 50-yard touchdown run by executing a key block. He also started this game, played more snaps than any wide receiver, and contributed on special teams. Tight end Stock up: Jackson Meeks Stock neutral: Brock Wright, Tyler Conklin Stock down: Thomas Gordon, Zach Horton Injured: Sam LaPorta (hip) It was the Jackson Meeks show on Saturday, as the tight end convert put his receiving skills on display, leading the team in receptions (4) and receiving yards (33), and was tied for the most snaps among the tight ends. But beyond the stats, he made plays when it mattered, converting a fourth down with an adapted route and reception , then forced a fumble late in the game with a wonderful special teams tackle . “It does feel like home,” Meeks said of adjusting to tight end. “I’m loving tight end. I think I am loving the challenge more than—I love football—but I am loving the challenge because I am learning a whole new part of football.” Conklin looked like a steady veteran on Saturday, displaying why he is likely locked in as TE3. While he did get beat for a sack on a push-pull from an edge rusher, the rest of the game he was solid. He sealed the other half of the hole on the Dobbs touchdown run, wiping out Commanders first-round pick Sonny Styles on the play, and caught two passes for 21 yards, including a third-down conversion . Gordon and Horton appear to be falling out of the TE4 competition. Gordon tied Meeks for the most snaps by a tight end in this game, but while Meeks was stellar, Gordon was not targeted. Meanwhile, Horton was the last tight end to find the field (in the third quarter) and also failed to register a target. Offensive line Stock up: Tate Ratledge, Blake Miller*, Miles Frazier, Mason Miller Stock neutral: Larry Borom, Christian Mahogany, Juice Scruggs, Devin Cochran Stock down: Seth McLaughlin, Melvin Priestly*, Colby Sorsdal Did not play: Penei Sewell Injured: Cade Mays (wrist), Ben Bartch (concussion), Giovanni Manu (NFI) Game injury: C Michael Niese (leg) I want to reiterate how difficult it is to grade offensive line play live, and remind folks that perspectives often change more with this group than any other once you can watch the game replay. That said, my initial positive looks mostly came from players’ run-game performances and clear wins in pass protection, while my negative grades went to those making obvious mistakes. Ratledge and Blake Miller looked like they had great communication and left me with encouragement that they’ll be in a good spot for the regular season, while Frazier and Mason Miller were people movers in the run game in the second half. McLaughlin had two false start penalties in a row (yes, the first was credited to Frazier, but the entire line moved except McLaughlin, meaning he didn’t snap the ball on time) and then got bull-rushed over a few plays later. I thought he was great at getting interior push in the run game, but the mistakes were too big to offset the positives. I still believe he has a great shot to make the roster, but I’m not sold that he can beat out Scruggs for the starting role. Defensive tackle Stock up: Skyler Gill-Howard*, Levi Onwuzurike, Ben Stille Stock neutral: Tyleik Williams, Chris Smith, Mekhi Wingo Stock down: Myles Adams, Tyre West* Did not play: Alim McNeill Gill-Howard continues to shine with his ability to generate interior pass rush, registering as many as five plays in which I thought he might get credit for forcing a quarterback pressure. In the locker room post-game, he was self-critical of his run defense; he did execute a beautiful tackle for loss. Onwuzurike’s power and positional versatility were on display in this game as he started at the 3-technique, but ranged out to the 5-technique at times, causing problems for the offensive line . After a slow start to camp, he is settling into the two-deep rotation. Stille continues to climb the depth chart and entered this game as NT2 behind Tyleik Williams, but ended up rotating the role with Chris Smith. But Stille wasn’t limited…
