title: Rams Depth Chart Reset: Jarquez Hunter makes his move
summary: With a short week looming before the L.A. Rams’ preseason finale on Thursday, second-year back Jarquez Hunter staked his claim to leapfrog Ronnie Rivers as the team’s third-string runner. Hunter ran for 68 yards at 5.7 per carry against the Saints on Saturday, showing off the burst, speed, and power that made him a top […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - Aug. 22, 2026: Los Angeles Rams running back Jarquez Hunter #27 runs the football against the New Orleans Saints in an NFL preseason game at SoFi Stadium on Saturday, Aug. 22, 2026. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) With a short week looming before the L.A. Rams’ preseason finale on Thursday, second-year back Jarquez Hunter staked his claim to leapfrog Ronnie Rivers as the team’s third-string runner. Hunter ran for 68 yards at 5.7 per carry against the Saints on Saturday , showing off the burst, speed, and power that made him a top running back in college and the team’s fourth-round pick in 2025. For fans, Saturday’s 34-0 throttling of the New Orleans Saints was a joy to watch and the initial 53-man roster is becoming clearer. Last chance for a final post-game roster reset, so where do things stand en route to L.A.‘s final roster decisions? Saturday snap counts are in parentheses, along with some opinions as to who’s in and who’s out. Quarterback In: Matthew Stafford, Ty Simpson (28), Stetson Bennett (51) Out: Matthew Caldwell It was Bennett’s turn for the limelight in Week 2. Four scores in five possessions is stellar efficiency. Again, like Week 1, his accuracy appears a bit off. One noticeable thing that is that his passing precision is better between the the numbers, on in-breaking routes and to settled receivers. When throwing outside or leading his receivers, his ball appears to float and sail. Did a nice job of making plays with his feet. Simpson didn’t play badly, just not sterling, as he did in Week 1. Running back In: Kyren Williams, Blake Corum Likely: Jarquez Hunter (40), Ronnie Rivers Out: Dean Conners (6), Jordan Waters (33) If last year is any indication, then Rivers not playing does not assure him either the RB#3 or #4 roles and the accompanying roster spot. He played just three snaps last year and did not make the opening 53. Hunter really showed off his traits, a heady combination of power and speed. Waters stacked another good performance. Just like in the 2025 preseason, he’s showing a competitive north/south running style. Conners didn’t get a lot of work, hard to put a finger as why, but the Rams only got off 26 offensive plays in the second half. Jarquez Hunter showcases the moves and finds the end zone 🙌 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EV1dfSKAIP — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Wide receiver In: Puka Nacua, Davante Adans, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpford Likely: Xavier Smith Still alive: CJ Daniels (38), Brennan Presley (59), Tyler Scott (37) Out: Tru Edwards (37), Alex Bachman (42) The battle appears now to be for one roster spot with Smith sitting out after a solid Week 1. I don’t think there is any wrong answer for WR#6 amongst the still alive candidates. It boils down to a fans personal preference. They all looked pretty sharp on Sunday. Tight end In: Colby Parkinson, Terrance Ferguson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, Max Klare (48) Out: Mark Redman (22), Dan Villari (27), Rohan Jones (6) Overall, It was a quiet afternoon for the unit. Short routes were the rule of the day. This unit has been pretty much set since the beginning of camp, but it was nice to see Villari show off his athleticism on the one catch. Offensive line In: Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, David Quessenberry Likely: Keagan Trost, Beaux Limmer, Justin Dedich Still alive: Dylan McMahon (28), Austin Blaske (79), Bill Murray (74), Garrett Bowles (79) Out: AJ Arcuri (52), Blake Hance (58), Bryce Henderson (25) A solid outing for the big guys up front, particularly the interior players.They consistently pushed the line of scrimmage back in the run game and allotted the L.A. quarterbacks all the time they needed in the pass game. McMahon started at center for the second straight game, and handled the pivot well. He subbed out in the middle of the second quarter vs the Saints, after playing nearly the full game in Week 1. He hasn’t been able to make the opening roster in either of his first two pro seasons Both Blaske and Bowles played every snap and stood out. Blaske played on both sides at tackle, looking comfortable at each. He was flagged for a holding call, but it looked like he was driving the defender to the ground three yards past the line of scrimmage. Bowles worked at at guard and at center. Just liked last year, he has proven he can compete and win in both pass and run blocking against preseason competition. Murray has stacked two solid games at left guard. He’s an interesting character, he was an undrafted defensive lineman for his first two NFL seasons and switched over in the summer of 2022. He’s made stops with four different teams. Hance played better than Week 1, but doesn’t appear up to grade. Arcuri got a good workout after sitting out the first game, likely too little, too late. Henderson again played late in the game, probably wouldn’t be guy to develop on the practice squad. Special teams In: Harrison Meevis (12), Ethan Evans (8), Joe Cardona (8) No news is good news for the specialists. Kick coverage was still iffy, but incrementally improved. I have to admit, I was disappointed seeing Alex Bachman back to return punts early in the game, after just four days on the team. Nothing against him, just seems the reps would be better served on someone who had put in the work for the whole of training camp and had a chance to make the team. Defensive line In: Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis Likely: Ty Hamilton Still alive: Tim Keenan (25), Bill Norton (30) Out: Larrell Murchison (23), Payton Zdroik (30), Jaxson Moi (34) L.A. used predominantly four-man fronts vs the Saints. The overall quality of play was up from Week 1, but the level of competition was down. Hamilton didn’t play and looks like he’ll hold on to DL#5. A nice position battle between Keenan and Norton, two big boys. Today, I would grade the edge to Norton by a shade. Murchison looks to have lost a step, while Zdroik and Moi are getting valuable work in a practice squad battle. Edge In: Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart Likely: Desjuan Johnson Still alive: Wesley Bailey (48) Out: Keir Thomas (14), Darryl Peterson (37), Tomon Fox (28) It’s not surprising Johnson didn’t play, he was almost a sure lock. Although sloppy in Week 1, he’s proven to be of rotational grade when it counts. It’s clear that Bailey grew from Game 1 and plays with confidence and speed. He’s still a long shot for him to make the roster, but it’s fair to say he got buildable traits. Thomas hasn’t really met expectations thus far in preseason work and depending on the severity of his groin injury, may have seen his last action in horns. Peterson and Fox lag behind. Off-ball linebacker In: Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, Grant Stuard Out: Nikhai Hill-Green (55), Elias Neal (26), Daniel Rickert (10), Monty Rice (32) No movement based on the Saints game. It was gong to be tough to knock off any of the incumbents. Hill-Green appears a bit tentative and not reacting quick enough to what he is seeing, a lot of rookies do it. Neal showed burst to the ball, but awaits the same fate. Rickert is a hustler, good guy for the practice squad. . Safety I n: Camren Curl, Quentin Lake, Kamren Kinchens, Jaylen McCollough Still alive: Nick Anderson (39), Nate Valcarcel (40) Out: Tanner Ingle (32), Alex Cook (41) Generally, the Rams used two-high in passing situations and one-high when a run was expected. The Saints didn’t or couldn’t get deeper than the short range, as such, the safeties didn’t get a lot of chances to shine. Can’t make a case for any one them to make any real progress based on this game. I would, however, mark off Tanner Ingle and Alex Cook. Cornerback In: Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace Still alive: Cam Lampkin (63), Al’Zillion Hamilton (57) Out: Nyzier Fourqurean (32), Alex Johnson (41), Zech McPhearson (0) Good outing for the corners, Lampkin and Hamilton are…
author: Venie Randy Soares

title: PFF Grades: The Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson role reversal
summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback battle burned hotter headed into Week 2 of the NFL preseason. After leading just two possessions in the opening game, Stetson Bennett was active for the entire first half. LA was likely being honest about the fact that rookie Ty Simpson is gaining ground on the veteran and wanted […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates his touchdown with Max Klare #86, to take a 17-0 lead over the New Orleans Saints, during the first half in a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback battle burned hotter headed into Week 2 of the NFL preseason. After leading just two possessions in the opening game, Stetson Bennett was active for the entire first half. LA was likely being honest about the fact that rookie Ty Simpson is gaining ground on the veteran and wanted to give them an equal amount of playing time. Instead, Bennett inspired the Rams to a first-half blowout that then—because of game script—limited Simpson’s opportunities. Bennett performed so well on Saturday that he unintentionally undercut the rookie. There are plenty of other take aways from Saturday’s game against the New Orleans Saints. Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades and data are a good way to match objective data to first impressions. Who made a positive impression ahead of the fast-approaching cutdown to the 53-man roster? Top five grades on offense: 1 – Bill Murray, LG: 92.3 2 – Stetson Bennett, QB: 81.1 Bennett was the lowest-graded player on the entire Rams offense last week . He swapped places with Ty Simpson—who made the top five) and Simpson fell to third from the bottom against the Saints. The veteran QB pushed the ball down the field more aggressively after appearing very conservative in the opener. He had an average depth of target (ADOT) of 9.9 yards. Bennett still finished with an impressive 69.0% adjusted completion rate and manufactured two big-time throws without a turnover-worthy play. Meanwhile, Simpson has been deadly accurate in his first two games. After posting an adjusted completion rate in the 90’s last week, he earned a mark of 75.0% in his encore. This throw from Stetson Bennett is crazy. Need the tv copy of McVay reacting pic.twitter.com/J1H9l8WlqW — Sam Schwartzstein (@schwartzsteins) August 23, 2026 3 – Dylan McMahon, C: 77.7 4(t) – Tru Edwards, WR: 74.4 4(t) – CJ Daniels, WR: 74.4 Edwards was a standout performer in last year’s preseason and was quiet in the opener. He was targeted four times in this game and hauled in three catches for 27 yards. At 6-3, 201 lbs., he brings a size element that other Rams reserve receivers don’t offer. Rookie CJ Daniels was the focal point of LA’s passing game. He led the team in targets on a two-fold basis with 13. The next closest was Brennan Presley at six. Daniels caught eight passes for 68 yards, of which 17 came after the catch. He’s known for his contested catch ability, but this didn’t show up on Saturday. On four contested targets, he caught only one attempt. CJ Daniels with a very nice win on the deep out despite the CB aligning in off cov with outside leverage. Stetson Bennett with some excellent anticipation also. pic.twitter.com/FMk5qnYmiK — Brett Whitefield (@BGWhitefield) August 23, 2026 Other notes on offense: The reserve offensive line had another strong performance in this game. Let’s take their summary together. Murray clearly led the way and led the line in both pass protection and run game grades. He played 73 of 78 snaps. Austin Blaske, who played RG and RT, was the only lineman to take every offensive snap. Blaske was a standout last week and put together another positive game, although not to the level we saw in his first game. He’s someone to keep an eye on for either the roster or practice squad. AJ Arcuri played in this game after sitting out the opener. He finished second on the offensive line and was just outside the overall top five. Arcuri played 46 snaps at LT and five at LG. He earned an impressive pass protection mark of 85.1. The only lineman that didn’t perform well in PFF’s grades was Bryce Henderson, who played 25 snaps split evenly between LT and RT. He finished with a grade of 54.3. Top five grades on defense: 1 – Alex Cook, DB: 91.3 Cook drew the media attention from the game because of his 100-yard pick-six. While he should be applauded for making a big play, it was a very curious decision by quarterback Spencer Rattler. It will be tough to crack the roster at safety unless he can standout on special teams. ALEX COOK COOKED UP A PICK-6 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZxGmBC0S1b — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 2 – Wesley Bailey, EDGE: 90.2 Leading the team with 10 (!) pressures, Bailey was a disruptive force on the defensive line. The box score will reflect only a single sack. He hit the opposing quarterback three times. Bailey also fared well in run defense with a grade of 79.4. Worth noting: Desjuan Johnson did not play in this game after being on the field deep into the fourth quarter last week. Bailey is probably a practice squad candidate barring a surprise. Wesley Bailey gets to the QB 😤 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/UrUy0EOL9I pic.twitter.com/0AfB2CvOoT — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 22, 2026 3 – Nyzier Fourqurean, CB: 89.9 Fourqurean cracked the top five despite a tackling grade of just 25.8. He missed two tackles on five attempts and was targeted three times to allow two receptions for 41 yards (all YAC). 4 – Monty Rice, LB: 83.9 Faring well in both run defense (76.6) and coverage (70.6), Rice was Saturday’s standout performer at linebacker. There may not be much opportunity for reserves to make the team since we know Omar Speights and Shaun Dolac are both likely safe. The Rams have a knack for developing unheralded linebackers, and Rice may be the next in the pipeline. 5 – Al’zillion Hamilton, CB: 74.6 The Saints went after Hamilton often, and the corner made them pay for it. Hamilton was targeted a team-leading eight times and he allowed just four receptions for 30 yards and recorded an interception. This was good for a passer rating of just 19.8. 55 of his 57 snaps came on the outside. Al’zillion Hamilton with the interception for the @RamsNFL 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SQSlo7Y6Vz — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Other notes on defense: Rookie Tim Keenan has struggled over the last two games. He was the lowest-graded player on defense. The Rams have plenty of depth on the interior defensive line, so it wouldn’t be surprising if they attempt to stash Keenan on the practice squad for a redshirt first year.
author: JB Scott

title: No team wants to trade for Stetson Bennett
summary: Stetson Bennett’s ideal place with the L.A Rams would be on the practice squad, and despite the belief by most that he was too good in Saturday’s preseason game to cut him, the quarterback may actually less likely to make the 53-man roster based on how he played against the Saints. A deeper look at […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams passes the ball during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Stetson Bennett’s ideal place with the L.A Rams would be on the practice squad, and despite the belief by most that he was too good in Saturday’s preseason game to cut him , the quarterback may actually less likely to make the 53-man roster based on how he played against the Saints. A deeper look at his already-average passing statistics in the second preseason game show a quarterback who: Can’t consistently throw an accurate pass beyond 15 yards Had the majority of his completions on short, routine passes Sailed way too many balls over the heads of his intended receivers Relies too heavily on shotgun formation and play-action designs meant for rookies like Ty Simpson Still lacks the size, arm strength, and ball placement to be an NFL quarterback No matter what you hear this week, nothing that Bennett has done in the preseason disproves that he’s the reason that the Rams drafted Simpson. Les Snead felt that L.A. needed a potential franchise starter, so he drafted Simpson knowing that it wasn’t going to be the 28 (soon to be 29) year old Bennett with zero career NFL games under his belt. Not zero passes. Not zero snaps. Bennett has never been active for an NFL game. But after rushing for two touchdowns (and wildly over-throwing several opportunities to pass for at least one), the narrative on Bennett has shifted dramatically just one week after the same people were saying that Simpson should be kicking him to the curb without passing Go. I think Ty Simpson is a fine prospect but Stetson Bennett could’ve been the Rams QB 2 for a couple more years. He actually reminds me of Brock Purdy – just a little bit more athletic but slightly smaller. — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) August 22, 2026 However, as you’ll see in this passing chart I created by watching the first half of the Rams-Saints game again, it’s not just the Rams who won’t have a place for Bennett: Nobody in the NFL cares. If he’s cut, it’s almost certain that Stetson Bennett would clear waivers. The @AtlantaFalcons should try and trade a late pick for Stetson Bennett — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) August 23, 2026 Where would he go? There’s not 32 quarterbacks in the league better than Stetson Bennett pic.twitter.com/JeI12gWNNP — Memes (@PardonMyMeme) August 22, 2026 First of all, there are definitely more than 32 quarterbacks better than Bennett. There are at least 50 . Using that as a caption for a highlight of Bennett turning down potential passing opportunities to run around the Saints’ second/third-string defense for a rushing touchdown is not a logical 1:1. Where would he go if he was cut? Nobody else in the NFC West wants him: Seahawks, 49ers, Cardinals all have 3 QBs they’re keeping Other McVay tree coaches are set with QBs: Packers, Vikings, Bengals wouldn’t be interested You’re talking about maybe at most the Jaguars with Liam Coen, if they decide that Bennett offers them more than Nick Mullens. But…why? Mullens isn’t good, but he’s been with Coen since last season, there’s nothing left to teach him, he’s familiar with how to help Trevor Lawrence week to week, it’s unlikely that a team is interested in disrupting the room at this point of the year unless they have to, like an injury happens. Besides, Coen doesn’t know Bennett. They never overlapped in L.A.. And it’s like that on most teams. They’ve been developing quarterbacks already, and they also see that Bennett doesn’t have a future as an NFL starter. He’d just be what he is on the Rams right now, which is a third-string QB. He’s a third-string quarterback who might get the backup job out of necessity. Instead, the Rams could — and probably should — risk cutting Bennett, clearing waivers, and putting him on the practice squad. The team would keep two quarterbacks, but in the event that Stafford got injured, sign Jimmy Garoppolo. That’s the most logical plan. Because pass-to-pass on Saturday, Stetson Bennett was more bad than good . And the “good” was not NFL-level good. It was just “preseason good enough”. No, I’m not former NFL zero-pass attempts quarterbacks Kurt Benkert (I’m being snarky, but I acknowledge he generally knows more than I do) but I’m also not motivated to lie to you. There’s no clickbait here. It’s simply an acknowledgement of what really happened in front of our eyes, not narratives, stats, and a single highlight that keeps getting passed around. A year ago this week, Bennett passed for over 300 yards and three touchdowns against the Chargers. I promise you, he’s not any better now than he was the last three years as a quarterback no team wanted that badly. Stetson Bennett passing chart vs Saints Notes: Play Action or Shotgun? I’ll keep track First-Read is my opinion , but a first-read is easy to diagnose Second-Read is a little trickier, but not really “Routine” is my opinion too, but I think we’d agree 95% of the time what is routine Somewhere along the line I missed a pass because I charted 30 out of 31 Watch the Game Highlights yourself Watch Bennett’s Highlights Pass 1 – Routine pass, LOS to Presley 9 YAC (Play Action) Pass 2 – High sideline pass to Daniels (Shotgun) incomplete * (1st read) *could be complete Very close but did look like a clean catch by CJ Daniels to me pic.twitter.com/V6HnwTu80N — Billy M (@BillyM_91) August 22, 2026 On the Daniels pass, let’s call it a serviceable pass that works, but not good enough ball placement to give Daniels a better shot of keeping his feet on the ground to catch it. Roughly 20 air yards. Pass 3 – Routine pass, 7 yards to Presley (Shotgun) (2nd read) Pass 4 – Presnap motion by TE Klare, Routine 1st-read pass to Klare 3 yards (Shotgun) Pass 5 – Under Center: Almost runs into RB, deep shot overthrow to Scott (1st read) On pass 5, Bennett is under center and it appears that he’s supposed to run play action, but miscommunication with running back almost causes him to run into Jarquez Hunter on accident and disrupt the play. Basically it looks like it’s 25% play action Pass 6 – Routine pass, 4 yards to Bachman (Shotgun) (2nd read) Pass 7 – Routine pass, 5 yards to Daniels on 3rd-and-6 (Shotgun) (1st read) Pass 8 – High difficulty pass, 20 yards to Scott (Play Action) (2nd-ish read?) Stetson Bennett is better than Ty Simpson I don’t care. #GoDawgs pic.twitter.com/eFxKrUcPuN — Top Tier Georgia (@TopTierUGA) August 22, 2026 This is the throw that people are talking about the most. It’s 4th-and-1 because the previous play did not go past the sticks, and Bennett is throwing under pressure of two Saints. He appears to turn down at least one receiver (Daniels in the middle of the field perhaps) if not two, prior to then throwing this one over the top to Scott. That’s good. What’s not so clear is why he turns down a wide open Jarquez Hunter standing six yards away from him and putting up the mailbox sign “I’m Open! I’m Open!” It could be that Bennett is not tall enough. It could be that Bennett didn’t see him. It could be the defender standing in between the two players. These are all good answers. It doesn’t change the fact that IF Bennett is able to see Hunter or IF he’s tall enough or IF he can throw the ball over the defender here, it’s so obviously the pass he has to make. It’s fourth down and Hunter is going to walk to the sticks if Bennett sees him. Instead he takes the shot with a far lower percentage of success and nearly overthrows it. And this other angle, which people are using to say that the pass was impressive, actually makes the decision look even worse relative to Bennett’s open receivers in the middle of the field: This throw from Stetson Bennett is crazy. Need the tv copy of McVay reacting pic.twitter.com/J1H9l8WlqW — Sam Schwartzstein…

title: Stetson Bennett or Ty Simpson: A case for each player as QB2
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have their starting quarterback for the regular season with 2025 NFL MVP Matthew Stafford set to return for his 18th season. But the team faces some decisions regarding the backup quarterback position after investing a 2026 1st round draft pick in Ty Simpson. The team still has Stetson Bennett on the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have their starting quarterback for the regular season with 2025 NFL MVP Matthew Stafford set to return for his 18th season. But the team faces some decisions regarding the backup quarterback position after investing a 2026 1st round draft pick in Ty Simpson. The team still has Stetson Bennett on the roster, a 4th round draft choice in the 2023 NFL Draft. Neither Simpson or Bennett has regular season experience; leaving a lot of fans wondering who is the best option if Matthew Stafford were to get injured. Well, after training camp and two preseason games, the job is still a very tight race… Rams QB preseason stats… Stetson Bennett: 23/37 (62.2%), 219 yds, 5.9 YPA, 2 total TDs, 78.5 passer rating, 69.2 PFF Grade Ty Simpson: 29/37 (78.4%), 263 yds, 7.1 YPA, 2 TDs, 114. 3 passer rating, 65.8 PFF Grade Through two games, it is VERY close. — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 23, 2026 Stetson Bennett’s Case: Stetson Bennett is the “incumbent”. Going into training camp, he was QB2 purely because of his familiarity with Sean McVay’s system and playbook. Bennett had a solid 2025 NFL preseason but was still stuck behind Jimmy Garoppolo on the depth chart. Now, Bennett is being tested to see if he is a viable option. Bennett’s four seasons in Sean McVay’s system give him a significant advantage in understanding the terminology, protections, timing and expectations of the offense. The Rams have already invested years in developing him, and that experience matters if Matthew Stafford is forced to miss time. One other argument for Bennett is that he has been exposed to more situations via joint practices and preseason action. Even though those experiences are not against an opposing defense’s best 11 players, being able to see coverages at the NFL carries weight that Ty Simpson has not quite been fully exposed to other than one training cmap. This throw from Stetson Bennett is crazy. Need the tv copy of McVay reacting pic.twitter.com/J1H9l8WlqW — Sam Schwartzstein (@schwartzsteins) August 23, 2026 Ty Simpson’s Case: Simpson’s case is pretty simple. He has more upside than Bennett. Simpson also brings physical tools and mobility that could give Sean McVay another dimension when plays break down. While Stetson Bennett has more experience in the Rams’ system, Simpson may have the higher ceiling. One of Simpson’s strong suits in his college film is his quick processing – a key staple for Sean McVay’s rhythm and timing offense. Is Simpson’s processing better than Bennett? It might be. It's subtle, but this is good eye manipulation from Ty Simpson. Gets the LB moving to the right with his eyes, which opens up the space for Connors. Simpson finds the Rams UDFA RB in the end zone an easy touchdown. pic.twitter.com/uBUkDLqZkN — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 16, 2026 Prediction: Bennett wins QB2 job Unless the Rams find a trade partner for Stetson Bennett, I believe he earns the QB2 job to start the regular season while still giving Ty Simpson a healthy amount of development in practices. If another team experiences an injury during the regular season, the Rams could dangle Stetson Bennett for a Day 3 pick. Les Snead loves a good 6th round draft choice.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams’ Good, Bad and Ugly: Ty Simpson played too little
summary: The Los Angeles Rams throttled the New Orleans Saints 34-0 on Saturday, and although it was encouraging to see Stetson Bennett lead the offense with such authority, it was equally disappointing that the coaching staff didn’t give more of those reps to Ty Simpson. Los Angeles has now won both their first two preseason matchups […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams prepares to pass the ball during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams throttled the New Orleans Saints 34-0 on Saturday , and although it was encouraging to see Stetson Bennett lead the offense with such authority, it was equally disappointing that the coaching staff didn’t give more of those reps to Ty Simpson. Los Angeles has now won both their first two preseason matchups with dominant showings on offense and defense. Imagine what the Battle for LA against the Chargers will bring on Thursday if this keeps up. Rather than get too ahead of ourselves, here’s the good, the bad and the ugly against the Saints in preseason Week 2. The Good Stetson Bennett shows his value to the NFL Stetson Bennett took a backseat to Ty Simpson against the Chiefs, as the rookie quarterback stole headlines for the majority of last week. Bennett earned most of the snaps this time around and wasn’t particularly great through the air. He completed only 19-of-31 passes and finished with a 77.5 passer rating. Average passing is more on-brand for Bennett. However, he didn’t turn the ball over and actually contributed on the ground. He rushed twice for nine yards and scored a touchdown both times, including an eight-yard scamper with just over two minutes left in the second quarter. Stetson Bennett IV had the home crowd on their feet for this @RamsNFL TD 💪 pic.twitter.com/BvGOkIMfEU — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) August 22, 2026 I’ve said all preseason that Bennett is fighting for his NFL future. This game might have secured him as Matthew Stafford’s backup this season. It was exactly the game he desperately needed to keep Simpson at a distance, as he proved he is still worth a damn in the league. Jarquez Hunter and CJ Daniels stepped it up A week after Dean Connors and Brennan Presley had good games while Jarquez Hunter and CJ Daniels were quiet, the opposite happened against the Saints. Initially, Connors looked as though he had put pressure on Hunter at running back behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. That didn’t happen, as Hunter rushed for a team-high 68 yards on 12 carries and a touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Jarquez Hunter so far today: 12 carries 68 rushing yards 1 TD pic.twitter.com/aHZ2NCPMh0 — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) August 22, 2026 Daniels finished with only 18 receiving yards in Kansas City, but ended Saturday’s game with 68 yards on eight receptions, both team highs. It was exactly the kind of game a player fighting for a roster spot and a chance to earn snaps alongside Puka Nacua and Davante Adams should have. This game proved again that the Rams have a wealth of young talent who can step up at any given time. While it’s undoubtedly a great problem to have entering the season, it would be better to see certain players maintain their standout performances for longer, more consistent stretches. Still, it was a jolly good show from both Hunter and Daniels, and here’s hoping it continues against the Chargers Thursday night. Defense continued to flex its muscles New Orleans didn’t stand a chance against this Rams defense. Last week, LA held the Chiefs without a touchdown, and this week, they held the Saints without points. Backups Spencer Rattler and Zach Wilson combined for 188 passing yards, two interceptions and a 49.2 passer rating. Rattler threw a 100-yard pick-six to Rams’ safety Alex Cook with 9:06 remaining in the third quarter. ALEX COOK GOES THE LENGTH OF THE FIELD 🤯 He ran a total distance of 118.38 yards on this pick-6, per @NextGenStats 💨 Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zk3JGARYiq — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) August 22, 2026 In total, the Saints had three turnovers and ended the game 0-for-2 in the red zone. New Orleans also finished with 105 rushing yards, but no player had more than 22 yards. It was simply one of those games where the Rams clicked on all cylinders and could do no wrong. The team’s defensive depth has been on display through the first two weeks of preseason. So if this is how the backups play, imagine how the starters will fare when they take the field. The Bad Coaching staff’s plan for Ty Simpson Having Bennett take the majority of the snaps under center would’ve been great if the Rams’ coaching staff was trying to figure out who he is. Well, they should already know he’s a wildly inconsistent quarterback who is not part of the team’s long-term future. Simpson clearly is, which is why it made zero sense to play him for as little as he did Saturday. The rookie had just 12 pass attempts, completing eight for 73 yards with zero touchdowns or turnovers. He has stood out from the pack compared to his fellow first-year quarterbacks. Ty Simpson continues to impress this preseason. The Rams rookie went 8/12 for 73 yards in Saturday's 34-0 win over the Saints. Simpson has been mistake free through two preseason games, completing 29/37 passes for 263 yards and 2 TDs. Sean McVay praised his efficiency in the… pic.twitter.com/kT5RlNl8dA — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) August 23, 2026 Regardless of his preseason performance or whether Simpson isn’t named the team’s QB2 ahead of the season, that isn’t the point. The coaching staff whiffed on the opportunity to play him for longer. Of course you don’t want your rookie quarterback airing it out late in a blowout preseason game, but it would’ve been great to see him get more experience. It wouldn’t have hurt. This preseason is about figuring out what the Rams have in Simpson, not about realizing the team is basically settled with Bennett at the backup spot instead of upgrading when they had the chance. Several youngsters failed to capitalize on standout first games A few of the standout performers from the preseason opener against the Chiefs were quiet in this one. Presley and Connors, though, were the most disappointing to see have minimal impact. Presley had a chance to bring competition and depth at WR3 behind Nacua and Adams. Instead, Daniels edged him out this week, and he finished with four receptions for 35 yards. That’s not bad, but not what you want to see from a player facing an uphill climb to make the roster. Connors had just five rushing yards on two attempts, and no receptions a week after having two touchdown catches. A second straight good day on the ground would’ve put the pressure on Hunter to have a good game. Hunter having a great game combined with Connors being quiet might’ve spelled doom for his chances of landing on the roster. The pressure will be on in the preseason finale. However, by then, it might be too late if they don’t play any better. The Ugly None this week. The Rams had a strong showing all around. It’s also pretty difficult to find something ugly after a shutout win.
author: Evan Craig

title: Who hasn’t played in Rams preseason?
summary: Under Sean McVay, Los Angeles Rams have a very clear agenda with how to use the preseason, which is to rest most of the players who will make the final 53-man roster and to play the guys who won’t. With some exceptions this year, like giving Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson reps at quarterback, that’s […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 17: Blake Corum #22, Kyren Williams #23, and Ronnie Rivers #20 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrate following the win against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on November 17, 2024 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Under Sean McVay, Los Angeles Rams have a very clear agenda with how to use the preseason, which is to rest most of the players who will make the final 53-man roster and to play the guys who won’t. With some exceptions this year, like giving Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson reps at quarterback, that’s exactly what McVay is doing again and some of the guys who are resting won’t make some fans happy to hear. Players like Ronnie Rivers, Xavier Smith, and out of the blue, Zech McPhearson. If these numbers are any indication, then 37 players on the Rams have sat out both games in entirety, whereas another five were given a break in Week 2 against the Saints, seemingly putting McVay at roughly 42 players who have already made the team. And that does not include the three special teamers, the two quarterbacks, or L.A.’s two day two rookies who are locks for the 53-man roster. Suddenly all these preseason, training camp names like “Wesley Bailey” and “Jordan Waters” are being thrown around recklessly, as if the Rams will have a final roster with 80 players on it. The numbers don’t add up: If 42 players are sitting and another seven (at least) are locks, that could only leave four more names to make the roster. Now there are ways to “fudge” the numbers and potential looming suspensions for two starters could change the math slightly, but anyone who says that every single preseason darling will make the roster — or even more than one of them — is not doing the legwork to actually explain how they came to that conclusion without also making corresponding moves to get rid of players. Whether that be someone who is now a “must-keep” like Bennett or being light on numbers somewhere that you don’t want to be light, like offensive line depth. So I ran the numbers for those people specifically, allowing them to actually look at the roster and explain themselves. Offense: 18 QB (1) – Matthew Stafford RB (3) – Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Ronnie Rivers WR (4) – Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield TE (4) – Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson OL (6) – AJ Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, David Quessenberry Week 2 changes: Xavier Smith sat out Week 2, indicating that as expected he will return as a punt returner and depth option at receiver after totaling over 300 yards last season. Ronnie Rivers — Gary Klein (@LATimesklein) August 22, 2026 Defense: 19 DL (4) – Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis EDGE (3) – Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart LB (4) – Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Grant Stuard, Shaun Dolac CB (5) – Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Quentin Lake, Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace S (3) – Kamren Kinchens, Kam Curl, Jaylen McCullough Week 2 changes: At least three players moved to the sidelines were Desjuan Johnson, Ty Hamilton, and surprisingly Zech McPhearson, who stood out in the first preseason game and is also one of the team’s best known special teams assets. Special Teams: 3 Total: 40 Including special teams on top of the 37 players who have not suited up at all in the preseason, that only leaves 13 spots on L.A.’s final roster, many of which are still already spoken for even if they did play the last two weeks. Remaining 13 slots: Offense (+8) QB (2) – Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson OL (4+) – A.J. Arcuri, Dylan McMahon, Keagen Trost, Beaux Limmer WR (1+) – Xavier Smith (PR) TE (1) – Max Klare These numbers are obvious and when included in our previous total, take L.A.’s offensive counting up to 26 players on offense. That’s already at least the limit of players the Rams can keep on offense, with a caveat. If Jackson and Nacua are suspended, the Rams will be able to keep two additional players at final cuts. Those players could be ones who play their same position, although in Nacua’s case it seems unnecessary. Defense (+3) DL (1+) – Ty Hamilton EDGE (1+) – Desjuan Johnson CB/Special Teams – Zech McPhearson Defensively, there are considerably more openings, although you’d have to think the majority come in a light front-seven. Hamilton and Johnson are almost certainly on the 53, bringing the total number of defensive linemen and edges from seven to nine. It may not have counted but huge play from #Rams CB Zech McPhearson. He barely joined the roster and made some noise already. — James Brizuela (@james_brizuela) August 15, 2026 It’s not as clear that McPhearson was held out because he made the roster, although zero injuries have been reported and he does fit the need on special teams. There’s a reason to believe he’s on the roster. The next-lightest position on the defense is safety, where a competition is brewing between Nick Andersen, Alex Cook, Tanner Ingle, and Nate Valcarcel. One of they key tiebreakers here, as will be the case for the rest of the roster, is special teams value. It is difficult, however, to gauge how the Rams value their coverage players because most of these guys don’t have much (or any) NFL experience here. What have they done in practice and preseason to earn it? That’s maybe something that could only be revealed on Thursday based on who is sitting against the L.A. Chargers, if not afterwards. Still, let’s change the numbers again by adding in these 10 names to the final roster, but not McPhearson just yet . Total On Roster: 50 Remaining Open Spots: 3 The Rams would now have 26 players on offense, 21 players on defense, and 3 players on special teams, for a total of 50 players on the roster and one side of the ball obviously lagging behind the other in terms of numbers. The Rams would need to keep at least one more safety (we think): I don’t know who, so let’s just say Alex Cook as a reward for his 100-yard interception. It is also believed that with his experience at the University of Washington, the UFL, and some NFL experience, that Cook has good value as a special teams contributor . Done. The Rams keep Cook because they need another safety. That leaves two spots and edge is also looking a little light with four names. A lot of people will say Wesley Bailey here because he was dominant against a third-string tackle for the Saints , and sure that would be fine. Nobody’s really going to complain if Bailey makes the roster . However, the Rams signed Tomon Fox specifically because he’s a special teamer with a solid reputation there. Keeping Fox over other names would upset a lot of fans, but so did keeping Troy Reeder (L.A.’s leading special teamer in snaps last season) once upon a many times. What we do know is that Bailey played a lot of snaps on Saturday and deep into the game (48 snaps) and Fox was used less often (28 snaps), which could mean nothing. Or something. Another clue we’ll wait to find out on Thursday. Ultimately, it doesn’t matter if you choose Bailey or I choose Fox, it’s sensible for the Rams to keep another edge. But then there’s the McPhearson problem. He was held out in Week 2 and he’s a special teamer. The Rams have five cornerbacks now, they could keep six. The Rams keep McPhearson, that leaves one spot open. It is at this point that you could go in any direction you want, but offensive lineman Austin Blaske may offer the most in terms of versatility to play all the offensive line positions and need given that Jackson could be suspended to start the season. Blaske played an incredible 78 snaps on Saturday. Indication that he’s going to get cut unless McVay really loved what he saw? Maybe. But it would make sense that if Jackson is suspended, someone like Blaske makes the team, especially if Trost is also still injured by then. If Jackson is suspended, then the roster spot opens up anyway. If he’s…
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams 53-man roster projection: Who’s on the bubble after Saints game?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have one of the most competitive rosters from top to bottom and making this year’s team is one of the most difficult challenges for rookie and young players around the NFL. But there could be a few names to watch in this final week as the team has one preseason game […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Bub Means #16 of the New Orleans Saints drops a pass as he is covered by Cam Lampkin #21 of the Los Angeles Rams during the first half in a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have one of the most competitive rosters from top to bottom and making this year’s team is one of the most difficult challenges for rookie and young players around the NFL. But there could be a few names to watch in this final week as the team has one preseason game left to play against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday, August 27th. Who is on the bubble for this past week? Here’s my latest 53 man roster projection for the 2026 season; including the “Last four in, Last four out”. Quarterbacks (3) Matthew Stafford, Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson Some people were questioning if Bennett could get cut. I just can’t see that happening. The Rams would trade Bennett for some Day 3 draft capital before outright cutting Bennett. Changes: N/A Running Backs (3) Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Jarquez Hunter I think the Rams need to consider cutting Ronnie Rivers. Here’s why. He is 27 years old and I find it highly unlikely that a team would use a waiver claim to snatch a player that has 72 career rushing attempts for just 295 yards and 0 touchdowns. The Rams should roll the dice, cut Rivers, and then resign him to the practice squad. They can then elevate him from the practice squad on gameday. Changes: Ronnie Rivers (Out) Wide Receivers (6) Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, CJ Daniels, Jordan Whittingon, Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith^ Xavier Smith received a vote of confidence from Sean McVay after the week one preseason game. Perhaps the Rams give Smith a shot at redemption after his fumble in the 2025 NFC Championship Game. Changes: Xavier Smith (In) Tight Ends (5) Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, Davis Allen, Max Klare I will repeat again: 3 personnel is here to stay. Changes: N/A Offensive Line (9) Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, David Quessenberry, Justin Diedich*, Beaux Limmer, Keagen Trost, Austin Blaske^ Some changes here. Justin Dedich is still nursing a hand incident from July. He is still wearing a cast but progressing in his recovery. Right now he is on the NFI which means he does not count against the 53 man roster. That allows for the Rams to keep Austin Blaske who has shown well in two preseason games. Changes: Austin Blaske (In) , Justin Dedich (NFI) Defensive Line (6) Aaron Donald*, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Poona Ford, Ty Hamilton, Tyler Davis “Believe and it will happen.” – Sean McVay (2021 SB speech). Aaron Donald will return and therefore I am making space on my 53 man roster for him. Changes: N/A Edge Rusher (5) Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josiah Stewart, Desjuan Johnson, Wesley Bailey^ Maybe the Rams decide to just keep four edge rushers but Wesley Bailey is highly likely to get claimed if the Rams cut him. title: What Stetson Bennett can do to keep himself employed: Upon Further Review
summary: Stetson Bennett needed a good showing on Saturday to help establish his role as the Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback, and he did exactly that. In fairness, maybe Bennett is locked in no matter what he does through three preseason games. But after rookie Ty Simpson looked solid (if not better) last week, there was […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stetson Bennett needed a good showing on Saturday to help establish his role as the Los Angeles Rams’ backup quarterback, and he did exactly that. In fairness, maybe Bennett is locked in no matter what he does through three preseason games. But after rookie Ty Simpson looked solid (if not better) last week, there was countless chatter about when Simpson would jump him, blogs about whether or not Bennett should be traded and general doubt about his status as an NFL player. But there was one throw in the preseason matchup with the New Orleans Saints that shows why Bennett can stay on an NFL roster for the long term. For the sake of transparency, this original topic for this week’s film review was rookie receiver C.J. Daniels, who led all players with eight receptions in the blowout win. After rewatching the game, there weren’t a ton of “wow” plays from Daniels en route to his successful outing, at least not ones we could easily break down without the coaches film available yet. This throw by Bennett, however, stood out as much on rewatch as it did live (and it even has an end zone view, so props to the CBS LA crew for that). J.B. Long called it out immediately on the local TV broadcast, that this is a perfectly layered throw from Bennett. He beats the Saints’ zone coverage by dropping this ball on a line right between two defenders, and watch for when Tyler Scott breaks at the top of his route. This isn’t the most astounding anticipatory throw in NFL history, but Bennett was still able to get this out and to the right spot without needing his receiver to camp out for it. Footwork-wise, it’s not perfect but for the sake of this particular evaluation it almost helps because you can see the torque Bennett gets behind this throw, hitting the exact equilibrium needed between power and touch to get this ball to Scott on time. We should also note that the protection is stellar here. Bennett gets bumped softly just after the throw, but you can’t ask for a better pocket than this regardless of the caliber of opponent. Receiver left and tight end right both execute their assignments well while the rest of the line totally neutralizes the Saints’ pass rush. It should always be easier to pass from a clean pocket than a muddy one, but don’t hold that against the quarterback here; you would rather see good protection and strong execution instead of more pressure and a total meltdown. When you’re used to watching a guy like Matthew Stafford or any other elite quarterback, this isn’t an other-worldly throw by any means. Mahomes, Allen, Jackson, Burrow, Prescott, Love, Herbert, that class of quarterback rarely, if ever, has an issue making this throw. But we’re not talking about a passer of that caliber, we’re talking about a somewhat fringe backup who still hasn’t taken a snap in a meaningful game. We know Bennett can complete easy, gimme throws like flats and arrows off of naked bootlegs, but he needs to show that he can make pro throws and push the ball downfield while doing it. He checks that box here. It’s harsh but fair to say Bennett does not have long-term starter upside in the NFL. The traits just aren’t there for that. However, a solid backup quarterback doesn’t need to be able to make every throw or create in every situation, they need to keep the ball safe and push it in specific spots. The Rams need to see completions like this to feel comfortable in putting him on the field in a pinch, and he needs to see it to feel comfortable getting another paycheck after his rookie deal expires next spring.

title: Wesley Bailey would be longest long shot to make Rams roster
summary: Wesley Bailey wasn’t on anyone’s radar to make the L.A. Rams 53-man roster, but a strong showing against the New Orleans Saints on Saturday had some comparing him to Leonard Floyd, a former top-10 pick in the draft. Eating against Alex Wollschlaeger, an undrafted rookie out of Kentucky who is listed as the Saints third-string […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Linebacker Wesley Bailey (47) of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after a New Orleans Saints fumble in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Wesley Bailey wasn’t on anyone’s radar to make the L.A. Rams 53-man roster, but a strong showing against the New Orleans Saints on Saturday had some comparing him to Leonard Floyd, a former top-10 pick in the draft. Eating against Alex Wollschlaeger, an undrafted rookie out of Kentucky who is listed as the Saints third-string tackle, Bailey hit Zach Wilson with a first quarter sack. Later, Bailey fought off a block in the run game to punch out the ball at the goal line to keep New Orleans scoreless on the day. An impressive performance in a preseason setting. Wesley Bailey was one of the Rams to watch in today's preseason game! 🔹5 Tackles 🔹Sack 🔹Forced Fumble 🔹 4 QB Hits He caught up with our @DarrenMHaynes after his stellar performance! @CBSLosAngeles | #RamsHouse | #RamsCentral pic.twitter.com/q0J2NHpxfE — Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) August 22, 2026 One month ago, Turf Show Times compiled over 100 53-man rosters compiled by Rams fans and made a single consensus edition, and unsurprisingly it did not feature Bailey. Nobody would have expected that for an undrafted rookie going into his first training camp and Bailey’s $35,000 signing bonus was decently-sized , although not as much as Dan Villari. There just wasn’t a lot about him that stood out, and Bailey didn’t even rank among the top-10 players to not make the cut on those 53-man rosters. Instead, Rams fans projected that L.A. would only keep four edge rushers, including Desjuan Johnson as the last man in behind the obvious top-three. Instead, Keir Thomas was on 33-percent of your rosters, which ranked as the most for any outside linebacker who didn’t make the team. If Bailey doesn’t make it, he could commiserate with Wollschlaeger, a player widely expected by Saints fans to get cut by the team in a week. But even the practice squad would be a phenomenal accomplishment for Bailey, a player who had 15.5 sacks over five years in college between Rutgers and Louisville . In comparison, Floyd had 17 sacks in three years at Georgia prior to blowing scouts away with a 4.6 40-yard dash at 244 lbs at the 2016 combine. Bailey got onto L.A.’s radar before the draft too, running a 4.69 40-yard dash at 260 lbs at the Louisville pro day . Floyd also had a 5” higher vertical. Sean McVay felt that Bailey had improved from where he was in the first preseason game, during and after which there were a couple mentions of Bailey but not many. Wesley Bailey making his presence felt. pic.twitter.com/MAqYeUYk6l — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 23, 2026 As usual, the clues behind who will make the Rams roster and who won’t are not subtle with McVay: It’s not who plays well in the preseason, it’s who sits on the bench in the preseason. Bailey has played a lot of snaps in two preseason games. If he sees the field in Week 3 against the Chargers at all, he’s still fighting just to make the roster. If he sits, he’s likely already on it. Whereas we know the Rams have four edge rushers already on the 53, we don’t know if they’ll keep a fifth and who that might be. We do know that Bailey looks like a better football player than Wollschlaeger. Is he a better football player than the guy the Rams would have to cut in order to keep him? Rams backups highlight the NFL’s flawed beauty in 34-0 win over Saints ( Sporting Tribune ) “Thousands of football fans traveled through an asphalt skillet and sun-baking rays to sit in SoFi Stadium air thick with the smell of polyethylene pellets and concession food, littering empty seats and staring down at a field full of men fighting for their lives. Peter Pan lost his shadow in Wendy Darling’s nursery. Peter Pan never played football. Peter Pan never had to stare down the barrel of an NFL roster cut or feel the August sun bake his last hope into the turf. Not the marquee names. The other ones. The New Orleans Saints never stood a chance in the 34-0 drubbing.“ Brenda Song makes color analyst debut for Rams ( B/R ) “Actress Brenda Song joined the broadcast of the Los Angeles Rams’ preseason clash with the New Orleans Saints as a guest color analyst on Saturday. She was part of the CBS broadcast in the third quarter of the game, which the Rams went on to win 34-0.“ This is a canon event for football fans everywhere. 😍 pic.twitter.com/DXfWxtIqN2 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 23, 2026 “After her stint in the booth on Saturday, maybe we’ll see Song next during a regular season game.“ Zach Wilson on Saints 34-0 preseason loss to Rams, “Yeah it was ugly” ( WDSU ) “The Saints (0-2) stirred up their own quarterback competition with Zach Wilson and Spencer Rattler playing one half apiece at SoFi Stadium, but neither prospective backup to Tyler Shough stood out during a rough overall outing for New Orleans. Rattler moved the offense better than Wilson while facing the bottom of the Rams’ defensive depth chart in the second half, but the Saints also made two goal-line turnovers, with Rattler throwing an interception that was returned for a 100-yard touchdown by safety Alex Cook.“ Wesley Bailey is making it incredibly tough for Rams to cut him ( RamsWire ) “Outside linebacker Wesley Bailey has stood out as an undrafted gem, using his natural length to win against offensive tackles and continuously establish dominant positions as a pass rusher. He’s done his part to blow up the opposition, both in practice and the preseason. Having drawn comparisons to Super Bowl winner Leonard Floyd, Bailey emulated Floyd’s destructive ability with five tackles, one sack, and four quarterback hits in the Rams’ 34-0 preseason win against the New Orleans Saints. Plus, he punched the ball out of Ty Chandler’s hands inside the 5 to preserve the shutout.“ 6 standouts from Rams’ 34-0 win over Saints ( RamsWire ) RT Austin Blaske “Keagen Trost is injured right now but Blaske has been a bright spot at right tackle. He played well against the Saints, both in pass protection and the run game, making a case to stick on the practice squad if he does get cut next weekend. The Rams didn’t allow a single sack and gained 5 yards per carry on the ground, a testament to the play of the entire offensive line.“ 5 Takeaways from Rams’ 34-0 preseason Week 2 win over Saints ( Rams ) “ Takeaways for days: Safety Alex Cook took a pick-six 100 yards to the house with 9:06 left in the third quarter to give the Rams a 27-point lead. Then late in the third quarter, Bailey’s forced fumble inside the Saints 5-yard line was recovered by defensive lineman Payton Zdroik . While the ensuing drive after the fumble recovery didn’t amount to points, it still kept New Orleans out of the endzone.“ Comment of the Day Sometimes you just want to see Ty Simpson. RamFan1970: Man, we are never going to get to see our offense in this 2nd half. I’ve never been so disappointed to get a pick 6….Lol Feed Post of the Day: Biggest Winner?

title: Raiders news: Ashton Jeanty avoids major injury
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have been relatively unscathed through training camp and the preseason this summer, yet, Sunday, exactly three weeks before they start the regular season the team may have been delivered a major blow as second-year starting running back Ashton Jeanty had to leave practice with an injury to his right leg. According […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Ashton Jeanty #2 of the Las Vegas Raiders watches from the bench in the first half against the Houston Texans during a preseason game at Reliant Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have been relatively unscathed through training camp and the preseason this summer, yet, Sunday, exactly three weeks before they start the regular season the team may have been delivered a major blow as second-year starting running back Ashton Jeanty had to leave practice with an injury to his right leg. According to multiple media reports, the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 draft went down awkwardly after diving for a pass in the team-practice period. He was down on the field for some time as the entire team took a knee and prayed in silence. He was helped off the field by trainers. Jeanty could not put any weight on his leg. The team did not have an immediate update on Jeanty. However, ESPN’s Adam Schefter later reported that the running back is “believed to have sprained his ankle”. Schefter also noted that the Raiders aren’t sure how long Jeanty will be out, but it isn’t considered a long-term injury. The team has big expecatitons for Jeanty in the both the running and passing game. If he has to miss time, rookie Mike Washington, who has looked great in the preseason, would likely move into the starting role. Las Vegas has been planning to use Jeanty and Washington as a potent 1-2 punch. In other practice notes: Kirk Cousins took all the first-team reps, while Fernando Mendoza took all the second-team reps. That’s another indicaiton the team is leaning heavily toward making Cousins the Week 1 starter. They were inside Sunday afternoon and had a padded practice. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson was back to work after getting banged up last Monday. He rotated with Caleb Rogers as he was doing before being injured. Wide receiver Dont’e Thornton is still not back. Coach Klint Kubiak had said he’d play in the preseason, but time is getting short with the finale in four days. Tight end Carter Runyon remained out. Safety Treydan Stukes got extensive reps with the first team defense.

title: 5 Las Vegas Raiders players who stepped up against the Texans
summary: There is only one cut day in the NFL now, but with two weeks of preseason action in the books some players have began to establish themselves. Aidan O’Connnell It took O’Connell three possessions, 23 plays, 195 yards, two touchdowns and 10:29 to turn the game around. The former 4th-round pick set the Raiders highest […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Aidan O'Connell #12 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass during the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is only one cut day in the NFL now, but with two weeks of preseason action in the books some players have began to establish themselves. Aidan O’Connnell It took O’Connell three possessions, 23 plays, 195 yards, two touchdowns and 10:29 to turn the game around. The former 4th-round pick set the Raiders highest point total for a single game in team history as a starter. He is on a rookie deal and doesn’t have to be declared active and can still play as the #3 quarterback. Additionally, he has trade value should another team want a capable veteran option at a low cost. Here is O’Connell’s biggest value to the Raiders. Let’s play out a doom scenario: the offensive line’s pass-protection issues don’t improve, and the receivers aren’t able to answer head coach Klint Kubiak’s callout. Kirk Cousins starts the season, plays x number of games and something happens. (Not wishing ill on Cousins, just a scenario). If protecting number-one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza remains the plan, rather than feeding him to the wolves, O’Connell can continue to showcase his abilities before his upcoming free agency. There is absolutely no need to cut him or move him unless something impressive is offered in return. Cian Slone Slone has been another eye-opener in the preseason. Playing a total of 43 snaps in two games, Slone has 5 tackles, 4 quarterback hits, 2 pressures (one leading to an interception) and a sack. Pure hustle and technique is how Slone is making it happen. The former Wolfpack edge has perfected the art of running the hoop and it’s results have been unique. Slone’s lateral quickness and change of direction is incredibly fast. His hustle to the echoes of the whistle leads to multiple second-chance opportunities where he has capitalized. Pat Johnson Johnson has shown up in both games as a well-rounded player. He has sacked the quarterback in both games and forced a game-changing fumble against the Houston Texans. With multiple run stuffs per game, Johnson is outplaying just about every defensive end on the roster. Johnson isn’t the biggest at defensive end, but you would never be able to tell that from watching him on the field. He has worked his way up from the bottom of the depth chart to starting with the twos against Houston’s ones. He is certainly a rotational piece that the Raiders defense will need in 2026. Folorunso Fatukasi It was only one preseason outing against a former team, but Fatukasi provided the push up front we haven’t seen all preseason. Fatukasi collapsed the pocket, bringing pressure on multiple occasions, fighting through double teams and stuffing the run. Size up front is an issue for the defense; if Fatukasi can continue to provide the push up the middle, he should start. Jermod McCoy The rookie bounced back nicely from his preseason debut last week; he didn’t surrender a touchdown against the Texans. McCoy showed the promise of a first-round corner’s ability, blanketing his coverage and preventing a catch. Where he went wrong this time was standing over the receiver and taunting him on the ground. A true rookie mistake that cost the team getting off the field. A coachable moment for a player the Raiders will be relying on heavily in the not-so-distant future. McCoy took a lot of heat for getting outmuscled against the Cardinals, none of that happened against the Texans.

title: The Year 2 bar for Raiders wide receiver Don’te Thornton Jr.
summary: Over the course of the “Year 2 bar” series for the Las Vegas Raiders 2025 NFL Draft picks, we’ve explored what kind of impact to expect from the second-year players. For Dont’e Thornton Jr. — the Tennessee wide receiver the Silver & Black took in the fourth round (108th overall) in last year’s draft — […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - JULY 29: Dont'e Thornton Jr. #10 of the Las Vegas Raiders stretches during the first practice of the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on July 29, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the course of the “Year 2 bar” series for the Las Vegas Raiders 2025 NFL Draft picks, we’ve explored what kind of impact to expect from the second-year players. For Dont’e Thornton Jr. — the Tennessee wide receiver the Silver & Black took in the fourth round (108th overall) in last year’s draft — the bar is not only lower, but is more distinct compared to his 2025 draft classmates: Make the team. This is a byproduct of the freakishly tall (6-foot-5 and 205 pounds) and fast (4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine) being an old-school Raiders fit on physical traits alone, but have minimal impact his rookie season in 2025. Height and speed alone tends to get prospects looks by NFL teams so taking a swing on the Tennessee product was apt in the middle rounds of the draft. But after flashes in the offseason and training camp after being drafted and early in the regular season — including a clutch long catch by Thornton against the New England Patriots in Week 1 last season helping seal the victory on the road — the 23-year-old’s confidence dipped severely as the season went on. And even when he garnered substantial snaps (such as in Weeks 2, 7, and 16), he was targeted 11 times hauling in just three passes for 32 yards with zero end zone visits. By The Numbers Dont’e Thornton Jr., Wide Receiver, 2nd Year 2025: 15 games (5 starts), 30 targets, 10 receptions, 135 yards, 0 touchdowns Career: See Above According to Pro Football Reference, Thornton logged 399 snaps on offense as a rookie (zero on special teams, oddly enough), and was targeted 30 times hauling in 10 of them for 130 yards . He was charted with three drops (a 10 percent drop rate). Thus a sophomore surge is warranted for for the Maryland native. Especially on a Klint Kubiak-led team which features an offensive-minded head coach that is also the play caller. If there’s a coach that can develop and guide a raw but talented Thornton, it’s Kubiak and his coaching staff. However, availability has long been the best ability by a player, and the wideout is more observer than participator on a recent string of practices. #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak on Dont'e Thornton Jr. who's missed four straight practices and last night's preseason opener "We do expect to get him back. He's been banged up a little bit, but we're expecting him to get back on the field and see some action in the preseason at some… — Jesse Merrick – Silver & Black Sports Network (@JesseSBSN) August 14, 2026 Thornton needs to showcase himself to the new coaching staff and after leaving practice earlier this month, he’s been working on the side without a definitive timetable for return despite Kubiak hoping he’d have his wide receiver available. In both the preseason opener on Aug. 13 and the second exhibition clash this past Thursday with the Houston Texans, you could see Thornton in street clothes on the sideline. That’s not where he wants to be. Especially with other wide receivers not only getting valuable reps and snaps, but putting on valuable game and practice film that Kubiak and his coaches will pour over to make final 53-man roster decisions and the ensuing 16-man practice squad (17 if the Raiders use the International Player Pathway Program slot for undrafted free agent Kansei Matsuzawa). Late-round rookie — Malik Benson, selected by the Raiders in the sixth round (195th overall) of the 2026 draft — opened eyes this offseason with his speed, route running, and soft hands. The 6-foot-1 and 195-pound Oregon product is a burner getting plenty of work on offense and special teams and is piquing fan interest — much like Thornton did as a rookie. But after a deep catch against Houston, the Kansas native had his bouts of drops and it’ll be intriguing to see Benson’s mental toughness going forward. Will his confidence sink or swim? Kubiak’s own confidence in the wide receiver room is just as questionable. “Yeah, I learned a lot in that we have to get a lot better very fast. That we took a step backwards; doesn’t mean we can’t go forward,” Kubiak said when asked what did he learn about his position group over the last couple of days with the joint practices and preseason clash with Houston. “But right now, we are trying to find someone that is accountable and can help us on Sunday. Still looking.” The last two words provides Thornton an ample door to kick in and make the coaching staff take notice — if he can get back on the field soon. Geno Smith to Dont'e Thornton Jr. for the @raiders TD! Watch on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Y7ighsyaaQ — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2025 Despite overshadowing NFL cornerbacks with his size, Thornton doesn’t play like a 6-foot-5 wideout who can outleap and out-physical defenders at the catch point. With his confidence waning last season, Thornton played more like 5-foot-8 teammate Tre Tucker than imposing himself on defenders. Engraining the belief that he’s simply bigger and faster than defensive backs tasked with covering him is a must-do in Year 2. Being able to play stronger and not get locked up by cornerbacks while aggressively outleaping them for the ball i flight is what Thornton needs to consistently showcase. Having elite size and speed is no good if the athlete doesn’t know how to or want to use it to their advantage. Then comes the heavy stuff, such as improving route running (refined sharper cuts to add more than just run fast deep down the field). Kubiak asks his wide receivers to run a full route tree and at this point in time, Thornton is the Charlie Brown Christmas Tree with straight-line deep routes being sparse branch. Kubiak did well to hire Zach Azzanni as his wide receivers coach as the 50-year-old assistant boasts a maniacal focus on fundamental techniques that’s no-nonsense, demanding, but focused on developing pass catchers. That’s similar to the Raiders’ head coach’s philosophy and Azzanni uses relentless drill repetition to instill the attention to detail and fundamentals into his wide receiver room that sharpens not only physical attributes but mental, too. And Thornton most definitely needs both. “Same thing with Dont’e. I always tell our room that the tape is our resume, let the tape be our guide,” Azzanni said of Thornton in early August. “So, all of those guys, if they have a down day, they got to come back and have a better day. We just press play. We evaluate it every day. He’s had a couple rough days and he’s bounced back and had some good plays here and there. And that’s what we’re looking for in training camp, we’re installing all this stuff. Everything’s not going to be perfect, but I am pleased he’s got a great attitude. He’s working his tail off. I saw some improvement today, which was good. We go day by day in training camp, so he’s coming along like the rest of them.” First, Thornton needs a clean bill of health to get back into the mix. From there, make an impression with the remaining practices and final preseason game (this coming Thursday against the San Francisco 49ers). NFL cut day — the drastic shift from 90-man to 53-man rosters — is on August 30 so time is dwindling. But with Kubiak wanting his wide receiver room to step up, there’s a window for Thornton. And making the final roster is the immediate bar in Year 2. Matching or improving upon his rookie numbers would be icing on the cake. And isn’t that a bit disconcerting for a player drafted in the fourth round just last year?

title: Your Thoughts On The Preseason Dolphins Vs Giants Game
summary: Following yesterday’s preseason game between our Miami Dolphins and the New York Giants, I asked the following question: What were your takeaways from last night’s preseason game between our Miami Dolphins and the Washington Commanders New York Giants? What were the positives and negatives that you saw? What was encouraging, and what has to be […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Jameis Winston #19 of the New York Giants drives for a touchdown ahead of Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins during the first half of a pre season game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following yesterday’s preseason game between our Miami Dolphins and the New York Giants, I asked the following question: What were your takeaways from last night’s preseason game between our Miami Dolphins and the Washington Commanders New York Giants? What were the positives and negatives that you saw? What was encouraging, and what has to be addressed/hopefully fixed before the season begins? Below are some of your thoughts and answers- Dolfan 22 points to one of many worrying stats from yesterday’s game. 3 first downs!!! My goodness!! Dave21 points out that these growing pains are all a part of the process. Well the game was not fun to watch that’s for sure, but all second ,third string and players that won’t make this team. We know the starters and some starting players were banged up before this game. Pre season is just for players trying to win a job. Our 1’s don’t look horrible, but if we lose any of them these season will be much worse than expected . This will be a long a bad season zero doubt in my mind, 27 should be much better and 28 should be great. Player growth takes time, I have been preaching that on here forever. These boys a green and they need experience. We have sucked for 30 years, 1 more is that bad!! We’re used to it!! Dolfanjoe is another who points out that this is going to be a year of painful growth, a bye year, if you will. What do you not understand about a complete rebuild ? Total salary cap dump. Signing a few player extensions, notice without trade clause in the contract ! We are and should be worse than an expansion team. We will have a first string team to go out and compete with many teams all year long. This will be whittled down by injuries as the season goes on. It is hard as a fan to accept that we very well may hold the first or second pick in the 27 draft. This is by plan ! No one in the organization is going to say that out loud. Just go to the podium and say we have some things to correct and are working towards that goal. The rebuild started with 13 draft picks. Another full draft next year with early picks that can be traded for many more picks. Yes we will actually have money for free agents also to fill those holes that will be very apparent this year. 22 starters on a 53 man squad that will be changing all across the bottom all year long. 32 other practice squads to pluck better players from. title: Dolphins rookie defender to miss time after injury during game against Giants
summary: Without most of their starters in the lineup, the Miami Dolphins fell to the New York Giants by a score of 26-3 during week two of the NFL preseason. While many players sat out the game, the team’s rookies were on full display for much of the contest. Unfortunately, one of Miami’s defensive rookies couldn’t […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 25: Trey Moore #DL53 of Texas speaks to the media during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 25, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Without most of their starters in the lineup, the Miami Dolphins fell to the New York Giants by a score of 26-3 during week two of the NFL preseason. While many players sat out the game, the team’s rookies were on full display for much of the contest. Unfortunately, one of Miami’s defensive rookies couldn’t make it through four-quarters of action — leaving early due to injury. Rookie linebacker Trey Moore — Miami’s first selection in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft — was pulled from Saturday’s exhibition game early due to an ankle injury. While rushing Giants quarterback Jameis Winston, Moore leapt into the air in an attempt to swat a pass to the ground. Unfortunately, it was Miami’s rookie who ended up in a heap on the grass instead — eventually needing assistance while leaving the playing field. Moore was listed as a starter when the Dolphins released their initial depth chart. According to head coach Jeff Hafley, Miami’s rookie isn’t expected back from injury any time soon. The Dolphins are still gathering information on how severe the ailment Moore suffered yesterday is. For a team that has displayed its lack of depth in two consecutive preseason contests, an injury to a starter — even a rookie — is a serious blow. Here’s hoping Moore can overcome his injury in quick fashion in order to return to a team that will surely need his services as the year progresses. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team prepares for its final preseason contest against the Atlanta Falcons this upcoming Friday.
