title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ 24-21 preseason win over the Eagles
summary: Joint practices. Scuffles. Wild overreactions. Peaks of optimism and valleys of depression. Now the preseason is really underway. Depending on who you listen to/follow out in the sports media world, the Patriots are either going to be the most dangerous team in the league or are light-years behind where they were this time last year. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Tommy DeVito #16 of the New England Patriots looks to pass during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joint practices. Scuffles. Wild overreactions. Peaks of optimism and valleys of depression. Now the preseason is really underway. Depending on who you listen to/follow out in the sports media world, the Patriots are either going to be the most dangerous team in the league or are light-years behind where they were this time last year. Crown them or start getting ready for the 2027 NFL Draft. This type of preseason buzz used to annoy the hell out of me, but now I just find it amusing. Maybe I’m getting soft in my old age. I’m definitely not any wiser than I was 20 years ago, so it can’t be that. It seems like we saw even less starters last night than we did in Week 1 of the preseason, so I’m not sure how much sense there is in breaking anything down. These games seem to have gotten even more pointless ever since they altered the preseason format. On the plus side, it makes me feel a lot less guilty for completely mailing these articles in until the season starts in earnest. Nothing that happened yesterday is more important than Ja’Quinden Jackson’s health and well-being. Injuries at any point in the season are absolutely brutal… but there’s just something about preseason injuries that hit different. It’s such a weird time of year; we’re seeing a number of guys who have spent their entire lives dreaming and working towards an NFL career, and they have such a limited window in which they can make it happen. All signs point to Jackson being OK, which is the best news you can ask for. In terms of the game itself… the punt team was fairly solid, I guess. Bryce Baringer has a great leg on him. I’m not sure how much value he adds to the finesse punting game, but if the Patriots ever need to flip the field, he’s a good guy to have on the roster. And this battle for RB3 is really fun. But other than that, is there anything of note that took place last night? I feel like the most intriguing storyline of the preseaon so far is how much time Kyle Williams has seen out there. On one hand, somebody has to play in these games, and the top of the WR room seems fairly well set. And if Williams saw significant second-half time, I missed it. Plus, the coaches are on record stating their intention to make Williams a major part of their offensive scheme. But on the other, maybe they’re just saying that? Maybe they want to showcase him to move on? He for sure has explosive ability and can break the game open with a single play, as we saw last night. I just don’t know how much of a factor he’s going to be. As with a lot of NFL teams, depth seems to be an issue for the Patriots, particularly along the offensive line and at the linebacker position. New England used to be lousy with versatile, rangy, cerebral LBs who could play on the line and off the ball, drop into coverage or add an extra pass rusher. As of right now, I couldn’t even fathom a guess as to what their base defense is going to be. There’s Landry, Spillane…and then kind of a drop off. Still waiting for Gabe Jacas to start Gabe Jacasing. And yes, I’m very aware of how little I’d need to change to label him Gabe Jackass. Hopefully it never comes anywhere close to that point. If I had to pick an RB3 right now, I’m probably giving it to Lan Larison. Seems to have more upside as a blocker and as a receiver. My preseason darling continues to be Kindle Vildor, who had three tackles (two solo) yesterday. I’m not sure how much additional special teams value he adds, but if the Patriots ever want to put some kind of Cruciatus curse on anyone, he’s their guy. I didn’t think I’d walk away from Week 2 of the preseason having gleaned even less about the team than I did in Week 1, but here I find myself. It seems that more and more teams are treating joint practices like the actual games, so when the time the game does come around it’s more or less a glorified scrimmage. At this point I’m wondering if Drake Maye will even take a snap this August. The only real substantive information any of us can take from yesterday was keeping count of who was still playing late in the fourth quarter. All that said, here are three things I’m particularly optimistic about based on what we’ve seen so far: There are more viable safeties on this team than I thought there would be coming into the year. I wasn’t sure how that position was going to shake out, and while I don’t think that there are any Pro Bowlers on the roster, safety doesn’t look to be a liability. May we never know, but as far as competent backup QBs go, I think the Patriots have a very solid one in DeVito and a competent, high-ceilinged one in Morton. I don’t see Morton making the final squad, but I can for sure see him sticking around Foxboro. If you want to take a massive amount of liberty with the phrase “breakout year,” I think you can apply it to Efton Chism. Whereas Williams brings the big-play skillset to the team, Chism is that shifty, versatile, change-of-pace receiver that the team hasn’t had in a while. I think he’ll make the final roster. How much time he’ll see is anyone’s guess, but he has enough ability. On the flipside, here are three things I’m pessimistic about based on what I’ve seen so far: I wish I had an opinion on Caleb Lomu by this point. He seemed adequate in his duties at left tackle, but he got spun around on several occasions and gave up a sack before halftime. You don’t want to redshirt your first-rounder, but maybe that’s the plan as Morgan Moses ages out of the game. Related to that, the most exciting rush of the season came on a 36-yard scramble from the backup quarterback. Jam Miller had a nice 20-yard cut and run last night, but any kind of running game has been more or less nonexistent. I’m less pessimistic about this than I am about the O-line, as coaches don’t really scheme up running plays and neither Rhamondre Stevenson nor TreVeyon Henderson have gotten a single meaningful carry thus far… but I would have liked to have seen more from the ground game at this point. I’m still a little worried about the tackling. Too many misses so far. Too many edges unset. Too many failures to wrap up and bring down. Tackling is either the kind of thing you have or you don’t. I know it’s early in the year… but I may have already found my favorite moment of 2026. She wasn’t on my radar before, but Dr. Jennifer Welter most certainly is now. She already shattered a glass ceiling as the NFL’s first female coach all the way back in 2015. And last night she proved that not only can she raise the bar, she can also close one down. Just an all-time interview. I’d be amazed if the starters don’t see at least a few drives on Thursday before the team has two full weeks off leading up to what is going to be an absolutely brutal road opener. So, maybe my next Fan Notes will have something of substance to say. Doubtful, I kn0w; I don’t think I’ve ever once said anything of substance. But I’m looking forward to Thursday, as it means that it’s almost time to really start caring. September can’t get here soon enough.

title: Kyle Williams, Efton Chism create ‘good problem’ in Patriots receiver room
summary: The New England Patriots’ wide receiver room is crowded. With seven players on the depth chart who have NFL experience and production, something could have to change by roster cutdown day next week. That decision will ultimately be made by head coach Mike Vrabel and  executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf. All in […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Kyle Williams (18) runs for a touchdown after making a catch against Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Ambry Thomas (38) during the first half at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots’ wide receiver room is crowded. With seven players on the depth chart who have NFL experience and production, something could have to change by roster cutdown day next week. That decision will ultimately be made by head coach Mike Vrabel and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf. All in all, it’s a welcomed problem. “It’s funny to listen to it, because a couple of years ago everybody was saying that we didn’t have anything and now we have too many, so it’s a good problem to have,” Wolf told WBZ during Saturday’s preseason game. “The thing I really like about the group — we have a bunch of good players, they all compliment each other well. [Josh McDaniels]’ offense, it’s pretty nuanced and there’s a lot of different roles. We have guys that can fill out those roles and we’re excited about what they’re going to bring to us this year.” The Patriots strengthened the room this offseason by acquiring A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. They joined a depth chart that included DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kayshon Boutte, and second-year receivers Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. With the veterans sitting out Saturday’s preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles , snaps were available throughout the first-half for Williams and Chism. The duo showcased why the Patriots’ wide receiver room is not only deep, but talented. “I love [Kyle’s] ability outside the numbers to be able to stretch the field. And we wanted to give him some more opportunities to be able to do that as well as work on some of the stuff that Todd [Downing] and Josh [McDaniels] have him trying to improve on,” Vrabel said. “And it was good to see Chiz come out tonight and do some things and just try to be able to evaluate everybody as we look to build this roster.” Williams night wasn’t perfect, as he hauled in just 2-of-6 targets, but he showcased that special ability to stretch the field in the second quarter, getting behind Philadelphia’s defense to haul in a 69-yard touchdown from Tommy DeVito — reaching more than 20 mph in the process. Chism, meanwhile, caught all four of his targets for 45 yards, including a 24-yard catch on third-down on a Josh McDaniels staple. As the young duo have continued to impress on the field, they have embraced the competition in their room, seeing the talent around them as something that can make everyone better. “I think anytime there’s competition, as a competitor, you rise up, you take that challenge on, and you just go out there and compete every day,” Chism said. “The room we have, it’s so special. It’s so awesome to be a part of.” “It’s competitive, but it’s friendly competition. Nobody gets mad at anybody,” Williams added. “It’s iron sharpening iron at the end of the day. So, I’m really glad to have these great group of guys — great vets from top down. So, it’s just a fun room to be in.” As New England ultimately cuts their roster down to 53 players by Aug. 30, it’s hard to envision either second-year receiver not being a part of the group. That could result in the team keeping all seven players on the active roster, unless a trade comes together for Boutte, who requested one back in the spring and remains in the final year of his rookie contract. For now, the Patriots have the kind of depth that makes difficult decisions a good thing. “That’s the best possible situation you can ask for in an organization,” Tommy DeVito said. “To have so many options where you have to make hard decisions like that. But again, that’s just a testament to the coaching and to the guys of just coming in every day, putting their hard hats on and working, and not worrying too much about what that [cut down] day is like.”

title: ‘Gritty, tough’ Lan Larison distinguishes himself in Patriots running back competition
summary: With just a week left until roster cutdowns, the competition for the New England Patriots’ third running back spot is heating up. So is Lan Larison. The second-year back was one of the top performers during the Patriots’ preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday. Serving as a runner, receiver and returner, he registered […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jose Ramirez (43) tackles New England Patriots running back Lan Larison (34) during the second half at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With just a week left until roster cutdowns, the competition for the New England Patriots’ third running back spot is heating up. So is Lan Larison. The second-year back was one of the top performers during the Patriots’ preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday. Serving as a runner, receiver and returner, he registered a combined 128 all-purpose yards and found the end zone once. And not just that, he also received some praise from head coach Mike Vrabel after the 24-21 victory. “I felt like Lan certainly had a good performance — a gritty, tough performance tonight, and did some really good things,” Vrabel said. “It is 4th-and-1, and he gets hit behind the line of scrimmage and finds a way to get the first down. And then we have another long pass, and then he is able to break a couple tackles there on third down when we needed it at the end of the game. So, he did some good things.” What makes Vrabel’s comments noteworthy in the context of New England’s running back battle was that he wasn’t asked about just Larison, but rather the entire backup group behind roster locks Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. Jam Miller, Hassan Haskins and JaMycal Hasty, his competitors for what might not be more than one spot on the team, did not get the same shoutout. They also didn’t have the same impact on the game, even though all of them had their moments as well. Overall, however, Larison proved to be more instrumental to New England’s offensive success: he caught three passes for 41 yards and ran the ball nine times for 33 and the aforementioned touchdown. “I just have to keep going,” the 2025 undrafted free agent out of UC Davis said after the game. “It wasn’t all just me, it was the line as well, and the team. We competed really well tonight, and it was fun. It was a good time.” Even though he can feel good about his overall outing, Larison still wasn’t perfect. According to Pro Football Focus , he gave up two quarterback hurries in five pass-blocking reps — a possible sign of his inexperience after he missed virtually his entire rookie season on injured reserve. “I’m still learning and seeing new things every single day,” the 24-year-old said. “Just taking it day-by-day.”

(Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots second-round rookie Gabe Jacas, a defensive starter during Saturday’s preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles , is seeing the field better after joining the team late during offseason workouts. The outside linebacker’s first practice with New England was on Aug. 1 in a limited role. Knee and pre-draft hamstring injuries kept him unavailable through the spring, along with an unresolved rookie contract that wasn’t agreed upon until July 26 . Jacas sees his second preseason matchup at Gillette Stadium as another learning experience, with the beginning of his rookie season in September soon approaching. “It was a good night. Another game under my belt. Another game I can learn from. New opportunities,” Jacas said after the matchup. “[I’m] just grateful and blessed that I was out there, running around and having fun.” Among the areas where the 22-year-old is learning to help himself develop as a player, identifying play designs at the NFL level is something he’s focused on. “Just the little things,” Jacas said about what he’s been working on during his first two preseason contests. “First of all is alignment, hand placement [and] looking at backfield sets. You know, all the little things that not only my coach (Mike Smith) but also [Mike] Vrabel talks about. So, those things I can work on.” The Illinois product concluded his Saturday night performance with four tackles and a quarterback hit on the Eagles’ backup Andy Dalton. On a second-down snap in the second quarter, Jacas immediately charged into the backfield after going unblocked, pressuring the veteran quarterback into an incompletion. But while there were flashes of strong plays, rookie mistakes remained. On the previous play, cornerback Kindle Vildor intercepted Dalton and returned the takeaway into the red zone; however, a roughing-the-passer call on Jacas wiped out the turnover. “I think [he’s] just still inconsistent,” his head coach, Mike Vrabel, said about Jacas’ development after the game. “I think that the effort is certainly there. The willingness. He is a very coachable player. We are just putting a lot on him right now as far as special teams and covering kicks and playing on kick return. We have to be able to see what he can do and maybe what we feel like we can count on when the regular season comes. “I think he will just continue to improve because he has that type of attitude, and he is willing, and I know he will get back to work real quick.” Jacas was asked about the penalty, calling it a “learning lesson” for himself and something he needs to be careful of. And because the Fort Pierce, FL, native began practicing late in the offseason, he missed crucial special teams reps that Vrabel believes are among the most important for young players to learn . Earlier in August, Vrabel spent extensive one-on-one time with the rookie working on punt protection drills. The Patriots’ physical pass rusher noted his special teams play as an area of improvement from last week’s preseason matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. “There are a lot of ebbs and flows of a professional football game,” Vrabel said about what he’s looking for in players fighting through adversity. “How can you handle making a mistake? How can you handle getting blocked? How can you handle having a good play and then coming back and being able to do it again? And how they bounce back, how they handle different situations. What they do in live action, I think, is really critical.”
author: Andrew Guindon

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Eagles preseason game
summary: The New England Patriots played their second preseason game of the summer on Saturday night at Gillette Stadium, and, once again, decided not to use their starters. Naturally, with the backups in the game, the roster competition was the main event against the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s find out what we learned about them, and the general state […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Casey Rogers #65 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a fumble recovery with Karon Prunty #21 and Namdi Obiazor #48 during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots played their second preseason game of the summer on Saturday night at Gillette Stadium, and, once again, decided not to use their starters. Naturally, with the backups in the game, the roster competition was the main event against the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s find out what we learned about them, and the general state of the roster, during the Patriots’ 24-21 victory . Behren Morton does it all Rookie Behren Morton had a solid night at quarterback for the Patriots and led the team to two touchdown drives to turn a 14-10 halftime deficit into a 24-21 victory. The first of those drives started late in the third quarter, and the second one proved to be the game-winning rally late in the fourth. Morton himself was poised, and looked confident throwing the ball. If that had been his entire night, it would have been a really good one. Of course, it wasn’t, because he also had three punts with at average 44.3 yards per kick. Bryce Baringer apparently wasn’t feeling great after his second punt in the second period, so they sent Morton in to punt instead, something he hadn’t done since he was in high school (Baringer, meanwhile, remained as the team’s holder). It makes sense for the Patriots to only keep two quarterbacks with the roster looking the way it does, but I could see a world where they decide to keep Morton as their emergency QB3. He looked decent last week, and looked solid this week, even though he didn’t get a single joint practice rep against the Colts or Eagles. I therefore still think it’s a long shot for him to be on the roster on cut down day. A tough receiver decision awaits Mike Vrabel has made it pretty clear that Kyle Williams is going to be a big part of their plans this year. He showed why late in the first half, when he caught a 69-yard touchdown pass from Tommy DeVito. Simply put, if you run man press on him without safety help over the top, he’s a good candidate to take any pass to the house. Having a guy with his releases who possesses natural speed and ball tracking abilities is invaluable to an offense. Sure, he only does one thing, but he does it very well and there’s now enough talent on the roster that he can do that one thing because of the guys ahead of him. Efton Chism, meanwhile, was a demon underneath and caught all four of his targets for 45 yards. He looked slippery with the ball in his hands, and that’s the exact type of thing that Patriots fans hope he can bring to the roster. He might not be a Pro Bowl-caliber player, but he’s proven himself to be a legitimate NFL talent. The Patriots are going to have to make tough decisions on roster cutdown day with the receiver position. I’m starting to think that they end up keeping all seven of their wide receiver and maybe only keep two tight ends, knowing that C.J. Dippre or Tanner Arkin are likely to clear waivers and end up on the practice squad as potential elevation candidates on game day. Nick DeGennaro bursts onto the scene Speaking of looking slippery with the ball in his hands, Nick DeGennaro, the rookie from James Madison, had a great night on Saturday. He caught four passes for 61 yards, and had a 37-yard touchdown to win the game, when he got behind former Patriot Isaiah Bolden for the score. With the receiver room as packed as it is, I can’t imagine he makes the active roster, but he might have secured himself a spot on the practice squad with his performance on Saturday. His ability to work out of the slot and also play on the outside was impressive, and that’s something the team might want to keep around. Cameron Dorner, who finished with two catches and also drew two flags when he beat his guy fairly decisively, also looks like a practice squad option with the way he’s performed all camp. No running room for the offense The Patriots had a tough time running the football on Saturday night. If you take away their longest runs of 20 and 10 yard, respectively, Jam Miller had 10 carries for 16 yards and Lan Larison had eight for 23. I thought they both ran hard but there was nowhere to go most of the night. The offensive line consisted exclusively of backups, yes, but the Eagles didn’t have any starters out there either, so you’d like to think you could have some level of success. That was not the case, unfortunately. RB3 battle is heating up Running back is one of the most intriguing positions on the roster right now because there are four guys vying for what appears to be a single roster spot, and all of them have looked good at times. On Saturday night, Lan Larison looked the best of the bunch. He ran hard between the tackles, including on a 4th-and-1 where he was hit in the backfield but kept the legs churning to bounce off a would-be tackler and move forward for the conversion. Larison looked good catching the ball out of the backfield as well, with his best plays a 28-yard screen pass in the first quarter that saw him dance down the sideline and a really nice pickup on 3rd-and-6 where he had to fight for the last few yards. Jam Miller ran hard as well, even though there wasn’t much available to him. He’s not super explosive, but he has good vision, and gets what is given to him. He’s similar to Terrell Jennings, who looked like the frontrunner for the RB3 spot before he was placed on injured reserve and subsequently released off of it. Hassan Haskins didn’t receive nearly the amount of snaps that the first two got, while JaMichael Hasty looked good catching the ball and pass-protecting, but a fumble in the second half might prevent him from making the roster. Hasty has been on and off the team the last few years, so even if he doesn’t make the 53-man roster or even the practice squad, the Patriots have shown a willingness to bring him back before to help in a pinch. Overall, it feels like Larison might have taken a small lead on Saturday night. We will see how it plays out, but his willingness and ability to run between the tackles and contribute in the passing game could have him on the inside track right now. James Hudson had a bad night Tackle-turned guard James Hudson did not have his best day at the office on Saturday. The veteran offseason signing had multiple holding penalties, and was beat on multiple occasions both in the run and the pass game. The Patriots brought in Greg Van Roten, who seems to be in a good position to make the roster , but the depth on the inside still isn’t great. Hudson might have flexibility to play both tackle and guard, but he doesn’t do either particularly well, so you have to assume that he is not going to make the roster. Chad Muma is not the answer at linebacker The Patriots have been in need of quality linebacker depth for multiple years, which prompted them to bring in a good amount of veteran players to try to address the issue. Chad Muma was one of those players; he arrived in New England as a practice squad pickup from the Colts last December. While he offers an intriguing athletic skillset and vast special teams experience, he hasn’t looked impressive in training camp so far. On Saturday, meanwhile, he had a forgettable night and found himself out-positioned on multiple plays. He then left the game in the late fourth quarter with an injury. Not great. Kindle Vildor makes a bid for a roster spot The Patriots need cornerback depth, and it appears that Kindle Vildor and Karon Prunty are right in the mix for the backup spots. Prunty had a consistent game against the Eagles; He wasn’t flashy, but did a decent job in coverage and in the run game. Vildor, on the other hand, had one of the best drives you will see a corner have. The offseason signing beat the receiver to…
author: Pat Lane

title: 8 winners and losers from Patriots’ preseason win over the Eagles
summary: The New England Patriots continued their preseason Saturday night at Gillette Stadium with a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners QB Behren Morton: Things looked much more comfortable for New England’s rookie quarterback in preseason game No. 2. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Behren Morton #15 of the New England Patriots looks to pass during the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles of a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots continued their preseason Saturday night at Gillette Stadium with a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners QB Behren Morton: Things looked much more comfortable for New England’s rookie quarterback in preseason game No. 2. Morton completed 13-of-17 passes for 129 yards and a touchdown as he led the offense down the field to score the game winning 37-yard touchdown by finding Nick DeGennaro down the right sideline. With punter Bryce Baringer also not feeling great after his first two punts, Morton, a former high school punter, handled those duties. WRs Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams: New England’s second-year wide receiver duo showed their potential as they played throughout the first half. As usual, Chism remained a reliable target underneath and over the middle of the field hauling in all four of his targets for 45 yards — including a 24-yard completion on third-down on a Josh McDaniels staple. Williams’ night was more volatile as he caught just 2-of-6 targets and potentially could have fought harder over the middle of the field. But the speedster made his mark, as he beat Ambry Thomas off the line of scrimmage on a go ball to haul in a 69-yard touchdown. TOMMY DEVITO TO KYLE WILLIAMS FOR 69 YARDS PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QvyMDDZYlC — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 DBs Kindle Vildor and John Saunders Jr.: The Patriots continue to look for cornerback depth behind Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. With Charles Woods sitting with the regulars, Kindle Vildor made his mark Saturday night. The veteran had an interception called back due to a roughing the passer penalty but rebounded by forcing an incompletion then driving downfield to break up a third-down pass. As for Saunders, the safety continued his strong summer. Saunders was on scene to shut down several of Philadelphia’s play-action bootleg concepts and recorded a pass breakup in coverage on second-round rookie tight end Eli Stowers. Saunders play style fits nicely into this defense and the 24-year old is seriously pushing for a roster spot. RB Lan Larison: As the battle for a third running behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson continues, Lan Larison made sure to keep his name in the mix with a strong performance. Larison totaled 33 yards on nine carries while finding the end zone and also added 41 yards on three catches. “I felt like Lan certainly had a good performance, a gritty, tough performance tonight, and did some really good things,” Vrabel said. Losers OG James Hudson III: The Patriots backup offensive line continued to struggle Saturday night. That was led by another tough performance by James Hudson, who recently moved inside to guard, as he allowed a sack and additional pressure while generating two holding penalties on the opening drive. LB Chad Muma: After a rough preseason opener, Muma’s struggles continued on Saturday as the linebacker missed a pair of tackles in the first half. Muma, who suffered an injury last week, later spent time in the blue medical tent before going on to play the whole second half until needing to leave the field again due to injury in the final minute. Linebacker depth is a concern right now as the Patriots also lost Khalil Jacobs Saturday night. Honorable mentions Tommy DeVito had some accuracy issues again but delivered a beautiful touchdown ball to Kyle Williams and made several plays with his legs. UDFA Nick DeGennaro hauled in the game-winning touchdown in the final minute. Making the roster at wide receiver is a no-win situation, but DeGennaro looks primed for a practice squad spot. JaMycal Hasty lost a fumble. Preseason game No. 2 seemed to draw better results for Caleb Lomu in live action. Lomu played 57 snaps at left tackle and gave up one sack failing to pickup a stunt. He seemed to struggle at times in the run game, but the athletic ability is seen in 1-on-1 pass pro situations. Gabe Jacas registered a QB hit as an unblocked rusher off the edge on a zero blitz. He did get flagged for a roughing the passer penalty on a similar play that negated a potential interception. Strong rush and strip sack to ice the game by rookie pass rusher Q Hutchins. Namdi Obiazor recorded an impressive pass breakup on fourth-down in the end zone playing the hands of an Eagles’ pass catcher. Andy Borregales rebounded after a poor preseason debut by making all four of his kicks (one field goal, 41 yards, three extra points). Borregales’ bounce-back came with Julian Ashby back at long snapper. Ashby, who missed last week with an injury, also logged two tackles on kick coverage.
author: Brian Hines

title: Ups and downs from Saints vs. Rams
summary: This week a better name for this piece would probably just be “Downs and downs”, as we saw the New Orleans Saints get completely crushed in their second preseason outing, losing 34-0 to the Los Angeles Rams. It was bad football all around, but hey, maybe it wasn’t all bad? Up: P Ryan Wright Punter […]
full_text: Inglewood, - August 22: Quarterback Spencer Rattler (2) of the New Orleans Saints against the Los Angeles Rams in the second half of a NFL preseason football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Saturday, August 22, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images This week a better name for this piece would probably just be “Downs and downs”, as we saw the New Orleans Saints get completely crushed in their second preseason outing, losing 34-0 to the Los Angeles Rams. It was bad football all around, but hey, maybe it wasn’t all bad? Up: P Ryan Wright Punter Ryan Wright had a better day on Saturday than his first preseason outing, punting four times for an average of 45 yards per punt, including a 58-yarder. More importantly, Wright didn’t have a shanked punt as he did in the team’s first preseason outing against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A mistake so bad you question a bit why New Orleans gave the veteran such a big payday. Despite this, Wright was solid on the day. Up: RB Kendre Miller Can I be honest with you? I’m a Kendre Miller guy. I think he can be a starting running back in this league if he ever figures out how to stay healthy, so as long as he finished this game, he was always going to end up as an “up” for this game. But Miller was impressive in the loss. The numbers don’t show it, with the fourth-year running back logging just 22 yards on six carries. But plenty of strong plays made by Miller were nullified by penalties (more on that later). Miller becomes even more of an up when you look at the injury second-year running back Devin Neal suffered. Neal, who was an iron man in college, has also dealt with a plethora of injuries since the Saints drafted him. With Neal going down and the Saints removing Miller from the game midway through the third quarter, it sure seems Kellen Moore is looking to keep his young running back healthy for the season, presumably to take over RB2 while Alvin Kamara recovers from injury. Wow, that’s a lot of injury talk. Down: Penalties There are too many downs to highlight today, so I’ll mostly focus on the ones that concern me for the regular season. There’s a clear standout from Saturday’s loss, and that’s the sheer amount of penalties. New Orleans was flagged 12 times in the loss for 96 yards worth of penalties. Preseason football won’t be clean. There will be mistakes, there will be turnovers, but what you don’t want to see is an undisciplined team. 12 penalties will lose any team a game, and that form of undisciplined football doesn’t come just from the reserves; that’s sure to stick its head into the starters in the regular season as well. The Saints weren’t clean against the Jaguars either. They were flagged eight times for 66 yards. They are now averaging 10 penalties per game which is absolutely unacceptable and needs to be cleaned up. Down: QB2 There wasn’t really a QB2 battle going into the preseason. Spencer Rattler was the team’s Week 1 starter last season and looked to resume his role as Tyler Shough’s backup going into Week 1 of this season. But that all changed after Zach Wilson lit up the stat sheet in the team’s initial preseason appearance. Wilson pushed the ball down the field and, despite a loss, looked like he could be the favorite to be the team’s QB2. That couldn’t have been more the opposite of what happened on Saturday, however. Wilson was more indecisive, antsy in the pocket, and flat-out inaccurate. Wilson finished the day completing 6-out-of-12 of his pass attempts for 55 yards and an interception. Spencer Rattler was truthfully the better quarterback, especially in his opening drive, but as the game went on, he was quite unimpressive as well. The third-year passer finished the day completing 14-of-his-23 pass attempts for 141 yards and a pick-six. The team needs a solid backup behind Shough and has yet to find that. There is a lack of consistency and too many mistakes. If neither passer can have a solid outing against the Dallas Cowboys to close out the preseason, New Orleans may need to look towards veterans to back up their young quarterback.

title: Pro Football Focus grades from the Giants’ 26-3 victory over the Dolphins
summary: It’s hard to draw conclusions from a game played on a rainy day against a rebuilding team that didn’t even play most of the small number of accomplished starting players they have on their roster. You don’t need Pro Football Focus grades to tell you that the Giants dominated their opponent, the nouveau Miami Dolphins. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 22: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. (3) runs after a catch during the preseason NFL game between the New York Giants and the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s hard to draw conclusions from a game played on a rainy day against a rebuilding team that didn’t even play most of the small number of accomplished starting players they have on their roster. You don’t need Pro Football Focus grades to tell you that the Giants dominated their opponent, the nouveau Miami Dolphins. Also, it’s preseason, so finely parsing individual grades is not of much use. Let’s instead try to get some general impressions, from the grades of course, but also from the playing time. We’ll just look at offense and defense and skip the detailed analysis of position groups. Offense Here are all the offensive players who scored at least 60, PFF’s threshold for adequate play: If I’m J.C. Davis today, nursing my aches and pains from playing 81 snaps at left tackle against Miami…yes, 81…I don’t know if I’m wondering what I did wrong during practice to get punished like this, or I’m thinking that maybe John Harbaugh is intrigued by my play and wanted to see as large a sample as possible, with cutdowns to the final 53 only a week away. I’m guessing the latter. Davis had an outstanding game, grading 89.3 overall with almost identically high pass blocking and run blocking scores. That’s a bit different from last week, when Davis also had an excellent 84.6 pass blocking grade against a tough Vikings defense but an abysmal 41.7 run blocking grade. Elsewhere on the offensive line, Aaron Stinnie, Evan Neal, Joshua Ezeudu, Lucas Patrick, and Marcus Mbow all graded in the 70s. Furthermore, all graded above average in pass blocking except Neal, who graded average. What surprised me about that was this play: Ya pic.twitter.com/Zc5YJ0CG7N — Bobby Skinner (@BobbySkinner_) August 22, 2026 PFF gave Neal responsibility for a sack allowed, and rightly so, because even on the inside, he shows that he doesn’t have the agility to maintain his position against pass rushers. PFF, however, gave Ezeudu no responsibility at all. To me the two should have each gotten half a sack. Ezeudu, playing at right tackle, seemingly consciously passes off his pass rusher to…whom, exactly? Among the skill players, wide receiver Dalen Cambre graded above 70 for the second week in a row, catching all three balls that came his way after catching the only pass thrown to him last week. Cambre likely won’t survive cuts next week given the crowd at WR, although he has played a little on special teams this summer as well, so he might make the roster there or be a practice squad candidate. Among other wide receivers, Darius Slayton had a much needed good game (4 catches in 6 targets for 58 yards), whether to solidify his place on the roster or his place as a trade chip for a 2027 draft pick. Regarding the latter, Calvin Austin, another competitor for a wide receiver roster spot, graded 61.4 with 2 catches in 2 targets for 24 yards. Darnell Mooney, another wide receiver on the roster bubble at this point, missed the game because Harbaugh excused him to be best man at his brother’s wedding. Not showing up above 60 is Odell Beckham Jr. (58.4), who caught two of the four balls that came his way for 17 yards. One of those was a nice play were he worked after the catch to elude tacklers and gain extra yardage in close quarters. Like last week, OBJ also had a play where he put a move on a DB and broke free downfield but was not thrown to. What everyone will remember, though, is the ball he let go through his hands in the end zone, a play that should have been a touchdown. PFF gave him a 29.9 drop grade because of that. Among the running backs, Eric Gray, who did some good things late in the game when no one was paying attention anymore, led with a 70.4 grade. Devin Singletary, who had a nice game and seems to be solidifying a spot on the roster, had a 64.7 grade. Tyrone Tracy, though, graded an ugly 40.9 because of his unforced fumble. Defense Here are all players who scored at least 60 on defense in the game: This is where PFF grades can understandably be frustrating to a lot of you. Dru Phillips led all Giants defenders with an outrageously good 96.3 grade. I’m sure that many of you can think only of the 30-yard reception that he surrendered, when he was in position to break up the pass but never looked back and let the receiver catch the ball despite putting a hand up: Cam Miller launches it to Kevin Coleman Jr.! NYGvsMIA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vUaXaumlY7 — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 However, on two of the other of his total six plays yesterday, he forced fumbles that the Giants recovered. Here’s one of them: I love how Dru Phillips responded to the slot-fade he surrendered. Phillips with back-to-back impact plays to shut down the Dolphins offense. Phillips' physical nature is one thing that can't be denied. pic.twitter.com/cgUPWZmk9E — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 22, 2026 Dennard Wilson will have to find ways to put Phillips in position to maximize his skills near the line of scrimmage while limiting his obvious vulnerability as a pass defender downfield. Returning to the overall defense grades, take a good look, BBVers. It may be a long time before you ever see the top six defense grades all going to defensive backs again. Tyler Nubin (90.3) had his second consecutive outstanding pre-season game. Maybe we’ll even see an interception from him this year? Likewise, Deonte Banks, after a bad game in coverage vs. Minnesota, bounced back with an excellent 85.3 defense grade vs. Miami. Finally, Greg Newsome II, in his first action as a Giant, had a very good 79.9 score. Beau Brade (79.0) and Nic Jones (75.5) also had a very good game. Elsewhere, Arvell Reese had another strong game (75.8), as did less-noticed outside linebacker Caleb Murphy (75.4) and linebacker Micah McFadden (74.5). Chauncey Golston (73.0) had his second consecutive good game; he’s someone to keep an eye on this year as a possible prime beneficiary of the switch in defensive coordinators. Among the 2026 draftees, Jack Kelly was more quiet than in his debut last week, but had a solid 63.7 grade, while Bobby Jamison-Travis (58.9) had a sack. At the other end of the spectrum, Darius Alexander (39.7) was the lowest-graded Giants defender. Alexander had a QB hit and a hurry in the pass rush but an abysmal 22.9 tackling grade with one missed tackle. The clock is starting to tick on Alexander to show that he can become a complete interior defensive lineman and not just a situational player.
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: NY Giants injury updates: Josh Ezeudu ‘OK’, Sisi Mauigoa, Colton Hood to practice
summary: The New York Giants came out of Saturday’s preseason game against the Miami Dolphins largely unscathed in terms of injuries. That has been the case throughout training camp. The Giants have had bumps and bruises throughout a grueling summer, and have had a handful of players miss some practice time. Yet, there have been no […]
full_text: Josh Ezeudu | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The New York Giants came out of Saturday’s preseason game against the Miami Dolphins largely unscathed in terms of injuries. That has been the case throughout training camp. The Giants have had bumps and bruises throughout a grueling summer, and have had a handful of players miss some practice time. Yet, there have been no major season-changing injuries. “We got out of it without anything major, which is a great accomplishment,” Harbaugh said. “You go down there [Miami] in two really intense days, two intense practices in three days, and you want to come through it healthy. “We’ve done that. We’ve had a great camp. Knock on wood.” You might say Harbaugh was tempting fate, but he had more to say about injuries, or the lack thereof. “We’ve had a great camp so far with injuries. We’ve had very few soft tissue injuries. I mean, almost really none, nothing of consequence, nothing serious that was in just a couple days,” Harbaugh said. “Nothing major so far. “People are probably saying, don’t say anything, don’t say anything. I’m not superstitious, but as Michael said in ‘The Office,’ I am a little stitious, so I’ll just have to leave it at that.” Josh Ezeudu ‘OK’ The one player who looked like he might have suffered a noteworthy injury on Saturday was offensive lineman Josh Ezeudu , who struggled off the field after going down in the second half. Harbaugh said Ezeudu got kicked in the back of the leg, and will be “OK”. “Not going to be any kind of a long-term injury,” Harbaugh said. “So a couple days, day-to-day type of deal. “Hopefully he’ll be playing on Friday night [against the New York Jets].” Ezeudu, who has spent most of his time at tackle in recent seasons after being drafted as a guard, has increasingly been used at right guard this summer. He appears to have a path to making the 53-man roster due to his versatility. “The position flex is the idea. You may have noticed he went back out to tackle in the fourth quarter, so the ability for him to play both guard and tackle, particularly on the right side, would be helpful for us, and that’s our thought,” Harbaugh said. “He’s kind of getting to the point now where we feel like he could swing, right tackle, right guard.” Harbaugh added that the Giants are “kind of keeping him off the left side and just keeping him to the right side, and that helps a little bit with some of the techniques.” “It’s like a hitter. He’s not a switch hitter right now on both sides,” Harbaugh said. “But he is playing both the inside position and the outside position, so we think he’s ready for it, that he can handle it, and that gives us some position flexibility as a backup.” Francis Mauigoa, Colton Hood to return Harbaugh said that rookies Sisi Mauigoa and Colton Hood will return to practice this week. Mauigoa, the starting right guard suffered a stinger in Thursday’s joint practice against the Dolphins and did not play in Saturday’s preseason game. Hood, competing for time at cornerback, did not practice or play in Miami. Malik Nabers and the red jersey Harbaugh said that it is “a possibility” that Malik Nabers will practice without the red, non-contact jersey at some point this week. “I don’t think it’s a necessity this week,” Harbaugh said. “We’re still three weeks out from the game, the first game and then after that, but we’ll see where he’s at this week. We’ll see how he feels tomorrow.”
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants rookies impress  against the Miami Dolphins
summary: The New York Giants didn’t play many of their starters on Saturday against the Miami Dolphins following a tough joint practice on Thursday. However, they still managed to carry the dominance from the practice over into the game, and most of the Giants’ rookies got at least a little action. Right guard Sisi Mauigoa didn’t […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese. | Getty Images The New York Giants didn’t play many of their starters on Saturday against the Miami Dolphins following a tough joint practice on Thursday. However, they still managed to carry the dominance from the practice over into the game, and most of the Giants’ rookies got at least a little action. Right guard Sisi Mauigoa didn’t play, nor did cornerback Colton Hood. Mauigoa is dealing with a stinger suffered in the joint practice with the Dolphins, and he likely wouldn’t have played anyway. Hood was reportedly dealing with an undisclosed injury earlier in the week, but took part in the joint practices with the Dolphins. The Giants could have been sparing him the reps after a tough practice, or they have a significantly different opinion of his play against the Minnesota Vikings than did Pro Football Focus. I also wanted to get another look at UDFA tackle Ryan Schernecke after a promising performance against the Vikings. However, the All-22 tape the NFL provides cuts out before the fourth quarter at the time of writing. It’s frustrating, but I didn’t want to delay this piece waiting on the NFL. So other than those players, let’s dive into the tape and see how the Giants’ rookies did in their second taste of NFL action. LB Arvell Reese Reese was on the field for all of 11 plays against the Dolphins. It’s a small sample size, but also a continuation of the play we saw from Reese against the Vikings. The first play of the game saw him win his gap against a power run concept, blow up the fullback, then continue to assist on Chauncey Golston’s tackle. The second snap had him defend the running back, taking an accurate first step on (what looked like) an outsize zone run, only to quickly recognize the play-action boot, disengage, and defend the rollout. We really didn’t need to see all that much from Reese to back up what he did last week. He’s explosive, agile, processes quickly, and hits like a truck. WR Malachi Fields The Giants’ third-round pick also played 11 snaps, eight of which came on offense and three on special teams. Normally we use the phrase “quicker than fast” to describe slot receivers — guys like Wes Welker or Victor Cruz spring to mind — but that might be a perfect description for Fields. He is not a fast receiver, but he is quicker than any receiver with his frame has a right to be. It’s consistently impressive how easily he’s able drop his hips and change direction without having to throttle down. It’s notable, then, that the Giants used Fields as a power slot on occasion. That versatility could give the Giants some interesting looks and options for how they deploy their offense. Fields is showing a developing understanding of how to use his frame to leverage defenders before using his quickness to cut and uncover. Likewise, he seems to be developing an understanding of how his routes fit into the larger passing concept. Fields isn’t a route technician just yet, but he could become a very interesting player as that aspect of his game develops. Interestingly, the Giants used Fields on punt teams to rush the opposing punter. DT Bobby Jamison-Travis I think it’s a mark of where Jamison-Travis lands on the depth chart that he too only played 11 snaps (including one play nullified by penalty). Granted, he played into the fourth quarter, but he played as many snaps as the other rookies who we know figure heavily into the Giants’ plans for the season. Like Reese, it really didn’t take that many snaps to reaffirm what we saw on tape from Jamison-Travis in the first preseason game. He is a powerful young man, who knows how to use his frame and strength to execute an unglamorous job. He does an excellent job of firing his hands into blockers’ chest plates, pressing them to establish leverage, and creating piles on the offensive interior. Even his sack came because his strength allowed him to walk the center into the backfield and discard him as the quarterback tried to scramble. OL J.C. Davis Davis was on the field for an incredible 89 plays against the Dolphins, including se ven special teams plays (field goals and extra point attempts) and plays that were nullified by penalty. It was a mixed bag for the young offensive tackle, and he definitely came away with some things to work on as well as things the coaches will love. He definitely needs to continue to hone his technique as a blocker. Davis was pretty consistently lunging at defenders, getting his chest out over his feet and bending at the hips more than his knees. That didn’t hurt him too badly against the Dolphins, but there were enough plays where he was unable to establish leverage or anchor that it could have been ugly against more explosive pass rushers. Likewise, he also needs to improve his hand usage and try to consistently gain control of his opponents’ chest plates. That said, Davis has solid feet and is a pretty smooth mover when he’s balanced. He also has enough play strength and is surprisingly fast when blocking in space. Davis also plays with some really impressive competitive toughness to hustle after plays and keep giving effort despite playing almost a game and a half worth of snaps. LB Jack Kelly Kelly played 32 snaps against the Dolphins, 20 of which came on defense and the other 12 were on special teams. Kelly is emerging as a core special teams player on the kick off, punting, field goal and coverage teams. Kelly wasn’t exactly a starter for the Giants against the Dolphins, but his first defensive snap came in relief of Arvell Reese with 4:08 left in the first quarter. Overall, Kelly has been impressive — and not just for a sixth rounder. He generally processes quickly and accurately, and has enough athleticism to cover some serious ground at the second level. The Giants have given Kelly a pretty big role on the field, using him in coverage, as a pass rusher, and playing downhill in run defense. He’s typically executed well, although there have been some instances where he’s overcommitted and taken himself out of the play. He bit hard on misdirection a couple times against the Dolphins, which created some voids Miami was able to exploit. Aggressive play is certainly a forgivable sin for a rookie linebacker, though it definitely should be a teaching point going forward. Likewise, he does need to get more consistent in playing with good leverage when he takes on blockers. K Dominic Zvada There isn’t too much to say about Zvada here. He performed well when on the field for kick-offs, extra points, and field goals. He clearly has a very strong leg and the operation between he, long-snapper Ben Mann, and holder Jordan Stout is very crisp. Zvada also appears to have a very compact kicking motion on kick-offs, which should make his kicks consistent and repeatable. He does a good job of delivering the ball in the back of the landing zone, similar to a golfer dropping a chip shot softly onto the green. It would have been nice to see Zvada attempt a longer field goal, but there’s enough evidence that he has plenty of leg and is an accurate kicker.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants-Dolphins ‘things I think’: Difficult roster decisions loom
summary: Head coach John Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen face some excruciatingly difficult decisions when it comes to setting the New York Giants’ season-opening 53-man roster. That is the most important ‘thing I think’ after Saturday’s one-sided 26-3 victory over the Miami Dolphins. “There’s a lot of guys fighting for jobs on this team,” Harbaugh […]
full_text: Will Odell Beckham Jr. earn a spot on the Giants’ 53-man roster? | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Head coach John Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen face some excruciatingly difficult decisions when it comes to setting the New York Giants’ season-opening 53-man roster. That is the most important ‘thing I think’ after Saturday’s one-sided 26-3 victory over the Miami Dolphins. “There’s a lot of guys fighting for jobs on this team,” Harbaugh said after the game. “And I thought they came out and they made a point to try to make their case. And they did a good job of it.” Here is a look at five of the places where decisions need to be made. Running back This really becomes the Tyrone Tracy question. The addition of Najee Harris has changed the equation. Do the Giants have room to keep five running backs, including fullback Patrick Ricard ? Harris, Cam Skattebo , and Ricard are staying. In my view, so is Devin Singletary . The veteran back just keeps making plays, and his reliability is clearly something Harbaugh appreciates. Here is what Harbaugh said about Singletary after he gained 40 yards on eight carries, including a 13-yard touchdown run, Saturday: “He did great. He played like he always plays. He is one of the most consistent players you’re ever going to see.” Which leads us to Tracy. He is a good player. Back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons from scrimmage are nothing to sneeze at. He did not compile those seasons for Harbaugh, though. What he has done for Harbaugh is make huge mistakes in two straight games. No matter what he did for Brian Daboll the past two seasons, if Harbaugh doesn’t trust him to keep Jaxson Dart healthy or hold on to the ball, how or why would he use him? I believe Tracy should stay. He is a good back. What, though, if the Giants look at their roster and think five backs is one too many? Could they swing a deal for Tracy like the one they did for Daniel Faalele? Wide receiver Unless they have injuries we don’t know about, the way to take Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios not dressing for Saturday’s game is that their roster spots are secure. That means six wide receivers — Malik Nabers , Mooney, Berrios, Malachi Fields , Calvin Austin, Darius Slayton — have roster spots. Can the Giants find room for a seventh? And, would that seventh be the sentimental choice, Odell Beckham Jr. , or the special teams ace, Dalen Cambre ? There are arguments for both. Beckham can still get open, but can’t play special teams and would likely be the last receiver on the depth chart. Cambre is a special teams first player, but keeps showing he can be useful if needed as a receiver. Offensive line How many offensive linemen can the Giants keep? And, which ones should be the backups? One player who has earned a spot is Josh Ezeudu . Of course, this happened in the second half on Saturday so Ezeudu’s health is now a question we have to ask Harbaugh about when he holds a call with media Sunday afternoon: Josh Ezeudu banged up and limping off pic.twitter.com/gjwrvqn9oX — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) August 22, 2026 Until recently, I felt rookie sixth-round pick J.C. Davis was headed to the practice squad. Now? After he played 81 snaps, and played them well, at left tackle against the Dolphins there is no chance the Giants get him through waivers to the practice squad. He has to be on the 53-man roster. Marcus Mbow , Aaron Stinnie , and Lucas Patrick also should have roster spots. Can the Giants keep 10 offensive linemen? I’m not sure how. Jake Kubas has played well in two preseason games. You can even make a case that Evan Neal has looked like a competent NFL guard, and deserves consideration. Cornerback The cornerback position isn’t so much about who makes the team. Paulson Adebo , Greg Newsome , Deonte Banks , Dru Phillips , Colton Hood , and Art Green seem secure. Could 2025 seventh-round pick Korie Black make the team as a seventh cornerback? Maybe. The real question comes down to who lines up against receivers from the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1? Phillips is the nickel cornerback, with occasional help from safety Ar’Darius Washington . As of yet, though, there isn’t a clear answer about how the Giants will decide amongst Adebo, Newsome, Banks, and Hood. I believe Adebo and Newsome emerge as the starters Week 1, but we’ll see. Defensive line Chauncey Golston has emerged as a starter in the base defense because he is a more reliable run defender than Darius Alexander . Golston, Alexander, D.J. Reader , and Shelby Harris should occupy four roster spots. Leki Fotu has had a good summer, and might have the inside track on a roster spot. Josh Topou was impressive against the Minnesota Vikings. Zacch Pickens and sixth-round pick Bobby Jamison-Travis were impactful Saturday against the Dolphins. There aren’t enough roster spots for eight interior defensive linemen.
author: Ed Valentine

title: Giants-Dolphins winners and losers: Which players helped themselves, and which did not
summary: The New York Giants had an easy time manhandling the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, winning 26-3. Let’s review the game in our traditional ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Darius Slayton — Recovering from double sports hernia surgery, Slayton has had a quiet summer. He had a loud first half, with four catches […]
full_text: Devin Singletary runs for a touchdown Saturday against the Miami Dolphins. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants had an easy time manhandling the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, winning 26-3. Let’s review the game in our traditional ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Darius Slayton — Recovering from double sports hernia surgery, Slayton has had a quiet summer. He had a loud first half, with four catches for 58 yards. He set up the Giants’ first touchdown with a 29-yard catch-and-run on a third-and-5. Jameis Winston — The Giants’ backup quarterback played the entire first half. He went 15 of 21 for 150 yards, ran for an 11-yard score, and led a nice two-minute drive for a field goal. Good work! Devin Singletary — The eighth-year running back doesn’t get anywhere in a hurry. He isn’t exactly a burner. He does, though, keep on making plays and being dependable. John Harbaugh will like both of those things. Singletary made a terrific cutback on his 13-yard touchdown run, and finished with 40 yards rushing on eight carries. Devin Singletary bounces it outside and takes it in for the @Giants TD! NYGvsMIA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cNcRnNMKwo — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 The secondary — I made this a blanket ‘Kudos’ for many of the guys who played in the first half. Greg Newsome had a pass defensed and was aggressive in run support. Deonte Banks was excellent. He was sticky in coverage, and had two passes defensed. He also made an an excellent, aggressive run stop. That would not have happened a year ago. Tyler Nubin missed a tackle on the opening kickoff, but was solid defensively. He had a pass defensed, continuing his tendency this summer of getting his hands on the ball more often. Early Pro Football Focus grades gave him an elite 90.4 grade. Dru Phillips gave up a 30-yard catch (and committed pass interference on the play), but responded with run stops and forced fumbles on his next two plays. I can’t point to a specific play, but Paulson Adebo started and also appeared to play well. Bobby Jamison-Travis — The rookie sixth-round pick needed a game in which he made a couple of plays, and he delivered one on Saturday. He got a sack, and even showed us that there is a new No. 97 sack dance in town: New celly alert 🍽️ pic.twitter.com/26uh4LXgfp — New York Giants (@Giants) August 22, 2026 J.C. Davis — The rookie sixth-round pick went the distance at left tackle in a performance that probably solidified a spot for him on the 53-man roster. In early grades from PFF, Davis scored an 86.6, best among offensive players. Davis played 81 total snaps and allowed just one pressure. Offensive line overall — Giants’ quarterbacks were sacked only once, and there were holes for all of the backs to run through. Well, except for poor Damon Bankston and his seven carries for 5 yards at the end of the game. Dare I say that there may actually be depth on the line. The Giants must think so, since they traded Daniel Faalele a few days ago. Dalen Cambre — The second-year wide receiver/special teamer did not enter the game until the second half. When he got on the field, he made the most of it. Cambre made the tackle on the opening kickoff of the second half, and had three catches in three targets for 26 yards. More importantly, all three of Cambre’s catches resulted in first downs. On third-and-7, he caught an 8-yard pass from Brandon Allen. On third-and-8, Cambre caught a 9-yard pass from Allen. On yet another third-and-8, Cambre caught a 9-yard pass from Jake Haener. Calvin Austin — Austin had a 21-yard rush, two receptions for 24 yards, and two punt returns for 29 yards. He will help the Giants in 2026. Related coverage What did we learn from the Giants’ 26-3 win over the Miami Dolphins? Giants-Dolphins instant grades: Lopsided victory leads to high marks Giants dominate Miami Dolphins in 26-3 victory Wet Willies to … Tyrone Tracy — Two preseason games, two major gaffes for Tracy. In Week 1 against the Minensota Vikings, he missed a blitz pickup resulting in a huge hit on quarterback Jaxson Dart. On Saturday, after runs of 11 and 12 yards, an untouched Tracy fumbled away a scoring opportunity. Tracy probably also fumbled away playing time with Najee Harris on the roster, and Singletary looking spry. Did he fumble away a roster spot? The miscues are unfortunate, because Tracy can be a plus in both the run and pass games. This, though, is a new coaching staff and they will go by what they are seeing with their own eyes. Darius Alexander — The second-year defensive tackle had a quarterback hit, but his overall play left a lot to be desired. His early 33.8 PFF grade was the lowest of any Giants’ defender. Alexander has been in both preseason games in the third quarter, and it is mostly because the Giants need better run defense from the 2025 third-round pick. There is a reason why Chauncey Golston has been starting on the defensive line. Maybe I was also influenced by the number of times Carl Banks spoke during the broadcast about Alexander needing to give the Giants more. Kwillies to … Odell Beckham Jr. — While fans, and even Harbaugh, are rooting for Beckham, his chance of making the season-opening 53-man roster remains murky. Yes, he can still get open. Yes, he had a 12-yard catch. Two catches for 17 yards and a dropped touchdown pass aren’t going to cut it, though. Not when the wide receiver room is as deep as it is, and other guys are making plays. You just can’t miss chances to make impact plays when you are fighting for a roster spot.

title: Eagles News: “Tanner McKee has to be the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Andy Dalton just isn’t very good.”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Instant Observations: McKee outplays Dalton in Eagles’ preseason loss – NBCSPSo much for that quarterback competition. If this game was any indication, Tanner McKee has to be the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Andy Dalton just isn’t very good. He had a couple nice completions to […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles makes a pass in the second quarter against the New England Patriots during a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Instant Observations: McKee outplays Dalton in Eagles’ preseason loss – NBCSP So much for that quarterback competition. If this game was any indication, Tanner McKee has to be the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Andy Dalton just isn’t very good. He had a couple nice completions to Darius Cooper Saturday night – 25 yards out to midfield on a 2nd-and-7 and 13 yards to Cooper on a 4th-and-1 on the Eagles’ first touchdown drive. But after an ineffective 3-for-6 for 20 yards against the Ravens last week, he finished 3-for-10 for 44 yards in New England, with all his completions going to Cooper. That leaves him 6-for-16 for 64 yards on nine drives this preseason with a miserable passer rating of 50.0. Dalton hasn’t been terrible in practice, but in the two games he just hasn’t brought any juice to the offense and has looked all of his 38 years. Tanner McKee needs to be the Eagles’ No. 2 QB, and he was sharp and decisive Saturday, going 16-for-22 for 173 yards with two touchdown passes, no interceptions and a 125.8 passer rating before giving way to rookie Cole Payton with 57 seconds left. And remember, Dalton was out there with the 2’s and McKee mainly with the 3’s. Maybe Howie can find a taker for Dalton for a bottom of the draft pick, but McKee needs to be Jalen Hurts’ backup. Eagles vs. Patriots preseason: The good, the bad, and the ugly – BGN Quarterback Tanner McKee completing 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns, and in doing so,may have become the leader in the backup race, considering Andy Dalton has not looked good at all in two preseason games. Tanner McKee outperforms Andy Dalton in the Eagles’ confounding backup QB competition — will it matter? – Inquirer Tanner McKee outplayed Andy Dalton despite having to work with the Eagles’ mostly third-string offensive line and skill position players. Nick Sirianni may claim that there has been a fair competition for the No. 2 quarterback spot, and that Dalton has only started both preseason games because he has more experience. But McKee hasn’t had the benefit of performing with players who will actually make the Eagles’ 53-man roster. And yet, he looked like a far more viable backup to Jalen Hurts than Dalton did in the Eagles’ 24-21 loss to the New England Patriots on Saturday night. McKee wasn’t without his faults. He missed throws from the pocket and struggled at times when pressured. But it is worth questioning how Dalton could end up winning the job, let alone entice some quarterback-needy team into trading for him. There’s still another preseason game and a week until the roster deadline, but time is running out on the 38-year-old veteran. Tanner McKee makes case for Eagles’ No. 2 QB, Joshua Weru pushes for roster spot – The Athletic There are a few ways to look at this. Perhaps the Eagles are showcasing him to the league. I still think Dalton would be more of a trade chip one week before the season because of his experience. Perhaps the Eagles wanted to give McKee confidence after the way last week went. Although if that were the case, I’d think they would play McKee with the second-team offensive line (a group that played well, as Brooks Kubena wrote). The Eagles might have wanted to put pressure on McKee this summer after how they approached last summer. Head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters after the game that McKee needed more work than Dalton because of the experience difference. I still can’t imagine the summer has gone the way the Eagles would have wanted at the position. It was a curious approach given how they’ve viewed McKee in recent years (and the initial messaging that the Dalton trade had nothing to do with McKee), but this game was a step in the right direction. Compared to how Dalton played (3-for-10 for 44 yards on Saturday; 6-for-16 for 64 yards in the preseason), it’s harder to make a Dalton argument. Dalton has far more experience, including big-game experience. And as Sean Mannion could tell you, there’s more to a No. 2 quarterback’s role than how he plays in relief. Dalton’s background is valuable in the quarterback room. But Howie Roseman would be keen to tell you that no organization has benefited more from the backup quarterback than the Eagles. If Jalen Hurts goes down, which quarterback gives them a better chance to win games? I still think it’s McKee. The Eagles haven’t treated it as such this summer, but it looked that way Saturday. Nick Sirianni: “It’s still a competition” between Andy Dalton, Tanner McKee for QB2 – PFT As the Browns and Raiders work through their starting quarterbacks for Week 1, the Eagles are still trying to figure out their QB2. After Saturday’s preseason game between Philadelphia and New England, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said “it’s still a competition” between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee. “I think both the guys are battling, and I’m really confident in both of the guys,” Sirianni told reporters after the game. “We’ll see where that goes.” Dalton has been getting first dibs during the preseason games, but that’s apparently not a tipping of Sirianni’s hand. “The reason Andy is going in first — in practice they’re still rotating,” Sirianni said. “Andy is going in first because he’s not going to play as much as Tanner because he has had more experience and he has more experience within this type of system, and Tanner needs to continue to play there because I think you saw the improvements there from Tanner. So we got to continue to give both of them opportunities within practice and potentially games.” 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis – ESPN Eagles: Who will back up QB Jalen Hurts this season? Andy Dalton has started both preseason games — seemingly an indication that he is ahead in the competition with Tanner McKee to be Hurts’ backup, despite the two splitting practice reps with the second team this summer. Dalton has not fared well in those games, however, going 3-of-10 for 44 yards against the Patriots and 3-of-6 for 20 yards versus the Baltimore Ravens. McKee tossed two touchdown passes against New England and was more efficient overall. But neither QB has clearly separated from the other, making for an interesting decision as the time nears to trim the roster to 53. Three trades that make sense for the Eagles – PhillyVoice Eagles QB Andy Dalton to the Patriots for WR Mack Hollins. Dalton had a decent couple of days in joint practices in Foxboro (though a poor game performance), and he would make some sense for the Patriots, seeing as their current QB2 is somehow Tommy DeVito. The Pats will have tape of Dalton from those practices, and he might be a valuable off-the-field sounding board for the young and talented Drake Maye. The Patriots are deep at receiver after trading for A.J. Brown and spending big money on WR2 Romeo Doubs. They also have a nice little slot receiver in Demario Douglas, a 2025 third-round pick in Kyle Williams, and a couple of backups with past modest production in Kayshon Boutte and Mack Hollins. Boutte has been the subject of trade speculation for the entire offseason, but I think the player who makes more sense for the Eagles is Hollins, who the Eagles selected in the fourth round of the 2017 draft. The Eagles cut Hollins during his third year with the team, and he was picked up by Miami, where he played out the rest of the 2019 season, plus two more seasons. He then played one year each with the Raiders, Falcons, Bills, and Patriots. Eagles Lose Late to NE, 24-21 – Iggles Blitz The Eagles struggled a week ago. They were much better vs New England, but still fell after blowing a late lead. The outcome isn’t as important as the fact the…

title: Eagles vs. Patriots preseason: The good, the bad, and the ugly
summary: This was a lot better, certainly light years healthier in comparison to how dismal the Eagles’ first dress rehearsal looked last week in Baltimore.
