full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: The New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles line up against each other during the first half of the preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images This was a lot better, certainly light years healthier in comparison to how dismal the Eagles’ first dress rehearsal looked last week in Baltimore. This time, the Eagles’s backups resembled somewhat of an NFL team, despite a 24-21 loss to the defending AFC champion New England Patriots on Saturday night at Gillette Stadium. The execution was tighter, the discipline was improved, and there were a lot of positives. What could haunt the Eagles is a leaky safety position that looks like it might not get any help from the twos or threes. Andrew Mukuba showed glimmers of what he could be in his rookie season last year, and he also made some glaring rookie mistakes, which is expected. Marcus Epps is also a question, with very little help coming from safeties J.T. Gray and Shaun Wade, who probably won’t make the team, and neither will cornerbacks Isaiah Bolden and Ambry Thomas, by the way they played. What the Eagles did receive were good performances by Tanner McKee, Ty Robinson, Will Shipley, Willie Lampkin, Drew Kendall, Markel Bell, and running back Carson Steele. There was a some ugly, some bad and some encouraging good in the Eagles’ 24-21 loss to the New England Patriots. The Good Center Willie Lampkin is stubby, has a belly, and is an earth mover. On Will Shipley’s 18-yard run in the first quarter, Lampkin hooked the Patriots’ nose tackle, giving Shipley a free lane down the sideline. He had a major push in getting Shipley into the end zone early in the second quarter. Cornerback Kelee Ringo almost had a pick six on the second play of the game, breaking on the play at the right time, but as with Ringo, something good is associated with something bad. The ball went right through his hands. Defensive tackle Gabe Hall working through a double team to make a tackle on the Patriots’ opening drive, stuffing the middle at midfield. Linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. played well again. He finished with a team-high five tackles by halftime, three solo, with one sack on the Patriots’ second drive. On second-and-10, Trotter went bolting through the line and took down Tommy DeVito for a four-yard sack, forcing as third-and-14. The Eagles may have a pleasant dilemma on their hands with depth at linebacker with Trotter, Zack Baun, Jihaad Campbell, Jalyx Hunt and Trotter. Last week, he had five tackles, two solo, and a sack—again, all in the first half. He is pushing for a starting role. Running back Will Shipley looked good again, rushing for 56 yards on 11 carries and a touchdown, after rushing for 22 yards on 7 carries last week in what was an otherwise overall bad team performance against Baltimore. Receiver Darius Cooper looked good, redeeming himself after a bad start last week. Cooper had a team-high three catches for 44 yards by halftime. He happened to be the only receiver Andy Dalton connected with on Dalton’s 10 passes. On fourth-and-one, Cooper made a 13-yard reception coming across the middle at the New England 27. The drive led to the Eagles’ first score. Defensive tackle Ty Robinson is impactful again. He continues to impress.Against the Ravens last week,he had two tackles, one tackle for loss, a quarterback hit, and a sack in the first quarter. Against the Pats, he broke through a double team midway in the second quarter and came up with a nine-yard sack on a third-and-seven that forced the Pats to punt. He had another sack late in the first half for a 12-yard sack that forced a third-and-22. He had three tackles in the first half, two for sacks for minus-21 yards. He has three sacks in two games. The Eagles’ second drive. Shipley punched it in on a 13-play, 77-yard drive. The Eagles converted a fourth down and a third down. The Eagles were 0 for 9 on third-down conversions last week against Baltimore. Britain Covey’s zigzag 14-yard TD reception from Tanner McKee to close the first half. The first half. The Eagles went into halftime leading 14-10.They had 12 first downs, a major jump from the six first downs that they had the whole game against Baltimore last week, and they gained 158 totals yards—just one shy of what they totaled the entire game against the Ravens. The bottom line is, they looked and played more prepared than they were a week ago. The offensive moved the Patriots for 71 yards rushing. Coaching box Sean Mannion looked better than sideline Sean Mannion last week. The Eagles mixed it up, using the screen game, setting the Patriots off balance and causing them to guess. He was not afraid to run plays again that worked. It was a nice confidence boost for the first-time offensive coordinator. Carson Steele may not make the Eagles, but he may make one team in the NFL. He caught six passes on seven targets—one for 28 yards—for 84 yards and a touchdown, while rushing for 33 yards on 12 carries. Edge rusher Joshua Weru’s third-quarter sack for minus-seven yards on a third-and-seven play that forced a Patriots’ punt. It was the first sack for the 22-year-old from Kenya. Linebacker Chance Campbell got a chance to get some good film, with seven tackles, six solo, but when the four-year NFL veteran was in, the Patriots rolled down the field for a 17-14 lead early in the fourth quarter. Uar Bernard, the hulking, sculpted 6-foot-4, 300-pound curiosity from Nigeria, made his first two tackles, sliding down the line of scrimmage to make a couple of plays in the fourth quarter.Bernard shows promise, considered he never played American football until this stage of his life. Quarterback Tanner McKee completing 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns , and in doing so,may have become the leader in the backup race, considering Andy Dalton has not looked good at all in two preseason games. The Bad Back-up quarterback Andy Dalton has been upgraded from ugly to just bad. He overthrew open receivers on the first drive and had to rely on Shipley and the offensive line to move the ball on the Eagles’ scoring drive. His 39,793 career passing yards are behind him. You would figure a veteran like him would have a natural veteran touch. He doesn’t. He finished 3 of 10 for 44 yards. It’s not just a matter of timing. Most of his throws are off. Ringo getting called for illegal contact in the second quarter. Ringo gets caught putting his hands on receivers more than he should. Safety J.T. Gray’s dropped interception with 2:41 to play. The discarded special team Pro Bowler with the New Orleans has to finish plays like that to continue to playing in the NFL. Safety Shaun Wade finished with a team-high 10 tackles, six solo, but he almost gave up a touchdown with 1:28 to play, if the pass was not overthrown, and Pats’ receiver Tajhaun Palmer did not lose track of the ball and stopped running on the route. Then, Wade got burned by Kyle Dixon on a fourth-and-one at the Eagles’ 37 for a first down. New England spotted its pigeon in the last minute and his name was Shaun Wade. The Ugly Cornerback Isaiah Bolden getting toasted by Pats’ receiver Nick DeGennaro for a 37-yard touchdown pass with :57 left. Again, it’s not away to make an NFL team, having a receiver run by you with the game on the line. Bolden may have thought he was going to get help, but it was a wrong assumption—and probably a costly one for Bolden. Cornerback Ambry Thomas getting beat—and beat bad—on Tommy DeVito’s 69-yard, second-quarter touchdown pass. DeVito’s rainbow dropped right into the hands of the waiting hands of Kyle Williams. title: Five Steelers on the roster bubble ahead of preseason finale
summary: With just one more preseason game on the slate, the Pittsburgh Steelers will close out exhibition play this Thursday against the Buffalo Bills. Through two games, several notable veterans find themselves on the brink of making the roster or being let go. These five names will be ones to highlight over the next week as […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Kaleb Johnson #20 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images With just one more preseason game on the slate, the Pittsburgh Steelers will close out exhibition play this Thursday against the Buffalo Bills. Through two games, several notable veterans find themselves on the brink of making the roster or being let go. These five names will be ones to highlight over the next week as potential cuts. QB Will Howard Howard is coming off a poor performance against the New York Jets , throwing two interceptions on 10-of-15 passing in his first start. Considering Mike McCarthy gave Mason Rudolph the night off, his spot on the roster feels all but secured. It’s rare to see a team keep four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, and McCarthy has never done so. With Howard’s performance, combined with the performance of Drew Allar through two games, as well as where the Steelers drafted him, Howard is certainly first in line to be let go should Pittsburgh opt to release a quarterback. RB Kaleb Johnson Johnson was given a far greater workload against the Jets, getting 12 total touches on offense compared to just two in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. The big caveat with Johnson remains his lack of usage on special teams. Will the Steelers keep him over Lew Nichols or Travis Homer, or will they let go of Johnson and opt to keep the other reserve backs? After a lackluster rookie season, his name is certainly one to watch. WR Roman Wilson This one may surprise some after the camp Wilson had, but through the first two preseason games, he’s shown the same concerning characteristics that have plagued him through the first two seasons of his career. On the second of Howard’s interceptions, he drifted too far up field, which made it easier for Samuel Womack to pick off the throw. Wilson has popped in camp for two consecutive seasons now. I’d like to see him get extended playing time and show some real pop agains the Bills on Thursday. If he doesn’t, Gabe Davis or Curtis Samuel could be better options to be the WR4 on the depth chart. OT Broderick Jones Jones put some rough play on tape against the Jets. He allowed a sack on Howard as David Bailey just plowed through him to get outside leverage. He also allowed a sack on Drew Allar late in the second half. Jones is, of course, coming off a neck injury and went without getting practice reps in during the spring. It was a surprise that he was cleared for the start of training camp. With the injury to Max Iheanachor, the Steelers may want to hold onto Jones for depth purposes, but his play has been less than optimal. LB Malik Harrison The writing is on the wall for Harrison. Elandon Roberts played fantastic in his first game back in Pittsburgh, and Carson Bruener has had a strong preseason. The Steelers can save almost $5 million by cutting Harrison, which feels like a forgone conclusion. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 17-0 loss to the New York Jets
summary: It’s just the preseason. The final score doesn’t matter. But when you’re shut out at home by the New York Jets of all teams, the vibes aren’t exactly great. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had after the Steelers’ 17-0 loss Friday night. 1. New updates in the QB battle, but don’t […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 21: Kaleb Johnson #20 of the Pittsburgh Steelers carries the ball in front of Andre Cisco #8 of the New York Jets during the third quarter of a preseason game at Acrisure Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s just the preseason. The final score doesn’t matter. But when you’re shut out at home by the New York Jets of all teams, the vibes aren’t exactly great. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had after the Steelers’ 17-0 loss Friday night. 1. New updates in the QB battle, but don’t blow it out of proportion Will Howard wasn’t great Friday night. Throwing two interceptions and no touchdowns in a half of football will do that. And yes, unless he lights it up next week, it’s going to be tough to argue that he brings more to the table as a QB2 than Mason Rudolph come cutdown day. Still, it makes hardly any sense to be victory-lapping over the Ohio State product’s poor showing against New York, just as it was foolish to victory-lap after the handful of good throws he made last week against Green Bay. Howard’s first interception was due to a clever defensive disguise from the Jets (he still should’ve seen the safety). All-22 of Will Howard's INT. #Steelers (via @KDKA ) pic.twitter.com/0HXuIGM0sB — Alex Kozora (@Alex_Kozora) August 21, 2026 His second probably could’ve been an incompletion if wide receiver Roman Wilson hadn’t heavily drifted upfield, but it still looks like the throw would’ve been behind in what was already a tight window. Man to man SNAP it off and flatten. This is on the receiver not the QB. It’s the tough part about playing in preseason football, you have to be on time and trust the spots but sometimes the DB wants the ball more than the receiver does. pic.twitter.com/TG4gZ91Zdn — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) August 22, 2026 Before anyone accuses me of making excuses, I’ll point out Howard carries plenty of the blame on both turnovers, and had some misses outside of those plays. His backwards drifting in the pocket on a first-quarter sack turned what was already a rough Broderick Jones rep into a big play-canceling mistake. If Howard steps up into the pocket here instead of drifting backwards, this would have been a big hit down the field. Freiermuth smoked Sherwood on the bender to split the safeties. Tough. pic.twitter.com/oBujZNyqDx — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) August 22, 2026 I never thought Howard would be any sort of long-term starter for the Steelers, and still definitely don’t. His realistic NFL ceiling has always been that of a good backup. Still, it’s easy to forget that this was his second-ever preseason game, and neither of his interceptions were of the embarrassing variety. At this point, Howard looks to be headed towards the practice squad to open the regular season, and for good reason. But he still has plenty of time to prove he has a career in the NFL. Please, stop overreacting to preseason games, good or bad. The same could be said of rookie Drew Allar, who played the entire second half for Pittsburgh. His third-quarter connection with Lake McRee while drifting left was the exact type of “wow” throw that shows why the Steelers took a gamble on the Penn State product in the first place. What a throw by Drew Allar 👏 NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/G9nVGjW8BQ — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Allar also had a number of passes that ranged from “catchable” to “very catchable” that were not caught by the third-string receivers he was throwing to. “Drew Allar was terrible last night. Look at his statline!” Meanwhile, Drew Allar’s receivers last night: ⬇️😂 pic.twitter.com/pea1OEnRzN — Jack Sperry (@jack_sperry) August 22, 2026 The flip side is true as well, though — Allar continues to look promising, but still hasn’t played against a defense in the preseason where the majority of players will be on a 53-man roster in September. The arrow continues to point up, but we haven’t really learned much that we didn’t already see last week. What we can take away from Friday’s game: Mason Rudolph, despite not even playing, took a clear lead in the QB2 battle. Will Howard showed he still has growing to do. And Drew Allar clearly has upside. Shocking. That said, I wouldn’t mind seeing Drew Allar start next week against the Bills, giving him a chance to play with and against better players. Not that Howard doesn’t deserve another shot, but it would be nice to get Allar some more interesting reps before he’s likely buried on the depth chart in the regular season. 2. New defenders bring the juice Big names such as T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and Joey Porter Jr. did not suit up against the Jets, but it was still disappointing to see Pittsburgh’s kinda-starting defense get shredded by a Geno Smith-led New York passing game on the opening drive. As might be the theme of this column, it’s really not worth freaking out over. But that drive did sort of look like the Steelers defense at their worst last year: the secondary allowing too much separation, and the pass rush failing to generate quick pressures. Outside of that opening drive, however, Pittsburgh’s defensive depth actually came to play. Veteran safety Rayshawn Jenkins, who was signed during camp, continued to build his case for a roster spot with one tackle for loss and two quarterback hits. He looked highly effective near the line of scrimmage and as a blitzer, making him a valuable backup to DeShon Elliott given their similar strengths. This stop by Rayshawn Jenkins 😮‍💨 NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4I63pxpt6x — NFL (@NFL) August 21, 2026 But Elandon Roberts, who reunited with the Steelers in mid-August, arguably put together the best game of anyone on the field Friday night. The veteran linebacker looked like a player whose experience put him a step ahead of anyone else playing deep in a preseason game, leading the Steelers with five total tackles, including one tackle for loss and an open-field fourth-down stop. He was everywhere against the Jets. It's great the Steelers brought Elandon Roberts back to make these type of plays. pic.twitter.com/273mDxXGYC — Steelers Black and Gold Nation – Preseason (@B_GNation1) August 22, 2026 It was good to see him back, and wearing No. 50 again, too. I would put Malik Harrison’s roster chances close to zero at this point. Other defenders who stood out included second-year linebacker Carson Bruener, who logged pass deflection as well as a gap-shooting sack where he overpowered a blocking running back, and rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings, who dislodged a catch with a big hit in the third quarter. Robert Spears-Jennings making his presence felt 🗣️ NYJvsPIT on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/K4ZSQEhBDB — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 I’ve written plenty about how the Steelers seem to only have strong safeties on the roster, but at least those strong safeties seem to be playing well. There will likely be some growing pains — I’m not forgetting that game-opening drive — but overall, new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham’s scheme seems built to maximize downhill players such as Roberts and Jenkins with a blitz- and sim pressure-heavy style. Already, the inside linebackers seem to be popping off the screen more than in years past. Don’t forget how Graham’s defense with the Raiders led to the best seasons of former Steelers linebacker Robert Spillane’s career, who was formerly seen as a highly one-dimensional player with the black and gold. 3. Good, bad and ugly on special teams Special teams is rarely the most exciting part of a preseason game. But it is an important facet. For roster bubble players, performance in the third phase of the game is an essential aspect of making the final 53. And it wasn’t always pretty for the Steelers Friday night. One clear positive was punter Cameron Johnston, who averaged 50.5 yards over a whopping six boots, even landing one on the…

title: Seahawks vs Titans score: Seattle loses after sloppy second half, but that’s not the worst part
summary: Despite playing primarily their backups, the Seattle Seahawks raced out to an early double-digit lead. Ultimately, however, they couldn’t get the job done as they dropped their second preseason game 19-16 on the road against the Tennessee Titans. In addition to the loss, the Seahawks will be without rookie safety Bud Clark (broken ankle) and […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Mohamoud Diabate #44 of the Tennessee Titans attempts to sack Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second half of a preseason game at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite playing primarily their backups, the Seattle Seahawks raced out to an early double-digit lead. Ultimately, however, they couldn’t get the job done as they dropped their second preseason game 19-16 on the road against the Tennessee Titans. In addition to the loss, the Seahawks will be without rookie safety Bud Clark (broken ankle) and offensive lineman Mason Richman (undisclosed) for several months as both suffered long-term injuries in the first half. Unlike last week against the Dallas Cowboys where quarterbacks Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe alternated every two drives, each was given a half to play. Lock kicked it off and the veteran quarterback generated the team’s best quarter yet, helping Seattle (0-2) put up 16 first quarter points. He finished with 102 passing yards and a touchdown. Milroe, on the other hand, struggled. The team failed to record any points while he was on the field as he netted just 52 passing yards and was picked twice. He also took another fourth-down sack. The team looked far more sound on the defensive front, with linebackers Chazz Surratt and Chris Paul Jr. producing big plays against Tennessee’s (2-0) starting offense, which only managed field goals. The Titans won the coin toss and opted to defer, which proved to be a poor decision as Lock helped Seattle march down the field for a quick eight-play, 79 yard score. He connected with second year tight end Elijah Arroyo on 3rd and 1 at midfield to move the sticks before finding him wide open on the following play for a 36-yard touchdown to put the Seahawks up 7-0 with 11:12 remaining in the opening quarter. Drew Lock ➡️ Elijah Arroyo for a Seahawks TD! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mpb74cucFq — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2026 Unlike Seattle, Tennessee opted to play the majority of their starters, including quarterback Cam Ward who led a field goal drive on their first possession. Tony Pollard got the best of the Seahawks backups with a 33 yard gain to extend the drive, but rookie Andre Fuller made his presence felt on the following third down play with strong (and questionable) coverage against Elic Ayomanor to force a field goal. Jacardia Wright secured his first career touchdown and extended the Seahawks’ league when he broke free for a 69-yard score led by blocks from center Christian Haynes and wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr., who’s continued to impress. However, Jason Myers missed the extra point from 48 yards out. Jacardia Wright takes it straight to the end zone for a 69-yard TD 🗣️ SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bVuJlpcBGS — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2026 The Titans were unable to convert on the ensuing drive, with Surratt delivering a big hit at the line of scrimmage on 3rd and 2 followed by a stop by Paul Jr. at Tennessee’s own 35 to force the first turnover of the game. Seattle received some help from Cor’Dale Flott’s illegal conduct penalty on the opening play of the drive, but Lock and company were unable to build off the promising field position. Despite his earlier shank, Myers converted from the same distance he missed from before to put the Seahawks up 16-3 at 13:40 in the opening frame. Seattle scored on all three of their first quarter drives. The Seahawks forced their first punt of the game on the Titans next possession, but it didn’t come cleanly. Noah Igbinhoghene was called for a rather soft pass interference 3rd and 8 to extend the drive. However, the defense kept their composure and delivered three consecutive stops, highlighted by a sack from Surratt — his second notable play of the half. Despite a stagnant look from Seattle’s offense on the ensuing drive, a face mask from Oluwafemi Oladejo provided some assistance and Cedric Gray bailed them out just two plays later with an unsportsmanlike penalty to put the Seahawks within field goal range. But, it was all for nothing as Myers’ shaky night continued, hooking the 44 yard attempt wide right. Seattle’s defense forced a three-and-out as Mitch Trubisky entered for Ward but Cody White fumbled the punt return and it was recovered by Tennessee at the Seahawks 11 yard line. On third down, Trubisky scrambled to the right and found Xavier Restrepo for the four-yard score but it was called by after Jackson Slater was flagged for offensive holding, prompting the Titans to settle for a field goal. With time winding down, the Titans were finally able to force a punt and took advantage of it. Julius Chestnut had a 16 yard catch and run entering the two-minute drill and Trubisky found Ayomanor later in the drive to thrust Tennesse into Seattle territory. Ayomanor’s grab set up a Joey Slye field goal on the last play of the half, but the Seahawks still entered the locker room with a somewhat comfortable 16-9 lead. Tennessee turned the ball over to Will Levis in the second half, who wasn’t able to generate any offense on his first drive. Jamie Sheriff and Connor O’Toole capped it off with a sack on third down. Milroe entered the game for Seattle and was tasked with a difficult situation after Logan Brown committed a false start on the opening play to eventually set up 2nd and 14. However, Milroe delivered with a 16 yard scramble. Jalen Milroe escapes the pressure and gets the first down! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gTcr6Ddcjh — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2026 Brock Lampe’s offensive holding halted the momentum once again, but Milroe connected with Foster Jr. for a 24 yard gain. Despite two promising plays, the drive resulted in a punt. Back-to-back big runs for the Titans set them up near midfield, but the Seahawks young came through. Michael Dansby broke up what would’ve been a first down conversion intended for Tyren Montgomery before nearly intercepting Levis on the following play as he took a deep shot into double coverage, looking for Bryce Oliver. On the following possession, Milroe delivered a throw directly into the hands of Anthony Hill Jr., who dropped back into coverage and gave Tennessee promising field position at Seattle’s 38 yard line. Levis opened the drive with two productive runs, putting the Titans just outside the redzone. Tasked with a 3rd and 8, Seattle was hit with too many men on the field to set up a much easier third down conversion but Connor O’Toole came up big a big hit to force fourth down. Slye converted his fourth field goal of the night, which cut the deficit to four with 14:55 remaining in the game. Milroe’s third series was hardly any better. He failed to complete either of his passes before taking a costly sack on third down to once again send the ball back to Tennessee, giving them a chance to take their first lead of the game. That’s exactly what they did. The Titans marched down the field and D’Ernest Johnson capped off the 13-play, 64 yard drive that spanned nearly seven minutes by punching it in for a two-yard score as Tennessee took a 19-16 lead with 5:45 remaining. Milroe seemingly got the Seahawks back on track when he connected downfield with Ricky White III or a third down conversion but it was nullified due to offensive pass interference. The second year quarterback found Julian Hicks to set up a 4th and 3 but once again couldn’t find anyone and was sacked. Trailing by three with 3:59 remaining, Seattle’s defense came up with a big stop on 4th and 1 to prevent Hendon Hooker, the Titans fourth quarterback of the night from ending the game. The Seahawks take over on downs! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ugasw28wWx — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2026 Pressured out of the pocket on the ensuing play, Milroe delivered a pass intended for rookie Emmanuel Henderson Jr. but he slipped, leading to an interception by…

title: Seahawks offensive lineman Mason Richman feared to have ‘a long-term injury’
summary: While much of the injury attention was placed on Seattle Seahawks rookie Bud Clark, another young Seahawks player may also be facing a season-ending injury. Second-year offensive lineman Mason Richman, who usually lines up at guard but can play all across the line, went down on the opening drive of Seattle’s 19-16 preseason loss to […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 07: Mason Richman #78 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on before the NFL Preseason 2025 game between Las Vegas Raiders and Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 07, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images While much of the injury attention was placed on Seattle Seahawks rookie Bud Clark , another young Seahawks player may also be facing a season-ending injury. Second-year offensive lineman Mason Richman, who usually lines up at guard but can play all across the line, went down on the opening drive of Seattle’s 19-16 preseason loss to the Tennessee Titans. It looked like his knee buckled without much contact, and there was at least hope the injury wasn’t serious when he walked off under his own power. Well, in Mike Macdonald’s post-game press conference, he delivered the bad news. “We’re going to try to figure out what’s going on with Mason, but we also think that’s a major injury,” Macdonald said. “A long term injury.” Richman was replaced at left guard by Bryce Cabeldue, his 2025 draft classmate who had otherwise spent a good chunk of training camp and preseason with the third-team offense. If you’re keeping score, one week in Nashville cost Jake Bobo his season with a knee injury in Friday’s joint practice, Bud Clark “multiple months” with a broken ankle , and now potentially Richman is done until 2027 with what looked to be a knee injury. Can Seattle play some random Field Gulls commenters in the preseason finale against the Kansas City Chiefs? Just to be safe. This was a brutal week for Seattle’s roster depth, particularly its young players.

title: Winners and Losers from Seahawks vs. Titans: Some good, some bad, some bad injuries
summary: The Seattle Seahawks had a much better preseason game than last week’s opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Well, at least much better in the first half. You know you’ve done well when your backups and deep reserves outplay the starters on the other team, and that’s what happened in Seattle’s 19-16 loss over the Tennessee […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks hands the ball off to Jacardia Wright #31 of the Seattle Seahawks during the first half of a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks had a much better preseason game than last week’s opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Well, at least much better in the first half. You know you’ve done well when your backups and deep reserves outplay the starters on the other team, and that’s what happened in Seattle’s 19-16 loss over the Tennessee Titans. The second half, on the other hand? Ehhhhhhh. Unfortunately, the game was marred early on by the injury to second-round rookie Bud Clark , which is a significant blow to Seattle’s safety depth. Let’s get to our second Winners and Losers of preseason. Seattle Seahawks Winners Elijah Arroyo continues a strong camp and preseason A mostly unremarkable rookie season meant we didn’t see as much of Arroyo has hoped last year. He’s been one of the standouts in training camp, and the hope was that Brian Fleury would help unlock Arroyo’s potential. On the game’s opening drive, he caught a play-action pass out in the flat for a sizeable gain on 3rd and 1, then torched Tennessee’s starting defense (who, admittedly, torched themselves with a blown coverage) with a 36-yard touchdown grab. Drew Lock ➡️ Elijah Arroyo for Seahawks TD! SEAvsTEN on FOX Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/z4NztTiDuC — NFL (@NFL) August 24, 2026 Jacardia Wright comes back with a bang Having missed almost all of last season (albeit on the practice squad) with an injury, then a decent chunk of training camp with another injury, the second-year UDFA dashed through a gaping hole for a 69-yard touchdown run against Tennessee’s starting defense. Straight to the end zone. 🙂‍↕️ @JacardiaW 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/Rfqy0mkgsr — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) August 24, 2026 It wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows for Wright, who had a brutal pass pro mix-up that led to a (negated via penalty) Drew Lock interception, and he also botched a 3rd and 9 conversion by not getting up the field instead of trying to juke a tackler. Drew Lock bounces back Lock had some wayward accuracy last week, but he was on point against the Titans, going 12/14 for 103 yards and a touchdown. He did have a pick taken away due to a ticky-tack penalty, and it was a poor decision, but I place the initial blame on Jacardia Wright. Given the performance of his teammate, Jalen Milroe, QB2 is safe. Connor O’Toole livens up the pass rush From my camp observations, beat reporter write-ups, and the first preseason game, the pass rush depth at the bottom of the roster had mostly underwhelmed. Connor O’Toole had such a good summer as a rookie that he stayed on the roster and wasn’t even exposed to waivers at any point. O’Toole was excellent against the Titans, recording a sack and a key third-down stop on a Will Levis keeper. Chazz Surratt, Chris Paul Jr impress in first half Tyrice Knight and Patrick O’Connell are so valuable that even they got the night off. Surratt was shooting gaps and closing in on ball-carriers, notably recording a strip sack of Cam Ward. Paul, who has scarcely featured in camp or preseason, had a nice fourth-down run stuff of Tyjae Spears. Christian Haynes looks better While I found it peculiar that Haynes played into the fourth quarter (maybe a result of Bryce Cabeldue being subbed in sooner for an injured Mason Richman), he looks like he’s improving a bit under John Benton. He had a key block as the pulling guard on Jacardia’s touchdown run, and he had a rep where he tossed Jeffery Simmons down in pass pro. Was there a snap where Simmons got him back? Sure! But he does that to a lot of guys. Maybe Haynes is salvageable as a backup guard. The cornerbacks have bright moments I thought Michael Dansby had a solid game in pass coverage, while Nehemiah Pritchett had a brilliant tackle on a screen pass when he undercut the blocker. Andre Fuller’s face mask was ugly but he had a nice sideline break-up that was, well, it was pass interference but let’s say it was great coverage. Noah Igbinoghene’s DPI was bogus and he looks like the most polished corner to me out of everyone who played tonight. Admittedly, Tennessee’s passing game looks so bad when guys like Will Levis and Mitchell Trubisky are doing whatever on the field. We’ll see how Trevon Diggs factors into the equation next week… and maybe Julian Neal? Montorie Foster might be making this team I forgot to put this in the original write-up, but Foster just narrowly missed out on what would’ve been a diving grab touchdown (one of Lock’s only two incomplete passes), had a 24-yard catch in the second half, plus a special teams tackle. If Foster is playing special teams, that helps his roster case. He did have a procedural penalty but that’s par for the course for preseason. Foster had tough odds without Jake Bobo, but Bobo isn’t playing this season so that changes the equation a bit. Seattle Seahawks Losers Seattle’s health is ravaged some more in Nashville First it was Jake Bobo , now it’s Bud Clark. The Clark injury on the first defensive play of the game was a real downer. You feel so much for Clark knowing he’s likely not going to play until 2027 after breaking his ankle . As if that wasn’t enough, backup lineman Mason Richman is believed to have a major injury as well after his knee buckled on the game’s opening drive. His season figures to also be over. Whether through roster cuts (Andre Fuller, Emmanuel Henderson, Deven Eastern, and Michael Dansby are all on the bubble, at best) or injuries (Clark likely out long-term, Julian Neal has missed most of camp and preseason), it’s looking like there will be very little impact from this year’s draft. That’s not some disastrous outcome but it’s what would’ve been ideal, and now the 2026 class is almost destined to be largely dependent on what Jadarian Price can do. The good news? As long as the mystery surrounding Tory Horton clears up, we should see him, Rylie Mills, and Elijah Arroyo all step up in year two. It’s more important the 2025 class takes that leap than ask a lot of out this year’s weaker (on paper) group. Richman, sadly, is part of that 2025 group and now he joins Robbie Ouzts on the long-term injury list. All the best to Bud and Mason. It’s Jalen Milroe discussion time That was bad. I can’t really sugarcoat it any other way. Milroe was 6/11 for 52 yards, two terrible picks, and two sacks. Once again he got sacked on a fourth down when throwing the ball up for grabs is arguably better. His best play was probably the over the middle throw to Montorie Foster Jr for 24 yards, followed by a deep ball to Cody White that was dropped. Everything else was just basic stuff that shouldn’t intrigue anyone as far as his ceiling. I get that Milroe is mobile and fast but if he can’t do the quarterback stuff well then you can barely run an NFL offense with him. The good news for the Seahawks is that he was a hedge against Sam Darnold not panning out. Darnold is panning out thus far. My skepticism about Milroe before he was drafted was rooted in him not being good at a lot of regular quarterback things like throwing on time, pocket movement, decision-making, and bad turnovers. I kept an open mind when Seattle drafted him but I’m not really interested in keeping this up beyond for too much longer if there is not major improvement. I could live with Russell Wilson’s sacks (before he lost his elite mobility and elusiveness) because he did so many other cool things and was a super accurate QB who made a lot of great decisions. Milroe’s sacks and bad decisions don’t have any sort of meaningful payoff outside of scrambles. Uhhhh is Jason Myers okay? The one practice I saw Myers have a struggle was at VMAC. It was a bit of a breezy day and he was pulling all of his kicks wide right. Thus…

summary: The first play of Bud Clark’s second NFL preseason game will likely be his last until the 2027 season. Following the Seattle Seahawks’ against the Tennessee Titans, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Clark suffered a broken ankle on Seattle’s first defensive play of the game. Clark was carted off the field with an […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Bud Clark #9 of the Seattle Seahawks is carted off the field injured during the first half of a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first play of Bud Clark’s second NFL preseason game will likely be his last until the 2027 season. Following the Seattle Seahawks’ against the Tennessee Titans, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Clark suffered a broken ankle on Seattle’s first defensive play of the game. Clark was carted off the field with an air cast on his right leg. “Bud has a broken ankle, to my knowledge,” Macdonald said. “Severity, I’m not sure, but he’s going to be out multiple months.” It’s a tough blow for Seattle’s secondary, which sought to replace Coby Bryant through Clark and Ty Okada. Clark’s ball-hawking prowess at TCU led to Seattle taking him in the second round . Even though Okada is projected to be the starting safety alongside Julian Love, Clark figured to be a part of Seattle’s rotation in sub-packages, of which it has plenty for extra defensive backs on the field. The likes of D’Anthony Bell, Rodney Thomas II, A.J. Finley, and Maxen Hook were already pushing for a roster spot heading into training camp. Clark’s absence just made it even more of a competition to see who will not only get on the 53, but possibly play significant regular season snaps. All the best to Bud Clark in his recovery.

title: Seahawks-Titans instant post-game reaction: A tough night for Jalen Milroe
summary: The Seattle Seahawks continued their preseason schedule Sunday night with a 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans, their second loss in as many exhibition games. These preseason games are about much more than the final score, and that is exactly where I want to take the conversation after the game. With roster decisions getting closer, […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up before a preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks continued their preseason schedule Sunday night with a 19-16 loss against the Tennessee Titans, their second loss in as many exhibition games. These preseason games are about much more than the final score, and that is exactly where I want to take the conversation after the game. With roster decisions getting closer, every rep matters for players trying to earn a role, move up the depth chart or secure a place on the 53-man roster. One of my biggest areas of focus will be the wide receiver room, especially after the season-ending injury to Jake Bobo. His absence changes the depth picture and creates a real opportunity for some of Seattle’s younger receivers like Montorie Foster Jr and Ricky White III to step forward. The quarterback room will also be a major part of the postgame discussion, with Jalen Milroe playing the second half and not playing particularly well, throwing a pair of brutal interceptions and taking another crucial fourth down sack. Another area of discussion is Seattle’s offensive line depth. I wanted to see improvement in both pass protection and the run game, especially when it comes to communication, handling pressure and creating movement at the line of scrimmage. Defensively, the young secondary and depth along the defensive front will be worth watching closely as several players continue fighting for roles, but unfortunately that secondary depth took a big hit with the loss of Bud Clark . We’ll get into the biggest takeaways, Stock Up and Stock Down, standout performances, roster battles, game balls and what Sunday’s performance actually means as Seattle gets closer to the regular season. Seahawks-Titans may be over, don’t let the conversation end when the game does. Come join me on Hawks Eye after the final whistle and bring your biggest takeaways, questions and reactions. I’ll see you for 4th & Final at 8:55 pm PT! Video

title: Seahawks won’t play Jadarian Price in preseason
summary: For anyone hoping to see even a small glimpse of Seattle Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday night (5 pm PT, FOX), all you’ll get is him in pads but exclusively on the sideline. Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Bell has revealed the Seahawks’ plans for both the Titans game […]
full_text: RENTON, WASHINGTON - JULY 25: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts during practice at Virginia Mason Athletic Center on July 25, 2026 in Renton, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images For anyone hoping to see even a small glimpse of Seattle Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday night (5 pm PT, FOX), all you’ll get is him in pads but exclusively on the sideline. Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Bell has revealed the Seahawks’ plans for both the Titans game and some of what is in line for the Kansas City Chiefs finale on Friday. The big headline is that Price, who ramped up with padded practices this week after missing time the week before with upper leg soreness , has shown enough in practice that the Seahawks won’t even risk him in preseason reps. Price, the first-round pick the Seahawks drafted this spring to replace departed (to Kansas City in free agency) Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, will not play Sunday night against the Titans. He’s not going to play at the Chiefs Friday, either. Macdonald and general manager John Schneider have seen enough of Price’s speed, decisiveness in cutting into outside-zone run gaps and his pass catching to know Price is too valuable, and the running-back room too thinned by injuries already this preseason, to risk the rookie lead back in these games that don’t count. Price himself missed a week this month with what Macdonald vaguely described as “upper-leg soreness.” So, no preseason games in uncontrolled environments against hungry foes such as the Titans that are planning to play their starters through the first half. This should mean another busy night for George Holani and Velus Jones Jr. We’ll also see Anthony Hankerson likely get some carries after he was signed earlier this week . Emanuel Wilson doesn’t appear to be ready to play after getting injured in camp earlier this month. Jacardia Wright is TBD given he’s only just recovering from an injury. Bell also noted that the usual starters like Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, DeMarcus Lawrence, and others are not expected to play any part of preseason, so the first we’ll see of them in live action is the season opener versus the New England Patriots. As far as tonight’s quarterback situation, Drew Lock is slated to start the first half, while Jalen Milroe gets the second half. This seemingly puts an end to the “rotate every two series” strategy utilized last week in what was a disjointed showing versus the Dallas Cowboys. Lastly, new cornerback Trevon Diggs just arrived on Wednesday, so it was probably asking a lot for someone who’s dealt with a lot of injuries to get snaps on Sunday. The Chiefs game on Friday is evidently more feasible for him to make his Seahawks debut.
author: Mookie Alexander

title: 5 things to watch in Seahawks vs. Titans preseason game
summary: The Seattle Seahawks continue their 2026 preseason with a nationally televised game against the Tennessee Titans, who have a new head coach in Robert Saleh and a significantly retooled roster. After a lively joint practice on Friday, the actual game is expected to involve starters for the Titans, but we don’t know if the Seahawks […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Montorie Foster Jr. #87 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks continue their 2026 preseason with a nationally televised game against the Tennessee Titans, who have a new head coach in Robert Saleh and a significantly retooled roster. After a lively joint practice on Friday, the actual game is expected to involve starters for the Titans, but we don’t know if the Seahawks will do the same. Given Macdonald’s history, it’s probably not in the cards, which is fine. In the regular season, we normally make five predictions for a Seahawks game. I’m not interest in game predictions in preseason, so we’ll focus on what to watch for on Sunday night in Nashville. Is Jadarian Price going to play? The Seahawks’ first-round rookie was absent from the Dallas Cowboys game due to a minor injury that probably would not have stopped him from playing in a regular season game, but in preseason it’s better to err on the side of caution. Price returned to full, padded practice this week , so that should be an indicator he’s ready for his first NFL action. But will Mike Macdonald play Price at all on Sunday, or save him for the short week finale versus the Kansas City Chiefs on Friday? Emanuel Wilson is still not practicing, so if Price doesn’t play then it’s another game for George Holani and Velus Jones Jr to get the bulk of the snaps. I’d like to see Price get some reps without getting Jeremiyah Love’d into a multi-week injury. How will the Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe rotation be handled this time? Mike Macdonald opted to rotate Lock and Milroe every two possessions, which isn’t unusual for preseason but isn’t something we’ve seen any time recently with Seahawks quarterbacks. I’d like to see Milroe still get some time with the second unit, so there’s a part of me who wants to see him start the first half at the very least. There’s not much to expand on. Lock is Lock and the curiosity is whether or not Milroe has made enough improvements to even make a case to be QB2 any time soon, let alone this season. Incidentally, I hope Milroe has more downfield opportunities to throw. The offensive line has to do its job, but it feels like Milroe has consistently been a “play it safe” QB in preseason, and I’d rather he make aggressive mistakes than rack up completions on easier, shorter throws against third-string competition. Can Montorie Foster Jr seize his opportunity with Jake Bobo out? The unfortunate Jake Bobo knee injury has changed the wide receiver picture a bit. Tory Horton remaining out means Seattle is thin at receiver even if the starters randomly played against the Titans. Montorie Foster Jr has been one of the bright stories throughout camp and preseason, but we’ve been here many times before with the Seahawks and preseason receiver superstars. If we assume Cody White could bump up to WR5 and replace Bobo, a potential WR6 path for Foster has gotten a little clearer. He had a generally good game versus Dallas (although a procedure penalty and drop in the fourth quarter were not ideal), and he has a major chance to stake his claim for a roster spot. I’ll be interested to see if Foster plays any special teams snaps after none last Saturday. When and how much will Trevon Diggs play? Diggs just signed with the Seahawks on Wednesday, practiced a little bit on Friday, and there was nothing done on Saturday. Despite the name familiarity, Diggs is on a veteran’s minimum contract and is fighting for a roster spot. There isn’t any inkling as far as whether or not Diggs will get any snaps on Sunday, and if so, how many reps and how early will he be in the game? Last week, we saw Nehemiah Pritchett, Shemar Jean-Charles, and Noah Igbinoghene get all the cornerback snaps in the first half. SJC is on IR, so someone is going to have to be that third corner. Could it be Diggs off the jump? What about either of Michael Dansby or Andre Fuller? Pass rush? Anyone? The Seahawks struggled to generate pass rush from the second-team and below throughout the Cowboys loss. No sacks, few QB hits, and too many clean pockets. Not that a fifth edge rusher is of paramount importance, but the Seahawks benefited greatly from minimal games missed from their top four guys (Derick Hall, DeMarcus Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu, and Boye Mafe). If such a situation arises where that quartet—swapping out Mafe for Dante Fowler Jr, of course—has to miss extended time, then someone has to be that fourth edge guy. Is it Connor O’Toole? Jalan Gaines? Are they going to persist with Mike Morris at edge when he never actually plays there in the regular season? I’d like for some semblance of hope that there’s playable depth deep in the roster. Is there anything you’re keen on watching in tonight’s game? Tell us in the comments below! Join the conversation! (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 49ers activate Kittle from PUP list; McCaffrey returns to practice “Sunday’s move means Kittle will, barring a setback, definitely be back at some point in the first four weeks. It’s just a matter of how soon he’s ready to play in a game after not playing football for more than seven months.” 49ers OC Klay Kubiak shares key updates ahead of Raiders preseason game “San Francisco 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak spoke with reporters after Sunday’s training camp practice. Here’s everything he had to say.” Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle provide ‘energy’ in return to 49ers practice “Obviously, when you don’t practice, the way the media works now is, (it’s a) firestorm,” McCaffrey said. “But this was kind of part of the plan from the jump, to ramp up pretty big, get nine, 10 practices in. Then, come back down and then ramp back up so we’re fresh for the duration.” 49ers’ George Kittle practices Sunday for first time since Achilles injury (paywall) “The five-time All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler worked through individual drills but did not play any snaps during the team 11-on-11 periods as he eased back in Sunday.” 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey returns to practice after 2-week absence: ‘I feel fresh’ (paywall) “Both McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle were in uniform for Sunday’s practice, Kittle’s first since tearing an Achilles tendon Jan. 11. Though he’s easing back in and was held out of everything but individual drills, McCaffrey took part in a handful of 11-on-11 snaps and carried the ball three times. He broke one of those carries to the right for a roughly 25-yard gain. “I feel fresh,” he said. “It’s good to be back out there.”…Black had another impressive practice, breaking at least two big runs. His hard-charging style, however, also created a friendly fire moment when he plowed into the back of center Jake Brendel, knocking the 300-pounder face-first to the ground. Brendel got up and took part in the next play…..All eyes were on Kittle on Sunday, but fellow tight end Jake Tonges was prolific for the second straight day. That included back-to-back sideline catches on throws from Purdy. If Kittle couldn’t take part in the Week 1 opener, Tonges likely would start at tight end.” 49ers trade for veteran linebacker who played under Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris “He spent his rookie season in Atlanta under offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan. Raheem Morris was coaching on the offensive side of the ball for the majority of his tenure when Jones was there. However, there was overlap in 2020, when Morris was the defensive coordinator alongside the interim coach. That was in 2020. So Shanahan and Morris have both seen Jones during 100+ tackle seasons…With Martin suffering a hamstring injury late Thursday, it could also be the team telling us that Martin’s injury is severe. If you’re on the roster bubble, the last thing you want to see is your team trade for the position you play. One of Jones’ calling cards has been as a pass rusher. As we’ve seen, that is something Raheem Morris is going to do early and often with his inside linebackers. Jones pressured the quarterback on 23.1% of his rushes last season with Tampa Bay. No matter where he’s been, Jones’ pressure percentage has been above league average. And even as he’s gotten longer in the tooth, Jones has still recorded multiple “hustle stops,” which is when a defender makes a tackle from 20 yards away. He had two last season in 20 snaps. That’s a sign that his speed remains above average.” 49ers training camp practice 16: Quick hits “Jacob Cowing also drew some attention during Sunday’s practice. “Jacob Cowing looking sharp in 1-on-1 drills. Finishing camp strong,” Tafur reported. Cowing is competing for a spot in a crowded wide receiver room, so strong practices at this point in camp can only help his case. Mike Evans was another player to watch. The veteran wide receiver left practice and took off his pads, appearing frustrated. Jennifer Lee Chan reported that the situation could be injury-related, although there was no immediate indication of the severity.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 16 of 49ers Camp: Kittle and McCaffrey Return “Black isn’t a hybrid slot receiver like McCaffrey, but he can catch passes, and the 49ers will throw to him. He’s a three-down player. But the best thing he does is run the ball, particularly between the tackles. He has the speed to get to the perimeter, but he wants to run downhill. He hits holes between the tackles with zero hesitation, and can squirt through the tiniest of creases. In that sense, he reminds me of Frank Gore. At one point, he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Fred Warner on a pass over the middle, stayed down for a second, shook his head, ran back to the huddle, lined up in the backfield, took the handoff and exploded around the left side for a 20-yard gain. He’s so tough….[James Thompson Jr] is probably the second-best defensive tackle on the team after Osa Odighizuwa. Thompson Jr. is a terrific run defender who actually can rush the passer as well. Today, he lined up with the starters and beat Carver Willis to “sack” Purdy. Whoever scouted this guy deserves a promotion….[Raheem Morris] is trying to install so many new things, and he doesn’t currently have the personnel to pull off any of them. To be fair, his players do a good job aggressively breaking on intermediate passes over the middle, but they can’t seem to stop anything else. Today, Morris kept using a defense with five defensive linemen, one linebacker and five defensive backs. And it couldn’t stop anything — not the run or the pass. On third down, he wants to be aggressive and blitz. This just leaves his subpar safeties one on one against superior players. And if the blitz doesn’t get to the quarterback right away, which it usually doesn’t, the defense gives up huge catches.”

summary: The San Francisco 49ers have made a trade! It’s player-for-player. Zamir White, who was signed after a couple of injuries at running back, is being traded for linebacker Deion Jones. full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - JANUARY 02: Deion Jones #45 of the Atlanta Falcons after a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on January 2, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have made a trade! It’s player-for-player. Zamir White, who was signed after a couple of injuries at running back, is being traded for linebacker Deion Jones. The Atlanta Falcons drafted Jones a decade ago. He spent his rookie season in Atlanta under offensive coordinator Kyle Shanahan. Raheem Morris was coaching on the offensive side of the ball for the majority of his tenure when Jones was there. However, there was overlap in 2020, when Morris was the defensive coordinator alongside the interim coach. That was in 2020. So Shanahan and Morris have both seen Jones during 100+ tackle seasons. Jones played in both preseason games for the New Orleans Saints. He played 23 and 25 snaps in each game, and also covered punts and kicks. During the first preseason game for the Saints, Jones didn’t take the field defensively until the end of the third quarter. Like White and San Francisco, New Orleans was probably going to part ways with Jones when it’s time for roster cuts. As a veteran with special teams experience, Jones likely spells bad news for one of the linebackers fighting for a roster spot. That could be Tatum Bethune, Garret Wallow, Jalen Graham, Luke Gifford, or all of the above. It could also be the 49ers adding a body they believe can fill in if there are injuries inside, acknowledging that neither Nick Martin nor Jaden Dugger is ready to play if Fred Warner or Dre Greenlaw suffers an injury. With Martin suffering a hamstring injury late Thursday, it could also be the team telling us that Martin’s injury is severe. If you’re on the roster bubble, the last thing you want to see is your team trade for the position you play. One of Jones’ calling cards has been as a pass rusher. As we’ve seen, that is something Raheem Morris is going to do early and often with his inside linebackers. Jones pressured the quarterback on 23.1% of his rushes last season with Tampa Bay. No matter where he’s been, Jones’ pressure percentage has been above league average. And even as he’s gotten longer in the tooth, Jones has still recorded multiple “hustle stops,” which is when a defender makes a tackle from 20 yards away. He had two last season in 20 snaps. That’s a sign that his speed remains above average

summary: Finally, the tight end news we’ve all been waiting for. The San Francisco 49ers announced they have activated George Kittle from the Active/PUP list. That’s meaningful news for a plethora of reasons. One being the 49ers activated Kittle before Sunday morning’s practice. Kittle’s positivity a week ago should’ve eliminated any fears of him missing meaningful […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers walks on the field before a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Finally, the tight end news we’ve all been waiting for. The San Francisco 49ers announced they have activated George Kittle from the Active/PUP list. That’s meaningful news for a plethora of reasons. One being the 49ers activated Kittle before Sunday morning’s practice. Kittle’s positivity a week ago should’ve eliminated any fears of him missing meaningful games. Seven days later, after receiving good news in the middle of the week, Kittle will return to practice. One of Kittle’s biggest concerns was not having enough practice time ahead of Week 1 to get into football shape. Kittle should be able to get in close to double-digit practices in before the 49ers play the Los Angeles Rams. Again, it’s not the end of the world if he needs another week with the game being in Australia, but the fact that Week 2 is realistic makes you appreciate Kittle attacking his rehab and putting himself in a position to play this early in the season. Kittle tore his Achilles the second week of January. It was a unique tear because it occurred higher up, rather than lower near the heel. It’s still incredible that he has a shot to play in September. Christian McCaffrey also returned to practice on Sunday. The 49ers will have their top three running backs on the practice field with Jordan James returning on Saturday for the first time in roughly three weeks.

title: De’Zhaun Stribling: The 49ers wide receiver both looks—and acts—the part
summary: Wondering why the San Francisco 49ers took De’Zhaun Stribling is so three months ago. After two preseason games, the narrative has turned from skeptical to optimistic on what the 49ers rookie might do when the regular season hits. In the preseason win against the Chargers Thursday night, he had three catches that, while small, stood […]
full_text: EL SEGUNDO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 18: De'Zhaun Stribling #15 of the San Francisco 49ers makes a reception during the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Chargers Joint Practice at The Bolt on August 18, 2026 in El Segundo, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wondering why the San Francisco 49ers took De’Zhaun Stribling is so three months ago. After two preseason games, the narrative has turned from skeptical to optimistic on what the 49ers rookie might do when the regular season hits. In the preseason win against the Chargers Thursday night, he had three catches that, while small, stood out. “Just trying to do my part to help the whole offense roll,” Stribling said to Steve Wyche after the game. That’s an offense that runs through quarterback Brock Purdy, who demonstrated great chemistry with his rookie. “He’s a guy that’s consistent, smart, and shows that he’s a guy that you can trust,” Purdy said via NBC Sports Bay Area. “That first drive, to go out there and be able to connect with him, felt really good; him making some tough catches with guys on him and things like that. So for me, that’s huge. I know he’s going to continue to get better.” While Purdy praises Stribling’s immediate ability, others, such as tight end George Kittle, have praised the rookie’s attitude and work ethic as well. “He’s got the right mindset off the rip,” Kittle said in an NFL Radio interview earlier in the week. “Zero ego. He asks questions—like, ‘Hey, what can I do on this?’” Kittle elaborated that the advice he gives new players is to be a sponge and absorb information from the veterans. Something Stribling has been doing quite a bit of. Stribling continues to stay humble and do his job. His mindset is best shown in what he told Steve Wyche: “Just doing my 1-11,” meaning he was one of 11 players on the field. This doesn’t seem like a guy who is going to quit routes when his number isn’t called, or he doesn’t get the ball.

title: Buccaneers Preseason Week 2 Winners and Losers
summary: The Buccaneers sneaked away with another preseason victory Saturday, skating past the Kansas City Chiefs, 16-15, at Raymond James Stadium. Several starters got some run this week, with mixed results. The offense looked inert, really just out there for some light exercise before exiting with two 3-and-out drives. The defense looked much better, completely stoning […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Rueben Bain #3 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers lines up against the Kansas City Chiefs during the first half of a preseason game at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buccaneers sneaked away with another preseason victory Saturday, skating past the Kansas City Chiefs, 16-15, at Raymond James Stadium. Several starters got some run this week, with mixed results. The offense looked inert, really just out there for some light exercise before exiting with two 3-and-out drives. The defense looked much better, completely stoning the Chiefs on both drives. The actual result was more about the Chiefs losing the game than the Bucs winning it, but that’s really secondary to the individual performances, which we’ll highlight now. Winners Rueben Bain Jr. The Buccaneers’ first-rounder, widely considered a steal by many at 15th overall, took the field for his first NFL action and he wasted no time creating a viral highlight. Bain with a sick hump move. Sheesh! pic.twitter.com/err5hv3PH2 — Billy M (@BillyM_91) August 22, 2026 He played less than 10 snaps, but one of those included a vicious pass rush rep to put immediate pressure on Justin Fields on third down. Now it was against undrafted tackle Khalil Benson, who Bain coincidentally terrorized in the National Championship Game, so context does matter, but you can only win the matchups you’re given so it’s still encouraging. He also showed instincts dropping in coverage and displayed his trademark relentless motor, all good signs. Reports about Bain, from practice to joint scrimmages to after-hours workouts, have been nothing but stellar. Expectations are high, and that highlight will only stoke more excitement. Jalon Daniels At this point, the at-large conversation is less about if Daniels is making the 53-man roster and more about if he deserves to be the primary backup QB. In two games, Daniels has looked promising in both, delivering bullet strikes, using his legs to create, and generally sparking an offense that has lacked vigor under anyone else. Down 9-0 at halftime, Daniels came in and led three straight scoring drives to deliver the Bucs another W — the second straight game he’s sparked a comeback. He threaded the needle on a rollout to Ko Kieft for an impressive touchdown, highlighting a great night where he finished 9-of-14 for 71 yards and a touchdown to go along with 7 rushes for 19 yards. Jalon Daniels with a JOLT to Raymond James! Great throw! pic.twitter.com/egvVzq1ZN1 — Jon Gruden (@BarstoolGruden) August 23, 2026 It feels unlikely that he’ll surmount Jake Browning as QB2 since the latter has real-game experience (10 career starts) — that matters in the NFL — and Daniels needs more polishing in a professional scheme (he had multiple fumbled snaps from under center), but it’s impressive that Daniels has even prompted people to wonder if he deserves the role instead. The Defense In two games, the Buccaneers defense definitely feels refreshed for the better. Many starters got their first reps of the preseason and looked good, from the edge rushers to the secondary. In two drives, the Bucs forced two easy 3-and-outs which saw the Chiefs gain just 13 total yards. Bain and Yaya Diaby got their moments, and Tykee Smith came screeching in on a blitz to create immediate pressure. Rookie nickel Keionte Scott showed up on an authoritative run stop, David Walker generated multiple pressures and Anthony Nelson even created a strip sack, and UDFA Ayden Garnes continued showing up in a positive way with a pass breakup. David Walker showed plenty of juice off the edge. Very close to having 3 sacks pic.twitter.com/1CZ1Yixzvs — Billy M (@BillyM_91) August 23, 2026 In general, the defense just looks more energized and focused through two preseason contests, allowing less than 17 points in both. If Todd Bowles can deliver a more fundamentally sound, aggressive unit, the team’s fortunes should be much improved. Dean Patterson and Kam Johnson On a night where the Bucs held out four of their top options in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin, Jalen McMillan, and Tez Johnson, the prime opportunity existed for the depth receivers to make their cases for sticking around. Two names stood out in particular, those being Dean Patterson and Kam Johnson. The latter was the team’s primary punt returner last year and he did well in that role, generating an above-league-average 11.2 yards per return —good for top 10 in the league. He showed more of that juice last night, creating a 23-yard scamper on one return. He also contributed 4 catches for 56 yards to co-lead the team, making a solid case to continue sticking around as WR6. That said, Patterson, an undrafted free agent out of Georgia Tech, has looked promising in both games. He notched a team-high 6 catches for 56 yards Saturday, including an impressive toe-touch snag for 24 yards. The 6-2 Tampa native is likely on the outside looking in no matter what, but what he is doing is forcing his name to the top of the list for the practice squad over other names like David Sills, Dennis Houston, Eric Rivers, and Garrett Greene. Look at that toe tap catch by Dean Patterson IV 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bl2sBGi0Bm — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 Losers Jake Browning and Connor Bazelak Browning is more a loser in the sense he got absolutely destroyed. On his second dropback, a practically uncontested sack left him laid out on the Raymond James grass and sent him into concussion protocol (which he cleared). He received another massive hit later in the game that created a forced fumble. But still, he didn’t look polished or precise enough to tamp down any mounting hype surrounding Daniels. The fact that he’s even having to answer questions about a quarterback competition when he signed a $1.3 million contract with $400k guaranteed does say something. He will need to look good against the Jacksonville Jaguars in joint practices and game action to inspire more confidence moving forward. Meanwhile, Bazelak is toast. He did not play at all on Saturday one week after looking significantly worse than Daniels. It doesn’t really matter what the reason was, Bazelak not being able to stymie Daniels’ momentum only worsens his chances of staying with the team. Keeping four QBs seems unlikely, so the second-year signal caller feels destined for the waiver wire. The Offensive Line Depth This was an ugly, ugly game for the offensive line depth. The low light of that ugliness was Marshall Foerner getting absolutely dusted and putting Browning in protocol, which practically signed the former’s death warrant when it comes to staying with this team in any serious capacity after next week. Marshall Foerner toasted and Jake Browning laid out because of it. pic.twitter.com/sY843TmdCp — Evan Closky (@ECloskyWTSP) August 23, 2026 Elijah Klein looked rough again, and multiple players (namely fourth-string left tackle Paul Rubelt and Luke Haggard) had costly penalties via false start and holding. When these guys are trying to make their case for the final depth spot and practice squad slots, this ineptitude is not the way to do it. The primary depth should be in a better position with names like Ben Chukwuma, Dan Feeney and rookie Billy Schrauth, but you’d really like to see better out of their competition.
author: Mike Kiwak

title: Titans improve to 2-0 with 19-16 win over Seahawks
summary: The Tennessee Titans improved to 2-0 in the 2026 preseason with a 19-16 win over the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks. The game was pretty brutal to watch. Cam Ward played much better in this one. One of the things that I was really hoping to see from him tonight was the ability to […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 23: Head Coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to Week 2 of the preseason game at against the Seattle Seahawks Nissan Stadium on August 23, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans improved to 2-0 in the 2026 preseason with a 19-16 win over the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks. The game was pretty brutal to watch. Cam Ward played much better in this one. One of the things that I was really hoping to see from him tonight was the ability to hit the layups. He did that. title: Commanders vs. Lions preseason Week 2: Mark Tyler’s Studs and Duds
summary: Washington traveled to Detroit for a preseason clash against the Lions at noon on Saturday. While the game was a snooze-fest, it did give fans a chance to see some of the starters in a bit more action. The Commanders first-team defense made a big play where they scored a touchdown, while the first-team offense […]
full_text: Washington traveled to Detroit for a preseason clash against the Lions at noon on Saturday. While the game was a snooze-fest, it did give fans a chance to see some of the starters in a bit more action. The Commanders first-team defense made a big play where they scored a touchdown, while the first-team offense looked COMPLETELY out of sync. Overall, the team was able to head home after a 17-13 loss without any significant injuries – so in that respect, this was a win. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs QB Athan Kaliakmanis Athan Kaliakmanis was under immense pressure during his time under center, but I thought he did a nice job moving around in the pocket and made some really nice throws. He finished 11-for-14 for 162 yards and did not get sacked. In my opinion he has VERY CLEARLY outplayed Sam Hartman over these first two games of the preseason. AK with a 55yd DIME to Nash! pic.twitter.com/aagZi1YBkx — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 WR Antonio Williams Playing primarily with the second team, Antonio Williams hauled in three passes, including the BEAUTIFUL snag below, for 41 receiving yards. His routes looked crisp, he catches everything with his hands and his body control is exceptional. AMAZING catch across the middle by the rookie Antonio Williams for 21yds 💥 pic.twitter.com/0WfQGcnkd3 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 WR Jaden Bradley Jaden Bradley made one HECK of a one-handed grab for a 30-yard gain in the third quarter. He also blocked really well and contributed on special teams. He’s making a solid case to somehow be included on the 53-man roster. UNBELIEVABLE catch by the rookie Bradley! pic.twitter.com/xL8c4i6RRq — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 CB Amik Robertson Mik didn’t get too many snaps, but he made the play of the game for Washington with his sack-fumble of Lions quarterback Joshua Dobbs (which was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown by Joshua Josephs) early in the first quarter on a picture-perfect hit. There was great pressure on the play by Josephs and Javontae Jean-Baptiste. Robertson with the BIG hit on Dobbs, but it was the pressure from Josephs and Jean-Baptiste that forced him off his spot pic.twitter.com/2iGyoop7Hi — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 Maurice Hurst II The former Michigan Wolverine was wreaking havoc against the Lions’ backup offensive linemen. The recent, in-camp signing tied for second on the team with five combined tackles and notched two sacks. Nice active hands here by Hurst who get off the block to collect a sack pic.twitter.com/rPaY2baKtI — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 Duds Washington’s interior offensive line The run blocking by the group was pretty non-existent, and there were WAY too many missed blocks and mistakes, mainly by the backups. I didn’t think rookie Matt Gulbin played well at right guard, and I though Julian Good-Jones struggled at center. Foster Sarell and Nicholas Petit-Frere weren’t good either, but the interior play was a lot worse. If Gulbin make this block, this play goes for a BIG gain pic.twitter.com/JbY1Tmrvcd — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 Good-Jones is too late recognizing the stunt and Jayden is forced to burn the ball pic.twitter.com/lA6n1nYOH2 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 S Will Harris By all accounts, Will Harris has not had a good camp. He looked slow to react to some passes Saturday and had a bad whiff on a screen early in the second quarter. I don’t know how many safeties Washington will keep, but Harris is no longer a roster lock. Harris needs to make this tackle! pic.twitter.com/nJy9X8qCaH — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 RB Robert Henry Jr. Someone fighting to make the team will need to prove they have special teams value. Robert Henry fumbling the kickoff in the fourth quarter was not a good look for the undrafted rookie. He had four carries for minus-three yards and missed a few blocks in pass protection. The rookie Henry fumbles the kickoff. Not a good look for a guy fighting to make the team. pic.twitter.com/DqPWeBhcfM — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) August 23, 2026 Notes Leo Chenal has not looked particularly good mixing in with the first- and second-team defense. He did have a nice stuff but also missed a tackle that went for a big gain. Hopefully, this is just a case of him working out the kinks early on. So far, he’s looked a lot better than Harris at safety. He gets quick penetration into the opposing backfield and had made some really nice plays. He was credited with five combined tackles, including one for a loss, and a quarterback hit against Detroit.
