title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from preseason Week 2
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders’ second preseason game, a 17-13 loss to the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Replacing the Commanders starting center won’t fix the offensive line There is no question that the Washington Commanders need to replace Julian Good-Jones at the center position. Even head coach Dan Quinn seems to have finally come to the realization, stating “(we’ve) got work to do to figure out where we want to get to at center.” Setting aside the fact the coaching staff and front office put themselves in this position with the surprise release of Tyler Biadasz , the return of Nick Allegretti to the starting lineup won’t solve all the issues with the offensive line. Good-Jones getting driven into the backfield disrupted several offensive plays, including backside pulls, but parts of the lineup also lack the movement skills to wall off defenders and create holes in the run game. Rookie Matt Gulbin didn’t look close to starting at guard in his second appearance in a Commanders uniform, and neither did most of the team outside of right guard Sam Cosmi. The issues don’t all come from personnel. Zone schemes are based on timing and cohesion, and the current version of the Commanders’ offensive line does not have it. Tight end John Bates is known as one of the better blockers in the league, but after missing most of training camp with an injury, he failed to set up his run block on the second offensive play of the game, and the rep quickly led to a sack. Jayden Daniels sacked on his 2nd dropback pic.twitter.com/zvAsRDAOtS — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) August 22, 2026 The team needs to settle on a starting offensive line and let the unit work together starting this week. The running backs also need to practice with that group on a regular basis to learn timing and develop a feel for how holes are developing in the run game. As of now, Rachaad White is going to earn his free-agent money as a personal protector for Jayden Daniels. Ricky Barber may have a leg up on a roster spot Shy Tuttle and Byron Cowart were both moved off their spots in the run game and didn’t appear to offer much disruption to Detroit’s offense. Ricky Barber , on the other hand, was able to penetrate upfield and disrupt the backfield on multiple occasions. He looks noticeably bigger this season and held his own in the run game. Barber failed to finish a number of plays; otherwise he would have had a much bigger game. Maurice Hurst II did have two sacks, but they came later in the game and he just joined the team. My guess is the team prefers the younger Barber as a player that can replace Newton’s skill set but also hold up in the run game. Jeffrey M’Ba also had an impressive showing and should be in line for a practice squad spot if the coaches don’t opt for one of the veterans. Will Harris might be on the outside looking in at final roster cuts Safeties Quan Martin and Will Harris both had a rough start to training camp, but while Martin has responded with two interceptions over the last two games, Harris continues to underwhelm. He doesn’t look physical enough at the line of scrimmage and doesn’t have the instincts and speed to play deep. While Joshua Josephs most certainly should have held contain better on Dobbs long touchdown run, Harris should also have been there to make the stop but instead lost track of the ball. Man coverage, so Josephs needs to take the QB and Styles is fine but the deep safety (Harris) completely loses the ball here https://t.co/7e3hS2oKtI — Nick Akridge (@nick_akridge) August 22, 2026 I was watching All-22 and came across this. Will Harris (#3) HAS to make this tackle, no excuses. pic.twitter.com/BI5NphfSID — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) August 23, 2026 Releasing Harris nets the team $3.7 million in savings , but more importantly, with the emergence of Tyler Owens and the special teams play of Percy Butler, there isn’t a role for Harris in Daronte Jones’ defense. Expect the team to cut him in favor of another player on the roster. The Washington Commanders defense has the potential to be special this season In four quarters of play, the defense created five takeaways to go along with multiple sacks and a defensive touchdown, all without the aid of starters Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, and Tim Settle. The Commanders' defense has produced 5 takeaways in their last 4 quarters of play. Pre Week 1 Q2 Quan Martin – INT Q4 Ale Kaho – INT Q4 Malik Spencer – INT Pre Week 2 Q1 Amik Robertson – FF Q1 Quan Martin – INT — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 22, 2026 Settle’s absence has been noticeable in stopping the run game, but the aggressive nature of Daronte Jones’ scheme has been paying off with turnovers so far and we haven’t even seen the full version yet. Getting the first team back on the field while allowing Sonny Styles more time to develop should make for a formidable group this season. While fans should expect the defense to allow some big plays, their ability to generate turnovers should keep the Washington Commanders in contention this year.

summary: The Daily Slop – 23 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles ESPN 2026 NFL […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-AUGUST 22: Quarterback Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders gets sacked by cornerback Avonte Maddox #29 of the Detroit Lions during the first half of an NFL preseason football game between the Washington Commanders and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Daily Slop – 23 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Back at it on Friday pic.twitter.com/Fq5X9lWMzV — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 22, 2026 Articles ESPN 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis Commanders: How will the O-line room shake out? The toughest decision will be wide receiver, considering the Commanders say they have eight worthy of a roster spot. But the biggest decision will be what to do along the offensive line. Do they even have nine linemen currently on the team worthy of a roster spot? Who is the backup center — presumed starter Nick Allegretti’s calf issues in training camp have limited him to two practices this summer. Right now it would be inexperienced Julian Good-Jones (two snaps, one game since entering the NFL in 2020) or rookie Matt Gulbin. Washington should continue to be on the lookout for interior line depth. — John Keim Next game: at Baltimore Ravens (Friday, 6 p.m. ET, NFL Network) To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) Chaos unleashed by Washington defense You wouldn’t know Washington’s defensive front was without Daron Payne, Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson. After generating three turnovers in the preseason opener against Miami, Daronte Jones’ group turned the Lions over twice in the first eight plays. The Lions played without quarterback Jared Goff and other offensive standouts, including running back Jahmyr Gibbs, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, and left tackle Penei Sewell. Still, the Commanders showed some of the chaos a blitz-heavy plan can create. Robertson’s sack off the edge was a good example of how this defense can confuse quarterbacks trying to gauge who is rushing and who is dropping. Dobbs took the hit from the front. The loose ball went backward toward the Lions’ end zone before Josephs fell on it. Three more sacks followed on Detroit’s first possession of the second quarter. Recently signed DT Maurice Hurst got the first before T.J. Maguranyanga and Kain Medrano combined for a takedown, and Javonte Jean-Baptiste got QB Luke Altmeyer. Charles Omenihu did not record a sack, but his pressure led to Dobbs throwing into traffic while on the move — and right to Martin. Safety Tyler Owens trucking a running back trying to pass-block was another highlight. For more from Ben Standig, click here The Athletic (paywall) Offensive highlights McLaurin and Diggs never saw the ball in their limited time on the field, but the handful of receivers hoping to snare one of those last roster spots showed quite a bit. Undrafted rookie Jaden Bradley had the play of the day when he pulled in a 30-yard catch with one hand while being held by a defender. Rookie Antonio Williams caught a 21-yard bullet up the middle on third-and-10 to help set up a field goal on that same third-quarter drive. Then, Nick Nash had a 55-yard over-the-shoulder catch along the right sideline to set up Drew Stevens’ second field goal of the day. The passer on all three of those deep balls was Athan Kaliakmanis, Washington’s seventh-round rookie who may have done enough to prompt the team to roster three quarterbacks, especially as Marcus Mariota recovers from an MCL sprain. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Jaden Bradley is making his Commanders’ roster case hard to dismiss It’s begging a question that will be answered by the end of the month. Is there room for Bradley to make the final 53-man squad ? The common belief has been that Washington will keep either six or seven wide receivers. Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, and third-round rookie Antonio Williams are roster locks, as are Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane for their return specialist roles. Then, it’s been expected that the Commanders will keep either one or two of Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown, and Van Jefferson Jr., with everybody else on the outside looking in. But a few of the camp bodies are making matters a bit more challenging, especially Bradley. At this point, Bradley has to be considered firmly in the race for one of those final roster spots. Bradley offers more long-term upside than Jefferson and Burks, and he can also play on special teams. The Commanders have been impressed with him all summer , and now he’s showing he can make plays against real NFL competition. The only problem Bradley faces is that after the addition of Diggs , the Commanders have a deep receiver room that can only afford to keep so many wideouts. Much of his competition has also made a strong impression this offseason, and head coach Dan Quinn has been known to choose experience over youth when it comes to the crunch. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Commanders’ Preseason Loss to Lions Winner Maurice Hurst II At a time when the team is looking for a pass-rushing defensive tackle after Johnny Newton went down with an injury, Maurice Hurst jumps out with two sacks in the Lions game. The Commanders were without Odafe Oweh, K’Lavon Chaisson, and Dorance Armstrong, among others, on the defensive front. Verdict : His possible depth status could see an increase in reps after two sacks. Losers Robert Henry Jr. No one had the complete opposite day from the opener quite like Robert Henry Jr. did against the Lions. After having 75 yards and a touchdown against the Dolphin , Henry left Detroit with minus three yards on four attempts. The offensive line didn’t help much with their run blocking either, but Henry also fumbled a kick return with Washington down four and getting the ball back for its final possession with 2:15 remaining. Verdict : While the rushing total is bad, it could have been overlooked given the offensive line’s issues, but the kickoff fumble is close to a fatal flaw with as much emphasis as these guys put on special teams and securing the football. Julian Good-Jones Julian Good-Jones has done more to hurt his situation over the last two weeks than to help, even with what is likely his career lying in his lap currently. Verdict : It’s still odd to me that Matt Gulbin isn’t being given more of a shot at this position, at least as the primary backup to Nick Allegretti. The fact that Good-Jones is not that guy, but they keep putting him out there over Gulbin, tells me who they trust, but that doesn’t help block people. Something needs to be done here as the red flags are waving. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Three young players shine against Lions LB Javontae Jean-Baptiste Commanders third-year linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste had an impressive afternoon against Detroit. The former Notre Dame linebacker recorded a sack, quarterback hit and tackle for loss. Jean-Baptiste is currently expected to serve as the third-string outside linebacker behind Joshua Josephs, while Odafe Oweh is projected to start. His performance is another example of the depth Washington has in its outside linebacker room. Jean-Baptiste missed much of the 2025 season after appearing in just three games. He only recorded one sack and six total tackles. Hopefully, his strong outing against Detroit is a sign of what’s to come this season and, most importantly, that he can stay healthy. title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis
summary: NFL Nation reporters tackle the biggest looming roster questions coming off each NFL Week 2 preseason game.
full_text:
Week 2 of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us more insight into position battles and the push to make 53-man rosters before the cut-down deadline Aug. 30. Action began with two games Thursday before Friday's three contests, with severe weather rolling through Jacksonville late in the fourth quarter -- causing league and team officials to end the game there because of lightning at the two-minute warning.

 Things continued Saturday with 10 games, including  Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson 's first home game since tearing his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and him being greeted with loud boos, and Minnesota Vikings signal-caller  J.J. McCarthy getting "banged up" during a rough first quarter in a loss to the Ravens.

 And Sunday's game wrapped up the weekend with the  Tennessee Titans  beating the defending Super Bowl champion  Seattle Seahawks .

 Our NFL Nation reporters picked out what you need to know about big roster decisions and more coming off Week 2 of the preseason.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full NFL schedule | Where to watch 
 Depth charts  | Sign up to play fantasy 

 

 

 Sunday's results 
 Titans 19, Seahawks  16 
 

 Should there be concern about the Titans' revamped secondary?  The secondary had a good showing against the Seahawks in joint practice, but the unit remains a concern. Starting cornerback Cor'Dale Flott was called for pass interference, which negated an interception by Kevin Winston Jr.  A bad coverage breakdown resulted in one of Seattle's two explosive touchdowns. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo got wide open when Winston and cornerback Alontae Taylor locked in on an outbreaking route by the running back. --  Turron Davenport 

 Next game:  vs. Chicago Bears (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 How bad is Bud Clark 's injury? The rookie safety was carted off with an air cast on his right leg after going down on the first defensive play. Clark, Seattle's second-round pick, had been working with the No. 2 defense, but the team's hope was that he'd begin to push Ty Okada for the starting job at some point. The Seahawks have more NFL-caliber safeties than they'd be able to keep even if everyone was healthy. If Clark is out long term,  AJ Finley 's chances of making the team increase. Rodney Thomas II , who also is fighting for a roster spot, didn't play Sunday after surgery this past week to repair a right hand fracture. -- Brady Henderson 

 Next game:  at Kansas City Chiefs (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Saturday's results 

 Cowboys 34, Cardinals 13 
 

 Cowboys: Has Joe Milton III separated himself in the No. 2 quarterback battle? Milton's command of the offense is so much greater than it was in 2025, and the results have been telling. In two games, he has completed 21 of 28 passes for 286 yards and three touchdowns. He also ran for a score. He has made the big plays -- a TD of 56 yards and a completion of 70 yards vs. the Cardinals -- but more importantly, he avoided mistakes.

 Milton's arm strength is unquestioned, but his poise and decision-making have impressed the coaches. Sam Howell has done nothing to lose the job (though that late-game pick with the Cowboys in the red zone against Arizona didn't help), but the roster gymnastics required by keeping three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster could be too costly when the Cowboys look to fill their spots at wide receiver, linebacker and cornerback. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs New Orleans Saints (Thursday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Cardinals: What does the bottom of the wide receiver room look like? There are a few guarantees to make the roster: Marvin Harrison Jr ., Michael Wilson , Kendrick Bourne and Devin Duvernay . After that, there are two questions: How many receivers will Arizona keep and who will the rest of them be?

 There are essentially three options for the last two (possibly three) spots: Simi Fehoko , Reggie Virgil and Jalen Brooks . Brooks has played great this preseason, and Wilson called Fehoko one of the best preseason receivers of all time. He plays a big role on special teams, so that will factor in. Virgil is a rookie who's quick and has shown promise. If Arizona keeps six WRs, Brooks might be the odd man out but won't last long on the practice squad, and if Virgil gets cut, Brooks could last a little longer. -- Josh Weinfuss 

 Next game: at Green Bay Packers (Friday, 8 p.m. ET)

 
 Patriots 24, Eagles 21 
 

 Patriots: Did veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor play his way onto the roster? The Patriots' top three at the position are solidified --  Christian Gonzalez , Carlton Davis III and  Marcus Jones  -- and coaches seem committed to third-year player Charles Woods as the fourth option. Vildor (seventh year) would be competing for a fifth or possibly sixth spot, and he made a case with tight coverage and two pass breakups Saturday. He also had a would-be interception nullified by an unnecessary roughness penalty on OLB Gabe Jacas . Vildor (5-11, 190) had an INT in Week 1.

 Other questions of note: Did Lan Larison 's strong performance give him the edge at RB3 and did Behren Morton 's poise in the second half force the Patriots' hand to keep him on the active roster as QB3? -- Mike Reiss 

 Next game : at Cleveland Browns (Thursday, 8 p.m. ET, Prime Video)

 

 

 Eagles : Who will back up QB Jalen Hurts this season? Andy Dalton has started both preseason games -- seemingly an indication that he is ahead in the competition with Tanner McKee  to be Hurts' backup, despite the two splitting practice reps with the second team this summer. Dalton has not fared well in those games, however, going 3-of-10 for 44 yards against the Patriots and 3-of-6 for 20 yards versus the Baltimore Ravens .

 McKee tossed two touchdown passes against New England and was more efficient overall. But neither QB has clearly separated from the other, making for an interesting decision as the time nears to trim the roster to 53. -- Tim McManus 

 Next game : at Cincinnati Bengals (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS)

 

 Bucs 16, Chiefs 15 
 

 Bucs: Has Jalon Daniels worked his way into the QB2 role behind Baker Mayfield ? Every time the undrafted free agent rookie out of Kansas has entered games, he has given the offense a jolt. He went 9-for-14 for 71 passing yards, including a 2-yard touchdown pass across his body to tight end Ko Kieft . Daniels also rushed for 23 yards and led a second scoring drive after Roman Parodie 's interception that was capped by a 1-yard Sean Tucker touchdown run. Then, Daniels went with a hard count on third-and-1 and lured the Chiefs offsides. His play on the move really stood out during a night when Jake Browning was pressured on 58% of his dropbacks and was sacked three times. -- Jenna Laine 

 Next game : at  Jacksonville Jaguars  (Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET)

 

 

 Chiefs: Who will be the right tackle for Patrick Mahomes on opening night? The team invested most of training camp in preparing Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana. Benson's performance Saturday, however, was quite disappointing. He struggled in pass protection, surrendering quick pressure to rookie Rueben Bain Jr . and a strip-sack to outside linebacker Anthony Nelson . At this point, the Chiefs likely move Benson to guard, where he played much better against the Los Angeles Rams last week. Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, hasn't been impressive, either. But Moore is likely the Chiefs' most ideal option. The only other possibility is Esa Pole , a second-year player who took snaps Saturday at left tackle with the second-team offense. -- Nate Taylor 

 Next game : at Seattle Seahawks  (Friday, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Bengals 27, Bears 9 

 

 Bears : Who will be the Bears' left tackle? The Bears are still searching for their starting left tackle and got an extended look at Braxton Jones and Theo Benedet in Cincinnati. After missing more than a week because of injury, Jones got back in the mix, and it feels like this…

title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: The most high-profile decision is whether Baltimore will place DT Nnamdi Madubuike on injured reserve.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- The Baltimore Ravens open the 2026 regular season at the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) at Lucas Oil Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Friday against the Washington Commanders  ( 6 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The most high-profile decision is whether Baltimore will place Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike on injured reserve to start the season. Coming back from neck surgery, Madubuike has yet to participate in team drills this summer, which means time is running out for him to be ready for Week 1. The Ravens also have to figure out how many players they can carry at cornerback, which is their deepest position, and at inside linebacker, which is their thinnest.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Ravens.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Lamar Jackson , Tyler Huntley 

 The Ravens re-signed Huntley this offseason to be Jackson's primary backup for a fifth season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano looks like he has earned a spot on the practice squad after two impressive outings in the preseason.

 
 

 Running backs (4) 
 Derrick Henry , Justice Hill , Rasheen Ali , Adam Randall 

 There are some question marks on the depth chart after Henry and Hill. After a solid training camp, Ali has missed a chunk of time due to an undisclosed injury, which could lead him to start the season on injured reserve. Randall, who was owner Steve Bisciotti's hand-picked selection in the fifth round this year, is on the bubble but he could land one of the last spots available with his special teams play.

 
 Wide receivers (6) 
 Zay Flowers , Rashod Bateman , Ja'Kobi Lane , Elijah Sarratt , Devontez Walker ,  LaJohntay Wester 

 Bateman could face a suspension under the personal conduct policy after being arrested on family violence charges, which would open up a roster spot. Flowers and Lane have been the Ravens' top receivers in training camp. Sarratt and Walker, a pair of fourth-round picks, are considered safe. Wester has secured the final receiver spot because he's the top punt returner and has received increased reps on offense this summer.

 
 Tight ends (4) 
 Mark Andrews , Durham Smythe , Matthew Hibner , Josh Cuevas 

 Andrews is the Ravens' only returning tight end, but Smythe is the most familiar with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system after playing for him in Chicago last season. Hibner is the favorite to become Baltimore's No. 3 tight end over Cuevas after a strong debut in the preseason opener.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Ronnie Stanley , John Simpson , Ethan Pocic , Olaivavega Ioane , Roger Rosengarten , Andrew Vorhees , Jovaughn Gwyn , Emery Jones Jr ., Carson Vinson 

 There was a shakeup on the offensive line last week, when first-team center Danny Pinter injured his right leg at a joint practice in Minnesota. Pinter is out for an extended period, which opens up the competition at center. Pocic is the favorite to take the job because of his experience, but he has to prove he is fully recovered from an Achilles injury that he suffered eight months ago. Vorhees, a former starting guard, improved his chances of making the team by taking a $2.2 million paycut.

 
 Defensive linemen (5) 
 Travis Jones , Calais Campbell , John Jenkins ,  Broderick Washington Jr ., Aeneas Peebles 

 One of the biggest questions at the start of training camp - Madubuike's status for Week 1 - still has not been answered. Along with Jones and Campbell, the other defensive lineman who is guaranteed a spot is Washington, who is guaranteed $2 million after taking a $2 million paycut. If the Ravens want to free up another roster spot, they could cut Jenkins and sign him to the practice squad, where he could be elevated for the first couple weeks of the season. Rayshaun Benny and CJ Okoye are on the bubble.

 
 Outside linebackers (5) 
 Trey Hendrickson , Tavius Robinson , Mike Green , Zion Young , Adisa Isaac 

 The Ravens have a good blend of youth and experience with their top four outside linebackers in Hendrickson, Robinson, Green and Young. Isaac, a 2024 third-round pick who has struggled with injuries, has to show he can make an impact on special teams in order to make the 53-man roster. Undrafted rookie Ethan Burke should land on the practice squad after making plays in the preseason.

 
 Inside linebackers (4) 
 Roquan Smith , Teddye Buchanan , Trenton Simpson , Jay Higgins IV 

 Buchanan was activated off the physically unable to perform list after tearing an ACL in December, but it's unknown whether he can be the top weakside linebacker at the start of the season. Given the Ravens' questionable depth at this position, it wouldn't be a surprise if Baltimore added an experienced inside linebacker after other teams make their major cuts.

 
 

 Cornerbacks (7) 
 Nate Wiggins , Marlon Humphrey , Chidobe Awuzie , T.J. Tampa , Chandler Rivers , Keyon Martin , Bilhal Kone 

 The big question here: How many cornerbacks can the Ravens keep? There are five who are locks to make the team: Wiggins, Humphrey, Awuzie, Tampa and Rivers. The Ravens likely have to make room for Martin and Kone because it's difficult to think two talented young cornerbacks will pass through waivers and land on the practice squad. This puts Robert Longerbeam , a sixth-round pick from a year ago, squarely on the bubble.

 
 Safeties (4) 
 Kyle Hamilton , Malaki Starks , Jaylinn Hawkins , Keondre Jackson 

 The Ravens essentially start three safeties in Hamilton, Starks and Hawkins. Jackson has earned a spot with splash plays on defense in the spring and summer. Baltimore can free up a roster spot by moving veteran backup K'Von Wallace to the practice squad for the first couple weeks of the season because he doesn't have to clear waivers.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Tyler Loop (K), Ryan Eckley (P), Nick Moore (LS) 

 The Ravens put a lot of faith in Loop after not bringing in competition in training camp after his 44-yard missed field goal in the season finale ended Baltimore's season. Eckley has shown a strong leg in camp after being the first punter drafted this year. The Ravens consider Moore to be the top long-snapper in the game.

title: 2026 Buffalo Bills: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: New coordinator Jim Leonhard will have some difficult decisions to make at inside linebacker and cornerback.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Houston Texans on Sept. 13 ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) at Reliant Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the Pittsburgh Steelers  ( 7 p.m. ET, NFL Network ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.
 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 While this roster largely carries over familiar faces on the offensive side of the ball, some tough decisions will have to be made on defense. This is the first year of transitioning to coordinator Jim Leonhard's new scheme, and the players who fit it best will translate to roster decisions that could look different than previous seasons. There are close calls to be made at multiple groups, including inside linebacker, outside cornerback and offensive line.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Bills.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 
 Josh Allen , Kyle Allen 

 It's the all-Allen lineup once again. The goal here for the Bills will be to bring back quarterback Shane Buechele to the practice squad.

 
 Running backs (3) 
 James Cook III , Ray Davis , Ty Johnson 

 The only question at the position is Johnson's health. He is dealing with a lower-body injury, per coach Joe Brady, and hasn't practiced since Aug. 8. Otherwise, this group is solid.

 
 Fullbacks (1) 
 Ben VanSumeren 

 The veteran became the only fullback on the roster when rookie undrafted free agent Jackson Acker was cut. There, however, is a huge question mark if the Bills will keep a fullback on the roster, especially with Brady's comments on Thursday that the team is evaluating if fullback is "a position and a role that we'll be able to have on our football team." This one is close.

 
 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 DJ Moore , Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman , Joshua Palmer , Skyler Bell , Mecole Hardman Jr . 

 To keep a punt returner or not? That's the question. The Bills showed they are wondering about it themselves by trying out Ray Davis , who is the primary kickoff returner, at punt returner to start both preseason games. Hardman has played behind other receivers, and if the Bills can go Davis at both returner spots, that opens a space elsewhere. Injuries could end up forcing the Bills to keep a six, so Hardman is on for now as he serves multiple roles, but that could easily change.

 
 Tight ends (3) 
 Dalton Kincaid , Dawson Knox , Jackson Hawes 

 This is another group that is relatively locked in. Keleki Latu has certainly stood out this camp, and if there were more roster spots, it would certainly make sense for the Bills to keep him. Otherwise, the biggest question at tight end is if Kincaid can stay healthy.

 
 Offensive linemen (9) 
 Dion Dawkins , Alec Anderson , Connor McGovern , O'Cyrus Torrence , Spencer Brown , Austin Corbett , Jude Bowry ,  Lloyd Cushenberry III , Tylan Grable 

 The Bills have shown just how they feel about Cushenberry, as he has taken over as first-team center in McGovern's absence because of a right leg injury. There is a tough decision to be made for the final spot. Sedrick Van Pran-Granger has an argument to be rostered, but the nod will go to Grable, who provides depth at tackle.

 
 Defensive linemen (11) 
 Bradley Chubb , Greg Rousseau , Michael Hoecht , TJ Parker , Javon Solomon , Ed Oliver , Deone Walker , Landon Jackson , T.J. Sanders , Zane Durant , Greg Gaines 

 This group appeared to have solidified itself when Phidarian Mathis was suspended for three games, but then the Bills signed veteran DT Greg Gaines . This week will be a crucial one for DeWayne Carter to prove a roster spot should be his. There could be a conversation about OLB Mike Danna as well, but the nod here will go to the 2024 fifth-round draft pick in Solomon.

 
 Linebackers (4) 
 Terrel Bernard , Dorian Williams , Kaleb Elarms-Orr , Keonta Jenkins 

 This position makes for one of the toughest decisions. Losing Buffalo legend Joe Andreessen is tough, and there's a good chance he ends up on the roster over Jenkins or that the Bills decide to keep five inside linebackers. This is a coin flip, but Jenkins has had played strong of late.

 
 

 Cornerbacks (6) 
 Christian Benford , Maxwell Hairston , Davison Igbinosun , Kani Walker , Dee Alford , Jordan Hancock 

 Walker is the only question mark here. If the team decides to add at outside corner, Walker would be the person to lose his spot. But as the roster currently stands, more bodies are needed at a position general manager Brandon Beane values investing in and the rookie undrafted free agent has impressed.

 
 Safeties (5) 
 Cole Bishop , C.J. Gardner-Johnson , Damar Hamlin , Jalon Kilgore ,  Sam Franklin Jr . 

 Hamlin has put together a solid camp. As he has done in years past, Hamlin's availability and reliability in the summer have shown his value. He has been a most consistent backup with Gardner-Johnson missing time. This could be a close decision with veteran Geno Stone , while the special teams capabilities of Kilgore and Franklin are important.

 
 Special teams (3) 
 Tyler Bass  (K), Tommy Doman Jr . (P), Reid Ferguson  (LS) 

 The only slight question here was punter, but it was Doman's job to lose, and he secured it over veteran Mitch Wishnowsky early on. No training camp competition was ever brought in for Bass, showing the team's confidence in the kicker.

title: 2026 Detroit Lions: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? Lions reporter Eric Woodyard makes his predictions.
full_text:
DETROIT -- The  Lions  open the 2026 NFL regular season against the  New Orleans Saints  on Sept. Sept. 13 at Ford Field. But first, they play one more preseason game (Saturday against the Indianapolis Colts ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 Despite a down season in which Detroit missed the playoffs for the first time since 2022, the Lions (9-8) still finished with a winning record for the fourth consecutive campaign in 2025. But for coach Dan Campbell and an organization with championship aspirations, that wasn't good enough.

 One of the biggest questions coming out of training camp is who will begin the season as Detroit's starting center after veteran Cade Mays suffered a wrist injury. There are also some lingering concerns within the secondary, as safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles) are unlikely to be back ahead of Week 1. However, the offense still has the potential to be one of the most explosive units in the league under first-year coordinator Drew Petzing.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Lions.

 

 

 Quarterbacks   (2) 

 Jared Goff , Joshua Dobbs 

 After veteran Teddy Bridgewater unexpectedly retired during training camp, the Lions had to pivot by signing Dobbs to play behind Goff. Undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer was having a solid camp, but the Lions will likely keep him around for the practice squad.

 

 Running backs (4) 

 Jahmyr Gibbs , Isiah Pacheco , Sione Vaki , Jacob Saylors 

 Gibbs is gearing up for a big season in which he is projected to take the bulk of the snaps as the team's unquestioned RB1, but he will have no shortage of talent around him. Former All-UFL performer Saylors has also turned heads throughout the preseason and training camp.

 

 Wide receivers (5) 

 Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams , Isaac TeSlaa , Greg Dortch , Dominic Lovett 

 Injured reserve: WR Kendrick Law 

 To no surprise, St. Brown and Williams have made big plays throughout training camp, but the veteran Dortch has been impressive on offense and special teams. Campbell has been pleased with watching him and said he has been "even better than I thought" while reuniting with new OC Petzing, after their days with the Arizona Cardinals .

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Sam LaPorta , Brock Wright , Tyler Conklin 

 Following a season-ending back injury, LaPorta has returned to full strength as he enters Year 4, which will undoubtedly boost the offense. However, Wright has also earned the trust of Petzing and could benefit from more opportunities behind LaPorta. Petzing described Wright as "arguably one of the most reliable pros in this organization just in terms of the role he has for us as an offense."

 

 Offensive linemen (9) 

 

 Penei Sewell , Blake Miller , Larry Borom , Seth McLaughlin , Tate Ratledge , Christian Mahogany , Miles Frazier , Ben Bartch , Juice Scruggs 

 Non-Football Injury list: Giovanni Manu 

 Former Panthers center Mays is expected to miss 8 eight to 10 weeks and will likely start the season on injured reserve. Mays was targeted by Detroit this offseason as an unrestricted free agent to help the unit after the Lions' offensive line struggled in 2025. Without Mays, the Lions continued to experimented with Scruggs, McLaughlin and Michael Niese at center as they search for the best fit at the position.

 

 Defensive linemen/Edge rushers   (10) 

 Alim McNeill , Tyler Lacy , Tyleik Williams , Skyler Gill-Howard , Levi Onwuzurike , Chris Smith ,  Aidan Hutchinson , Derrick Moore , DJ Wonnum , Ahmed Hassanein 

 Lacy is entering his second season with the Lions. He has emerged as a standout throughout training camp and is projected to be a starter. Campbell described Lacy and Onwuzurike as "two of our most powerful D-linemen that we have."

 "You talk about 'knock back and they are hard to move," Campbell said on Aug. 16.

 

 Linebackers   (6) 

 Jack Campbell , Malcolm Rodriguez , Derrick Barnes , Trevor Nowaske , Devin White , Damone Clark 

 Jimmy Rolder , a fourth-round selection out of Michigan, was off to a promising start throughout the offseason training program but will likely begin the season on injured reserve after suffering a leg injury early in training camp. The Lions signed free agent linebacker White to add depth after Rolder's injury and White has pushed hard for a starting spot.

 

 Cornerbacks   (8) 

 D.J. Reed , Nick Whiteside , Rock Ya-Sin , Ennis Rakestraw Jr ., Roger McCreary , Khalil Dorsey , Keith Abney II , Christian Izien 

 The Lions released Terrion Arnold , a first-round pick in 2024, after he was arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping in June. Detroit will now be counting on Reed and Ya-Sin to anchor the secondary after Arnold's release, which left the Lions thin at the cornerback spot.

 

 Safeties (3) 

 Avonte Maddox , Chuck Clark , Thomas Harper 

 Both Joseph and Brian will likely begin the 2026 season on injured reserve, while Clark and Maddox are expected to start in Week 1 after getting the bulk of the first-team reps throughout camp. The Lions won't rush back Joseph and Branch until they're fully healthy, but there is a chance that they could return for practices later in training camp or possibly early September.

 

 Special teams   (3) 

 Jake Bates  (K), Jack Fox  (P), Hogan Hatten  (LS) 

 This trio has become a mainstay in Detroit for three straight seasons. No one should be surprised by this unit. Fox received First-Team AP All-Pro honors in 2024.

title: Green Bay Packers: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: Will the Packers trade or release CB Keisean Nixon? Will rookie kicker Trey Smack make the cut?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The Packers open the 2026 NFL regular season at the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 13 at U.S. Bank Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday against the Arizona Cardinals ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 The Packers have been the NFL's youngest team for three years running, but they might finally shed that label. They've added veterans in defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (33), linebacker Zaire Franklin (30) and quarterback Tyrod Taylor (37) among others. But this is still a draft-and-develop organization, and there will be plenty of young players on the roster.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Packers.

 

 Quarterbacks (2) 

 Jordan Love , Tyrod Taylor 

 The Packers had one of the league's best backups the past two seasons in Malik Willis , who is now in Miami. Now they'll have one of the most experienced in Taylor, who is entering his 16th season. Look for them to try to keep Kyle McCord on the practice squad as a developmental backup.

 

 Running backs (3) 

 Josh Jacobs , MarShawn Lloyd , Chris Brooks 

 The Packers might be holding their breath that Jacobs doesn't get suspended because of his arrest earlier this year and that Lloyd can stay healthy after playing one game in his first two NFL seasons. If not, then they'll need help here.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 

 Christian Watson , Jayden Reed , Matthew Golden , Skyy Moore , Savion Williams , Bo Melton 

 The Packers are deep at this spot even after losing Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks  during the offseason. Isaiah Neyor and J. Michael Sturdivant had strong camps and would be under consideration if they keep a seventh guy here.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 Tucker Kraft , Josh Whyle , Drake Dabney (or a player or two to be named later) 

 Kraft looks like he's healthy enough to be ready for Week 1 after last year's torn ACL, but there's not a lot of proven production behind him. Luke Musgrave will likely stay on the physically unable to perform list because of a neck injury. This is the No. 1 spot for general manager Brian Gutekunst to upgrade via trade or waivers. Gutekunst kept four tight ends on his initial 53 last year.

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 

 Jordan Morgan , Aaron Banks , Sean Rhyan , Jacob Monk , Zach Bako-Bewele , Anthony Belton , Jager Burton , John Williams , Darian Kinnard , Donovan Jennings 

 Gutekunst kept only nine here after the initial cuts last season, but perhaps all the injuries up front in 2025 will convince him to keep an extra lineman.

 

 Defensive tackles (6) 

 Javon Hargrave , Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks , Warren Brinson , Chris McClellan , Jonathan Ford 

 New defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon wants bigger bodies up front, and this group should give him that. Ford appears to have moved ahead of Nazir Stackhouse , who made last year's roster as an undrafted rookie.

 

 Edge rushers (5) 

 Lukas Van Ness , Barryn Sorrell , Brenton Cox Jr ., Dani Dennis-Sutton , Collin Oliver 

 There's pressure on this group to generate pass rush until the return of Micah Parsons , who will start the season on PUP while recovering from the torn ACL suffered last season.

 

 Linebackers (5) 

 Zaire Franklin , Edgerrin Cooper , Isaiah McDuffie , Ty'Ron Hopper , Nick Niemann 

 The switch to having only two off-ball linebackers in Gannon's scheme means McDuffie likely loses snaps, but the Packers feel great about the duo of Franklin and Cooper. It's either Niemann or Kristian Welch for special teams purposes.

 

 

 Cornerbacks (6) 

 Keisean Nixon , Brandon Cisse , Benjamin St-Juste , Carrington Valentine , Kamal Hadden , Domani Jackson 

 If there is going to be a high-profile move on cutdown day, it would be Nixon . Perhaps the Packers will try to trade him or release him. They have another corner, Jaylin Simpson , whom they like.

 

 Safeties (4) 

 Xavier McKinney , Evan Williams , Javon Bullard , Kitan Oladapo 

 The Packers are light here since they usually keep five. If that's the case, Mark Perry is the best option.

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Trey Smack  (K), Daniel Whelan  (P), Matt Orzech  (LS) 

 Barring a collapse, it appears the they are going with a rookie kicker .

title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams: Projecting final 53-man roster

full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams open the 2026 NFL regular season against the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10 at Melbourne Cricket Ground. But first, they play one more preseason game Thursday against the  Los Angeles Chargers  and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season?

 This roster projection doesn't include Aaron Donald , who is currently going through a "regimented" process to determine whether he wants to come out of retirement. This is an offensive-heavy projection, in part because it includes six receivers, five tight ends and 10 offensive linemen.

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Rams.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 
 Matthew Stafford ,  Stetson Bennett IV , Ty Simpson 

 After the Rams drafted Simpson with the No. 13 pick in April, coach Sean McVay said the rookie and Bennett would compete to back up Stafford. After two preseason games, McVay has not announced who has won that job. This projection includes all three quarterbacks, as Bennett has taken the majority of the second-team reps during training camp.

 

 Running backs (4) 
 Kyren Williams , Blake Corum , Ronnie Rivers , Jarquez Hunter 

 Williams and Corum had about a 65-35 percent split in carries last season, with Williams rushing for 1,252 yards and 10 touchdowns on 259 carries. That could look closer to a 50-50 split this season if both running backs can stay healthy.

 

 Wide receivers (6) 
 Davante Adams , Puka Nacua , Jordan Whittington , Konata Mumpfield , Xavier Smith , CJ Daniels 

 Last season, Adams led the league in touchdown receptions (14) and Nacua led the NFL with 129 catches. Whittington and Mumpfield are likely competing for the No. 3 receiver spot behind that pair.

 

 Tight ends (5) 
 Tyler Higbee , Terrance Ferguson , Colby Parkinson , Davis Allen , Max Klare 

 Five tight ends on a 53-man roster would be unheard of for most teams -- and the Rams before last season -- but it seems the most likely scenario going into training camp. Los Angeles had 331 plays in 13 personnel last season , more than twice as many as any other team, according to ESPN Research.

 

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 
 Alaric Jackson , Steve Avila , Coleman Shelton , Kevin Dotson , Warren McClendon Jr ., David Quessenberry , Beaux Limmer , Keagen Trost , Dylan McMahon , Justin Dedich 

 The Rams have several uncertain spots on the offensive line given Jackson's legal situation and possible suspension. Trost, a rookie third-round pick, injured his hamstring in the Rams' preseason opener and could miss several weeks. Dedich missed all of training camp on the NFI list after injuring his hand in early July.

 

 Defensive linemen (5) 
 Kobie Turner , Poona Ford , Braden Fiske , Tyler Davis , Tim Keenan III 

 If Donald decides to return, that would shake up this group. Donald, a future Hall of Fame defensive tackle, retired in March 2024. Turner, a third-round pick in 2023, is going into the final season of his rookie contract and is a candidate for a contract extension.

 

 Linebackers (8) 
 Myles Garrett , Byron Young , Josaiah Stewart , Desjuan Johnson , Nate Landman , Omar Speights , Shaun Dolac , Grant Stuard 

 The biggest offseason addition for the Rams came on June 1, when they traded for Garrett , the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Young, who is coming off a 12-sack season for Los Angeles, is also entering the final season of his rookie deal.

 

 Cornerbacks (5) 
 Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson , Josh Wallace , Emmanuel Forbes Jr ., Cam Lampkin 

 The Rams revamped this room after last season , trading for McDuffie and signing Watson to a three-year, $51 million deal. Lampkin, who has spent most of the past two seasons on the Rams' practice squad, impressed during training camp.

 

 Safeties (4) 
 Quentin Lake , Kam Curl , Kamren Kinchens , Jaylen McCollough 

 The Rams have continuity in their safety room after signing Lake to a contract extension during the 2025 season and re-signing Curl before the start of free agency. Kinchens, a third-round pick in 2024, could be a breakout candidate for the group.

 

 Special teams (3) 
 Harrison Mevis  (K),  Ethan Evans  (P), Joe Cardona  (LS) 

 Special teams was a weakness for the Rams last season, forcing an in-season change at kicker and long-snapper. Mevis, who took over in mid-November, missed just one kick in nine regular-season games and was perfect during the playoffs.

title: Minnesota Vikings: Projecting final 53-man roster
summary: At least four rookies are poised to contribute out of the gate on both sides of the ball. Who are they?
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings open the 2026 NFL regular season against the Green Bay Packers on Sept. 13 at U.S. Bank Stadium. But first, they play one more preseason game (Friday at the Denver Broncos ) and then must cut their roster to 53 players by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. 

 Who will make the team? Which positions have tough decisions on deck? And where might the lineup be deepest and thinnest this season? 

 While most eyes were on the Vikings' quarterback competition, won to no surprise by veteran Kyler Murray , competition was playing out across the roster. What emerged, most notably, is the potential for immediate offensive or defensive contributions from at least four and possibly five members of the 2026 draft class. 

 Here is our projection for the 53-man roster for the Vikings.

 

 Quarterbacks (3) 

 Kyler Murray , J.J. McCarthy , Carson Wentz 

 It's possible the Vikings will look to put No. 4 quarterback Max Brosmer on the practice squad. Otherwise, the only question was deciding whether McCarthy or Wentz will be No. 2 on gamedays behind Murray. It appears that McCarthy will open the season there, with Wentz as the emergency No. 3, but that is always subject to change.

 

 Running backs (5) 

 Aaron Jones Sr ., Jordan Mason , Demond Claiborne , Zavier Scott , Max Bredeson (FB)  

 Two veterans in the final year of their contracts (Jones, Mason) and two members of the 2026 draft class (Claiborne, Bredeson) make up the crux of this position. Jones and Mason will be the primary ball carriers, but Claiborne has a burst that neither of them possess. Based on usage in training camp and the preseason, Bredeson figures to play a prominent blocking role. 

 

 Wide receivers (5) 

 Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison , Jauan Jennings , Tai Felton , Myles Price 

 Jefferson, Addison and Jennings will comprise the Vikings' three-receiver sets, which Jennings has compared to the  Golden State Warriors ' championship trio of Kevin Durant , Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson . Felton and Price were both impressive during training camp but will play limited roles unless there are injuries.

 

 Tight ends (3) 

 T.J. Hockenson , Josh Oliver , Gavin Bartholomew 

 Could this position get a makeover next spring under new general manager Nolan Teasley? Hockenson's contract expires after the season. Oliver has been an elite blocker over the past three seasons but has been used minimally in the passing game, catching 59 passes while earning $22 million. Bartholomew emerged as a smooth pass-catcher after missing his rookie season because of a back injury.

 

 Offensive linemen (10) 

 Christian Darrisaw , Donovan Jackson , Blake Brandel , Will Fries , Brian O'Neill , Ryan Van Demark , Michael Jurgens , Joe Huber , Caleb Tiernan , Walter Rouse 

 Four starters return from 2025, while Brandel completes the transition from guard/tackle to center following the retirement of Ryan Kelly . The Vikings hope they have upgraded their depth at all positions, particularly after prying Van Demark away from the Buffalo Bills via restricted free agency.

 

 

 Defensive linemen (6) 

 Jalen Redmond , Levi Drake Rodriguez , Caleb Banks , Domonique Orange , Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins ,  Elijah Williams 

 The Vikings have infused this position with young talent, and they should have five players in their rotation with no more than three years of experience. That includes two rookies in Banks and Orange, both of whom received first-team work during training camp as defensive coordinator Brian Flores tested various packages.

 

 Linebackers (8) 

 Andrew Van Ginkel , Dallas Turner , Eric Wilson , Blake Cashman , Jake Golday , Ivan Pace Jr ., Bo Richter , Tyler Batty 

 Camp did not reveal obvious depth at edge pass rusher, where Turner has taken over the spot vacated by the trade of Jonathan Greenard to the Philadelphia Eagles . But Ingram-Dawkins has shown some position flexibility, and Golday got work at the off-ball position and edge. 

 

 Cornerbacks (4) 

 Byron Murphy Jr ., Isaiah Rodgers , James Pierre , Charles Demmings 

 It's possible the Vikings will add to this position during the flurry of cuts, but for now they were encouraged to see Demmings -- a fifth-round draft pick from FCS Stephen F. Austin -- challenge some of their top receivers and push Pierre for the No. 3 cornerback job. In some cases, however, Flores will use a safety as his nickel.

 

 Safeties (6) 
 Joshua Metellus , Jay Ward , Theo Jackson , Jakobe Thomas , Tavierre Thomas , Jacob Thomas 

 The Vikings didn't backfill Harrison Smith 's starting role as if they were certain he would retire. (He hasn't made any announcements one way or the other.) Following Jamal Adams ' season-ending torn right quadriceps in the first preseason game, two rookies with nearly identical names -- Jakobe Thomas was a third-rounder, Jacob Thomas was an undrafted free agent -- are on track to make the roster. 

 

 Special teams (3) 

 Will Reichard  (K), Johnny Hekker  (P), Andrew DePaola  (LS) 

 Rookie punter Brett Thorson has had a strong camp, but Hekker is the more reliable option for a veteran team hoping to make a playoff push.

title: Patriots' Will Campbell leaning into advice from top linemen
summary: After an up and down rookie season, Campbell focused this offseason on regaining strength lost due to 2025 injury. And he's leaning on his peers for advice.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Campbell's truth: To prepare for his second NFL season, Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell leaned into the advice of veteran Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson .

 "Lane told me, 'You have to be very honest with yourself about the season,'" Campbell told ESPN.

 "I felt like before I got hurt [Nov. 23], I was playing some solid ball. And after that, I didn't play the way I needed to play. So just learning from it, fixing it. After the season, I was just worried about getting healthy, building my strength back to where I knew it needed to be and coming into [spring practices] ready to go, trying to do everything I can to put myself in the best position possible to help the team."

 Since the Patriots' loss to the  Seattle Seahawks  in Super Bowl LX , and perhaps even before that, there hasn't been a more scrutinized New England player than Campbell, the No. 4 pick in the 2025 draft.

 Some wondered if the Patriots would consider moving him to guard, especially after selecting Utah offensive tackle Caleb Lomu in the first round (No. 28 selection). But Campbell has remained a fixture as quarterback Drake Maye 's blindside protector through 20 training camp practices as he's fully recovered from tearing a ligament in his right knee in late November.

 

 A key part of his preparation for the 2026 season was spending a week with Johnson, Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive tackle Tristan Wirfs , Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Dion Dawkins and Kansas City Chiefs center Creed Humphrey . They were joined by a former Navy SEAL, a former champion in the "World's Strongest Man" competition and celebrity chef Robert Irvine (a close confidant of Johnson).

 In 2025, Dawkins (95.9%) and Wirfs (95.5%) were the top- and third-ranked tackles, respectively, in pass block win rate. Humphrey led all centers in the metric (98.5%).

 "[Lane] reached out to me about coming out there; I was super grateful to be able to be around him, Tristan and Dion -- those guys were all super nice to me and welcoming," Campbell said.

 "They've played a lot of football at a high level. Lane and Tristan have both won Super Bowls, so they have everything a young, aspiring tackle in this league wants by the time they're that age. It was not only being able to hang out, but seeing how they work, and just to get in there and compete and soak up anything I can from them."

 The 36-year-old Johnson has taken the 22-year-old Campbell under his wing. Campbell also attended Johnson's "OL Masterminds Summit" in the offseason, while working out in Dallas.

 "Will kind of reminds me of myself in a way -- country kid, drafted first round, so I know the kind of pressures that are on guys like that. I thought he had a really good rookie season," Johnson said following Patriots-Eagles practices. "You can see him getting better. I was watching him [Wednesday]; he looks thicker and bigger. He's healed up from his knee injury."

 For Campbell, it all comes back to Johnson's advice to honestly assess his body of work.

 "In this game, if you're not honest with yourself, you won't make it long. Because there's always room for corrections, no matter who you are. There's always room to get better and grow," Campbell said. "So I don't think it's very hard to be honest at all."

 

 2. Maye's preseason: Will Maye play in the preseason finale Thursday in Cleveland?

 That's one hot-button question after the quarterback didn't play in each of the Patriots' first two preseason games. Coach Mike Vrabel said practices with the  Indianapolis Colts  and Eagles gave Maye ideal work while also creating situations that couldn't be guaranteed in a preseason game.

 At the same time, the idea that Maye could benefit from feeling game speed -- when defensive players can finish the play with a tackle unlike practice -- has merit with the regular-season opener at Seattle fast approaching on Sept. 9.

 "I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available," Vrabel said late Saturday when asked about Maye & Co. playing in the preseason.

 "And if that means playing Thursday as part of preparation, then that is what we will do. I have not made that decision yet, but I would say that that is something that I am confident in with where we are set up currently."

 3. Gonzo update : In a halftime interview during the Patriots' preseason game against the Eagles, Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf was asked where things stand with cornerback Christian Gonzalez on a potential contract extension. Gonzalez hasn't practiced since Aug. 10 when he landed hard in the end zone.

 "Each side is trying to do what's right for them," Wolf told Devin and Jason McCourty . "Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed. We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done."

 4. OL injuries mount: The preseason hasn't been kind to the Patriots' offensive line depth.

 In Saturday night's game against the Eagles, third- or fourth-string offensive tackle Marcus Bryant sustained a left ankle injury in the first quarter and was quickly ruled out, highlighting the importance of Lomu's development (the rookie struggled on a couple stunts in the game). This came a week after top backup center/guards Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich were knocked out of the opener with injuries that are expected to sideline them for multiple weeks.

 

 5. Kendall's take : Longtime former NFL offensive lineman Pete Kendall (1996 to 2008) of Boston College watched Patriots-Eagles practices last week since his son, Drew, is a backup in Philadelphia.

 "My biggest takeaway is that both fanbases have good reason to be excited for the season," he said. "The other takeaway is how productive those two days were. Very professional. Very little of the extracurriculars, and it looked like both sides got a lot of good work in. And another good thing is we didn't see a cart come out as it didn't look like there were any significant injuries. I think both teams will be happy."

 6. McDaniels' insight: Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels hit on two timely topics in his interview on sports radio WEEI on Friday.

 
 Kayshon Boutte 's potential contributions: "It's a really, really good [receiver] room. We have a lot of guys that have a lot of different sets of skills, and KB has certainly done a great job for us ... the reality is they all have different roles. ... There's so many variables that go into what somebody may end up doing during the course of the season or a month, or what have you. It's hard to predict all that. But I know Kayshon has had a great approach, has made a bunch of plays ... and continues to show up and do his job. Love KB and love that group." 
 Impressions on A.J. Brown : "He's really a smart player. I had an interaction with him before he was drafted and had a brief chance to get to know him when he came in on a '30' visit for us [in New England in 2019] but just seeing the wealth of knowledge that he has now. The wisdom he gives to some of the other guys in the room, the way he sees the game -- very similarly through the quarterback's eyes -- it's really cool to see how that can impact your room. ... He's been awesome. Love every day working with him. Really enjoy his personality -- he's a mature guy that wants to do the right thing, help the team get better, help his teammates and perform and do his job. Couldn't ask for anything more from A.J. than that."

title: Seahawks' Devon Witherspoon got paid. Will his role change?
summary: The NFL's highest-paid cornerback blitzed with success for Seattle in the Super Bowl. Could we see more of that from Witherspoon this season?
full_text:
RENTON, Wash. -- As the confetti had just finished falling on the Seattle Seahawks minutes after their victory in Super Bowl LX , NFL Films captured coach Mike Macdonald and cornerback  Devon Witherspoon in a moment of elation.

 In between bear hugs, Witherspoon called it "bulls---" that Macdonald had been snubbed for AP NFL Coach of the Year. Macdonald asked Witherspoon how many sacks he had that night against the New England Patriots , to which the star corner -- ever the unselfish team player -- responded that it didn't matter.

 "I'm gonna ride with you always," Witherspoon said.

 The two will be riding together for the foreseeable future now that Seattle has extended Witherspoon for four years and $132 million . He's under contract for the next six seasons at a total cost of around $158.3 million, with the new-money average of $33 million resetting the market at his position.

 Witherspoon got paid. Will he now get unleashed in the defense? That is, will Macdonald turn him loose as a blitzer and send him after opposing quarterbacks like he did against Drake Maye and the Patriots in the Super Bowl?

 It's a question worth asking given how much Witherspoon has impacted the game in that regard and how that skill set put him in position for his massive new deal. He is not the NFL's highest-paid cornerback because he possesses Derek Stingley Jr .'s elite ball skills or the super sticky coverage of Pat Surtain II or Christian Gonzalez . Witherspoon is one of the best players at his position for other reasons, like his instincts and anticipation, a relentless motor, a violent style that belies his 185-pound frame -- and when Macdonald moves him into the slot, his ability to get home as a blitzer.

 "He plays in the trenches like he's a big guy," defensive lineman Leonard Williams said last season, "and I love to see that."

 

 Macdonald said it was a testament to Witherspoon's love of football and commitment to his teammates that he practiced throughout the spring and summer despite his unsettled contract situation.

 Though the deal took much longer than expected, no one batted an eye at the dollar amounts. Witherspoon, who has made the Pro Bowl in each of his first three seasons and was a second-team All-Pro in 2025, was always expected to set a new financial benchmark for cornerbacks even without the coverage metrics or the ball production of some of his peers.

 Witherspoon has two career interceptions. (One was a pick-six.) But according to ESPN Research, his 36 passes defended are tied for 10th among cornerbacks with at least 1,000 defensive plays in coverage since 2023 (including playoffs). That total doesn't count the two Matthew Stafford passes he broke up in the end zone on consecutive plays late in the fourth quarter of last season's NFC Championship Game , with Seattle clinging to a four-point lead over the Los Angeles Rams .

 "It doesn't matter the situation; he's playing it at top speed, top intent," Macdonald said. "That's how we want our football team to operate. There are plays earlier in the [championship game] that Spoon probably could have played better, but the mentality to just attack the next play all the time is probably what makes it so special. Then in both those [pass breakups], they were both extended plays where I think we were in man coverage on both of them. To be able to guard your man for that amount of time relentlessly, it's legendary type stuff."

 Two weeks later, Witherspoon's blitzing helped swing the Super Bowl in Seattle's favor.

 Macdonald sent him after Maye six times. The result: three pressures, one sack and another hit that set up Uchenna Nwosu 's interception return for a touchdown in the fourth quarter -- the nail in the coffin of Seattle's 29-13 win. Had it not been for running back  Kenneth Walker III  and his 161 scrimmage yards, Witherspoon could have easily been voted the game's MVP.

 Witherspoon's six pass-rush snaps that night were tied for the most of any game in his career and a big jump from the 1.5 he averaged during the regular season (which led to a half-sack). His average was 1.9 pass-rush snaps in 2023 and 2.4 in 2024 (4.0 sacks over those two seasons).

 

 The drop-off was tied to where he lined up. After drafting Witherspoon No. 5 in 2023, former coach Pete Carroll and his staff played him outside in base situations and moved him inside in nickel packages, which put him closer to the action as a run defender and blitzer. Macdonald used Witherspoon similarly when he arrived in 2024. In each season, he played the CB slightly more in the slot than on the perimeter. But with Nick Emmanwori emerging as a force at nickelback, Witherspoon played almost twice as many snaps outside than in the slot.

 That meant fewer blitzing opportunities -- until Super Bowl LX.

 Macdonald answered in the affirmative when asked if he's inclined to blitz Witherspoon more going forward after seeing the way it impacted that game.

 "Yes," Macdonald said. "He's a great corner. He's a great nickel. When Nick is available, Nick is also a great nickel. It's a great problem to have as a coach. How do you deploy your people to have success? All those instincts about timing and even beating guards, setting them up and beating backs in one-on-one pass-rush situations, it's not common for that skill set."

 How does Witherspoon feel about the possibility of blitzing more?

 "Whatever he want me to do, I'm going to be able to do it," he said. "So just let me know, Coach."

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the 49ers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 49ers activate Kittle from PUP list; McCaffrey returns to practice 
 Shanahan dismisses idea RB McCaffrey sitting out for new deal 
 Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling? 
 49ers' Ricky Pearsall has knee surgery, targets 9-month recovery 
 How the 49ers' defense looks different under Raheem Morris 
 Kyle Shanahan nears full strength, plans to coach preseason opener 
 Kittle eyes opener in Australia 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 23 
 The 49ers welcomed tight end George Kittle (Achilles) and running back Christian McCaffrey (tightness) back to practice on Sunday. First, the team activated Kittle from the physically unable to perform list, clearing his path to practice again. About 20 minutes later, McCaffrey trotted on to the field in pads for his first session in a couple of weeks.

 The Niners eased both back in, with Kittle only doing individual drills and McCaffrey taking about seven reps in team drills, including a handful of carries. Regardless, it was a positive step for both in the mission to have them ready for Week 1.

 "It definitely just gives us energy," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said. "It just changes things. You have two Hall of Fame caliber players out there who are back out there and getting their work in and they practice at a high standard and they lift everybody up. ... It's good to see them back out there." 

 More observations :

 
 The only new name on the non-participant list was rookie DE Romello Height . He was seen Saturday moving slowly after practice, but it's unclear what he is dealing with at the moment. 
 Practice got a bit animated late in the session when QB Brock Purdy dropped a perfect pass beyond the reach of LB Fred Warner and into the hands of WR  Deebo Samuel Sr . for a big gain over the middle. Purdy apparently took issue with Warner's trash talk after an earlier pass breakup and let him know about it after the completion to Samuel. No hard feelings, though, as Warner and Purdy were seen talking and laughing a few moments later. 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling and CB Deommodore Lenoir were both back in practice after missing Saturday with a shoulder issue. Lenoir (blue) and Stribling (black) were in no-contact jerseys. 
 CB Upton Stout had an interception against Purdy on what seemed to be a miscommunication with Stribling. The pass went right to Stout, who would have had a long return on it in a real game. 
 Among the kick return combinations they worked on Sunday: RBs Kaelon Black and Jordan James . Both have fresh legs after recently returning from injury and both have stood out in recent practices. 
 Another good day in one-on-one pass rush drills for undrafted DT James Thompson Jr . Thompson might be hard to keep off the initial 53-man roster, both because of his strong camp and because of uncertainty in front of him at the position. 
 

 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 22 
 Wide receiver Mike Evans was back at practice Saturday after leaving Tuesday's session early with quad tightness. The Niners weren't concerned about it at the time and suggested Evans would be back soon, so his presence wasn't a total surprise.

 Evans went on to have a nice practice, connecting with QB Brock Purdy a few times for big gains and catching a short touchdown pass from Purdy in the red zone. RB Christian McCaffrey , meanwhile, did not return to practice from his own bout with tightness -- but he was seen in the weight room going through a workout.

 More observations: 

 
 Coach Kyle Shanahan is basically all the way back to full duties from his car accident, but he took another step Saturday when he was seen calling in plays on the walkie-talkie. It's the first time I've noticed it in this camp (doesn't mean it hasn't happened before), and he didn't do it the whole time, but it is also a sign that the regular season is fast approaching. 
 WR De'Zhaun Stribling and CB Deommodore Lenoir did not practice because of shoulder issues. They're considered day-to-day, according to the team. 
 The Niners welcomed back three potential important contributors from injury Saturday: RB Jordan James (rib), G Dominick Puni (concussion) and DT C.J. West (concussion). WR Malik Turner was also back in the mix, though he did some work on the side after individual. 
 Among the others not practicing after suffering injuries in Thursday's preseason game: LB Nick Martin (hamstring), CB Renardo Green (hamstring) and OL Austen Pleasants (knee). 
 James and rookie RB Kaelon Black have fresh legs and it shows after their returns from injury. Black, in particular, showed off some sure hands in the pass game, one of the questions surrounding him coming out of the draft. 
 Other 49ers I did not see participating today who haven't had any injuries disclosed: LB Jalen Graham , WR Wesley Grimes (was seen with a wrap on his hand), RB Zamir White and DL Xavier Thomas . 
 

 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- The 49ers' offense largely had its way with the Titans in a joint practice last week, but that was far from the case against the Chargers.

 The unit started well, as rookie running back Kaelon Black broke some big runs early. But the Chargers settled in for the second half and made life hard on QB Brock Purdy & Co. in the move-the-ball, two-minute and red zone periods.

 Chargers linebacker  Del'Shawn Phillips  even picked off a Purdy pass intended for tight end  Luke Farrell when safety  Derwin James Jr . got his hand in the way and tipped it to him.

 All in all, it wasn't the most encouraging outing against another team that should be a playoff contender this season.

 "Obviously, there was some good stuff, some stuff we need to work on, but I just feel like they came out with a little more of a chip on their shoulder," Purdy said.

 More observations: 

 
 The 49ers and Chargers were all about their business with no notable skirmishes. That's unusual for a joint practice, and it led to Shanahan delivering the funniest line of the day as he poked fun at Robert Saleh, the Titans' coach and his good friend. Asked if there was a reason for the lack of fighting, Shanahan joked, "No, [the Chargers'] head coach has more discipline than Tennessee's." 
 Black was one of three 49ers to return to practice Tuesday, joining receiver  Demarcus Robinson (who only missed Sunday) and defensive lineman  Keion White . White and Black had been dealing with adductor injuries, though White did not finish the session. 
 Defensive tackle  C.J. West did not practice because of a concussion, which makes him the fifth player in this camp to have suffered a head injury. Defensive lineman  Titus Leo also had a concussion and was waived/injured Tuesday as the team brought back defensive tackle  Evan Anderson . 
 The competition for the backup running back job behind Christian McCaffrey has been difficult to handicap because of injuries to all of the primary contenders for that job. But Black picked up where he left off before his injury. He broke a long, possible touchdown run down the left side early in the session and clearly has the freshest legs of the bunch. 
 Chargers OLB  Tuli Tuipulotu  gave the Niners fits, particularly in the run game where he had at least three run stuffs.
